articles.title: After a busy day of work and play, the body needs to rest
articles.fallbackTitle: After a busy day of work and play, the body needs to rest

blocks.text: After a busy day of work and play, the body needs to rest. Sleep is necessary for good health. During this time, the body recovers from the activities of the previous day. The rest that you get while sleeping makes it possible for your body to prepare itself for the next day.
blocks.translation: 忙碌地工作、玩耍一天之后，身体需要休息。睡眠对健康必不可少。在这段时间里，身体会从前一天的各种活动中恢复过来。睡眠中得到的休息，让身体能够为第二天做好准备。

blocks.text: There are four levels of sleep, each being a little deeper than the one before. As you sleep, your body relaxes little by little. Your heart beats more slowly, and your brain slows down. After you reach the fourth level, your body shifts back and forth from one level of sleep to the other. Although your mind slows down, from time to time you will dream.
blocks.translation: 睡眠有四个层次，每一层都比上一层更深。入睡时，身体一点一点放松，心跳变慢，大脑也慢下来。到达第四层之后，身体会在不同睡眠层次之间来回转换。虽然思维变慢，但你仍会不时做梦。

blocks.text: Scientists who study sleep point out that when dreaming occurs, your eyeballs begin to move more quickly (although your eyelids are closed). This stage of sleep is called REM, which stands for rapid eye movement. If you have trouble falling asleep, some people recommend breathing very slowly and very deeply. Other people believe that drinking warm milk will help make you drowsy. There is also an old suggestion that counting sheep will put you to sleep.
blocks.translation: 研究睡眠的科学家指出，做梦时你的眼球会开始快速转动（尽管眼皮是闭着的）。这一睡眠阶段叫作 REM，即快速眼动。如果你难以入睡，有人建议缓慢而深长地呼吸；也有人相信喝热牛奶能让你犯困。还有一个古老的说法：数羊能让你睡着。

paragraphs: After a busy day of work and play, the body needs to rest. Sleep is necessary for good health. During this time, the body recovers from the activities of the previous day. The rest that you get while sleeping makes it possible for your body to prepare itself for the next day.

There are four levels of sleep, each being a little deeper than the one before. As you sleep, your body relaxes little by little. Your heart beats more slowly, and your brain slows down. After you reach the fourth level, your body shifts back and forth from one level of sleep to the other. Although your mind slows down, from time to time you will dream.

Scientists who study sleep point out that when dreaming occurs, your eyeballs begin to move more quickly (although your eyelids are closed). This stage of sleep is called REM, which stands for rapid eye movement. If you have trouble falling asleep, some people recommend breathing very slowly and very deeply. Other people believe that drinking warm milk will help make you drowsy. There is also an old suggestion that counting sheep will put you to sleep.

articles.title: Doctors have known for a long time that extremely loud noises can cause hearing damage or
articles.fallbackTitle: Doctors have known for a long time that extremely loud noises can cause hearing damage or

blocks.text: Doctors have known for a long time that extremely loud noises can cause hearing damage or loss. The noise can be the sound of a jet airplane or machines in factories or loud music or other common sounds found at home or at work. A person only needs to hear the noise for a little more than one second to be affected.
blocks.translation: 医生们早就知道，极响的噪音会造成听力损伤或丧失。这种噪音可能是喷气式飞机、工厂机器、大声的音乐，也可能是家中或工作中的其他常见声音。人只要听到这种噪音超过一秒，就可能受到影响。

blocks.text: An American scientist has found that using aspirin can increase the temporary hearing loss or damage from loud noise. He did an experiment, using a number of male students at a university who all had normal hearing. He gave them different amounts of aspirin for different periods of time, and then he tested their hearing ability. He found that the students who were given four grams of aspirin a day for two days suffered much greater temporary hearing loss than those who did not use aspirin. The hearing loss was about two times as great.
blocks.translation: 一位美国科学家发现，服用阿司匹林会加重噪音造成的暂时性听力损伤。他用一些听力正常的男大学生做实验，让他们在不同时间段服用不同剂量的阿司匹林，然后测试他们的听力。他发现，连续两天每天服用四克阿司匹林的学生，其暂时性听力损失比不服用阿司匹林的学生严重得多，约为后者的两倍。

blocks.text: The scientist said millions of people in the United States use much larger amounts of aspirin than were used in the study. He said these people face a serious danger of suffering hearing loss from loud noise.
blocks.translation: 这位科学家说，美国有数百万人服用的阿司匹林剂量远高于研究中的用量。他说，这些人面临因噪音而听力受损的严重危险。

paragraphs: Doctors have known for a long time that extremely loud noises can cause hearing damage or loss. The noise can be the sound of a jet airplane or machines in factories or loud music or other common sounds found at home or at work. A person only needs to hear the noise for a little more than one second to be affected.

An American scientist has found that using aspirin can increase the temporary hearing loss or damage from loud noise. He did an experiment, using a number of male students at a university who all had normal hearing. He gave them different amounts of aspirin for different periods of time, and then he tested their hearing ability. He found that the students who were given four grams of aspirin a day for two days suffered much greater temporary hearing loss than those who did not use aspirin. The hearing loss was about two times as great.

The scientist said millions of people in the United States use much larger amounts of aspirin than were used in the study. He said these people face a serious danger of suffering hearing loss from loud noise.

articles.title: If someone is sleepwalking, they are walking around while they are asleep
articles.fallbackTitle: If someone is sleepwalking, they are walking around while they are asleep

blocks.text: If someone is sleepwalking, they are walking around while they are asleep. Sleepwalking happens when a person is not fully asleep but not quite awake. Usually we move from our deepest levels of sleep to a lighter level and stay there. Sleepwalkers come right up to wake levels but do not fully awaken. It is at this time that they get up and walk.
blocks.translation: 梦游的人会在睡着时四处走动。梦游发生在一个既没有完全睡着、也没有完全清醒的状态。通常我们会从最深睡眠阶段转到较浅阶段并停留在那里。梦游者会接近清醒状态，却没有完全醒来，正是在这时他们起身走动。

blocks.text: The longer a person stays in deep sleep, the more time there is for the sleep to be broken. That opens up the possibility of being awakened (but not fully) and of sleepwalking.
blocks.translation: 一个人在深睡中停留的时间越长，睡眠被打断的机会就越多，也就越可能出现“被唤醒（但没有完全清醒）”以及梦游。

blocks.text: Sleepwalking happens more often among young people than grown-ups because young people usually have more deep sleep. Up to 7% of 5- to 12-year-olds sleepwalk, while only about 2% of grown-ups sleepwalk. We get less deep sleep as we are getting older and the possibility of sleepwalking is also reduced.
blocks.translation: 梦游在年轻人中比成年人更常见，因为年轻人通常深睡更多。5 至 12 岁儿童中多达 7% 会梦游，而成年人只有约 2%。随着年龄增长，我们的深睡减少，梦游的可能性也随之降低。

blocks.text: Sleepwalking may run in families, too. If one of your parents was a sleepwalker, you have about a 50 % possibility of also being a sleepwalker.
blocks.translation: 梦游也可能与家族遗传有关。如果父母一方曾梦游，你梦游的可能性约为 50%。

Up to 7% of 5- to 12-year-olds sleepwalk, while only about 2% of grown-ups sleepwalk. We get less deep sleep as we are getting older and the possibility of sleepwalking is also reduced.

articles.title: Our eating habits are very important for good health and a strong body
articles.fallbackTitle: Our eating habits are very important for good health and a strong body

blocks.text: Our eating habits are very important for good health and a strong body. There are times when most of us would rather eat sweets and ice cream than meat and rice. Sweets and ice cream are not bad for the stomach if we eat them at the end of a meal. If we eat them before a meal, they may take away our appetite. It is important for us to eat our meal at the same time each day. When we feel hungry, it is a sign that our bodies need food. When we feel angry or excited, we may not want to eat. When we are worried, we may not want to eat, either.
blocks.translation: 我们的饮食习惯对健康和强壮的身体非常重要。有时我们大多数人宁愿吃甜食和冰淇淋，也不愿吃肉和米饭。如果在饭后吃，甜食和冰淇淋对胃并无害处；但如果在饭前吃，它们可能会让我们失去食欲。每天在固定时间吃饭很重要。感到饥饿，是身体需要食物的信号。生气或兴奋时，我们可能不想吃东西；担忧时，也可能不想吃。

blocks.text: A long time ago, in England, some judges used to decide whether a man was telling the truth by giving him some dry bread.If the man could not swallow the bread, it was a sign that he was not telling the truth. He was telling a lie.Although this seems very strange and rather foolish, it is indeed an excellent way of finding out the truth.A man who is worrying about something has difficulty in swallowing anything dry.Because when he is worrying, he loses his appetite and does not want to eat.
blocks.translation: 很久以前在英国，一些法官会让嫌疑人吃干面包，以此判断他是否说真话。如果那人咽不下面包，就被认为没有说真话，是在撒谎。这听起来很奇怪甚至愚蠢，却确实是查明真相的好办法。一个心里担忧的人很难咽下干的东西，因为担忧时他会失去食欲，不想吃东西。

blocks.text: With obesity now affecting 29% of the population in England, and expected to rise to 35% by 2030, should we now recognize it as a disease? Obesity, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that health may be adversely affected, meets the dictionary definition of disease, argues Professor John Wilding. He points out that more than 200 genes influence weight. “Thus body weight is strongly influenced by biology—it is not an individual’s fault if they develop obesity.” Yet the widespread view is that obesity is self-induced and that it is entirely the individual’s responsibility to do something about it. blocks.text: Doctors believe that second-hand smoke may cause lung cancer in people who do not smoke. Nonsmokers often breathe in the smoke from other people’s cigarettes. This is second-hand smoke. The US Environmental Protection Agency (美国环保局) reports that about fifty-three thousand people die in the United States each year as a result of exposure to second-hand smoke.
blocks.translation: 医生认为，二手烟可能导致不吸烟的人患肺癌。不吸烟的人常常吸入别人香烟的烟雾，这就是二手烟。美国环保局报告称，美国每年约有五万三千人因接触二手烟而死亡。

blocks.text: It is harder for children to avoid second-hand smoke. In the United States, nine million children under the age of five live in homes with at least one smoker. Research shows that these children are sick more often than children who live in homes where no one smokes. The damaging effects of second-hand smoke on children also continue as they grow up. The children of smokers are more than twice as likely to develop lung cancer when they are adults as children of nonsmokers. The risk is even higher for children who live in homes where both parents smoke.
blocks.translation: 儿童更难避免二手烟。在美国，有九百万五岁以下儿童生活在至少有一名吸烟者的家庭中。研究表明，这些孩子比家中无人吸烟的孩子更常生病。二手烟对儿童的危害还会随着他们长大而持续。吸烟者的孩子成年后患肺癌的可能性是不吸烟者孩子的两倍多。如果父母双方都吸烟，孩子的风险更高。

blocks.text: People are becoming very aware of the danger of second-hand smoke. As a result, they have passed laws that prohibit people from smoking in many public places. Currently, 45 states in the US have laws that restrict smoking. The most well-known law doesn’t allow people to smoke on short native airline flights, i.e. flights within the country.
blocks.translation: 人们正越来越意识到二手烟的危险。因此，他们通过了法律，禁止人们在许多公共场所吸烟。目前美国有 45 个州制定了限制吸烟的法律。最著名的法律不允许人们在短途国内航班上吸烟，即在美国境内飞行的航班。

blocks.text: A warm drink of milk before bed has long been the best choice for those wanting a good night’s sleep. But now a study has found it really does help people nod off—if it is milked from a cow at night.
blocks.translation: 睡前喝一杯温牛奶，长期以来一直是想睡个好觉的人的最佳选择。但如今一项研究发现，它确实能帮助人入睡——前提是这牛奶来自夜里挤奶的奶牛。

blocks.text: Researchers have discovered that “night milk” contains more melatonin (褪黑激素), which has been proven to help people feel sleepy and reduce anxiety.
blocks.translation: 研究人员发现，“夜间牛奶”含有更多褪黑激素，而褪黑激素已被证明有助于让人产生睡意并减轻焦虑。

blocks.text: The study, by researchers from Seoul, South Korea, involved mice being fed with dried milk powder made from cows milked both during the day and at night.
blocks.translation: 这项由韩国首尔研究人员进行的研究，让老鼠食用由白天和夜里挤出的牛奶制成的奶粉。

blocks.text: Those given night milk, which contained 10 times the amount of melatonin, were less active and less anxious than those fed with the milk collected during daytime, according to the study published in The Journal of Medicinal Food.
blocks.translation: 根据发表在《药用食品杂志》上的这项研究，喂食夜间牛奶（其褪黑激素含量是白天牛奶的十倍）的老鼠，比喂食白天牛奶的老鼠活动更少、焦虑更轻。

blocks.text: Night milk quickened the start of sleep and caused the mice to sleep longer.
blocks.translation: 夜间牛奶加快了入睡速度，并使老鼠睡得更久。

blocks.text: While the effect of cows milk harvested at different time has not been tested on humans up to now, taking melatonin drugs has been suggested to those who are struggling to fall asleep at night.
blocks.translation: 虽然不同时间采集的牛奶的效果迄今尚未在人类身上测试，但已有建议让那些夜里难以入睡的人服用褪黑激素药物。

blocks.text: Previous studies have also indicated that milk can be excellent for helping sleep because of the calcium content, which helps people to relax.
blocks.translation: 此前的研究还表明，牛奶因含钙而非常有助于睡眠，钙能帮助人放松。

blocks.text: Milk is also sugar-free and additive-free with nutritionists recommending skimmed milk as the best choice before bed as it is the least fattening. The more fat you take in before bedtime, the greater burden you will put on your body at night.
blocks.translation: 牛奶还不含糖、不含添加剂，营养学家推荐脱脂牛奶作为睡前最佳选择，因为它最不容易让人发胖。睡前摄入的脂肪越多，夜里给身体带来的负担就越大。

Researchers have discovered that “night milk” contains more melatonin (褪黑激素), which has been proven to help people feel sleepy and reduce anxiety.
The study, by researchers from Seoul, South Korea, involved mice being fed with dried milk powder made from cows milked both during the day and at night.

Those given night milk, which contained 10 times the amount of melatonin, were less active and less anxious than those fed with the milk collected during daytime, according to the study published in The Journal of Medicinal Food.
Night milk quickened the start of sleep and caused the mice to sleep longer.
While the effect of cows milk harvested at different time has not been tested on humans up to now, taking melatonin drugs has been suggested to those who are struggling to fall asleep at night.
Previous studies have also indicated that milk can be excellent for helping sleep because of the calcium content, which helps people to relax.

Milk is also sugar-free and additive-free with nutritionists recommending skimmed milk as the best choice before bed as it is the least fattening. The more fat you take in before bedtime, the greater burden you will put on your body at night.

articles.fallbackTitle: Unlike Britain, the United States does not have a national health care service

blocks.text: Unlike Britain, the United States does not have a national health care service. The government does help pay for some medical care for people who are on low incomes and for old people, but most people buy insurance (保险) to help pay for medical care. The problems of those who cannot afford insurance are an important political subject.
blocks.translation: 与英国不同，美国没有全国性的医疗保健服务。政府确实会帮助低收入者和老年人支付部分医疗费用，但大多数人购买保险来帮助支付医疗费用。那些负担不起保险的人所面临的问题是一个重要的政治议题。

blocks.text: In Britain, when people are ill, they usually go to a family doctor first. However, people in America sometimes go straight to an expert. In Britain, if a patient needs to see a specialist doctor, their family doctor will usually recommend a specialist.
blocks.translation: 在英国，人们生病时通常先去看家庭医生。然而，美国人有时会直接去看专家。孩子通常会被带到专门治疗儿童疾病的医生那里。在英国，如果病人需要看专科医生，家庭医生通常会推荐一位专科医生。

articles.title: The food we eat seems to have profound effects on our health
articles.fallbackTitle: The food we eat seems to have profound effects on our health

blocks.text: The food we eat seems to have profound effects on our health. Although science has made enormous steps in making food more fit to eat, it has, at the same time, made many foods unfit to eat. Some research has shown that perhaps eighty percent of all human illnesses are related to diet and forty percent of cancer is related to the diet as well, especially cancer of the colon. Different cultures are more likely to cause certain different illnesses because of the food that is characteristic in these cultures. That food is related to illness is a new discovery. In 1945, government researchers realized that nitrates, commonly used to preserve color in meats, and other food additives, caused cancer. Yet, these carcinogenic additives remain in our food, and it becomes more difficult all the time to know which things on the packaging labels of processed food are helpful or harmful.
blocks.translation: 我们吃的食物似乎对我们的健康有深远影响。尽管科学在使食物更适合食用方面取得了巨大进步，但与此同时，也让许多食物变得不宜食用。一些研究表明，人类所有疾病中或许有 80% 与饮食有关，40% 的癌症也与饮食有关，尤其是结肠癌。不同文化更可能引发某些不同的疾病，因为这些文化中有其特色的食物。食物与疾病有关是一个新发现。1945 年，政府研究人员意识到，常用于保持肉类色泽的硝酸盐和其他食品添加剂会致癌。然而，这些致癌添加剂仍留在我们的食物中，而且要知道加工食品包装标签上的哪些东西有益、哪些有害，变得越来越困难。

blocks.text: The additives which we eat are not all so direct. Farmers often give penicillin to beef and living animals, and because of this, penicillin has been found in the milk of treated cows. Some times similar drugs are given to animals not for medical purposes, but for financial reasons. The farmers are simply trying to fatten the animals in order to obtain a higher price on the market. Although the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has tried repeatedly to control these procedures, the practices continue.
blocks.translation: 我们摄入的添加剂并不都那么直接。农民常给牛和活体动物使用青霉素，因此，在接受处理的奶牛的牛奶中发现了青霉素。有时，类似的药物被用于动物并非出于医疗目的，而是出于经济原因。农民只是想催肥动物，以便在市场上卖个更高的价钱。尽管美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）多次试图管控这些做法，但这些做法仍在继续。

The additives which we eat are not all so direct. Farmers often give penicillin to beef and living animals, and because of this, penicillin has been found in the milk of treated cows. articles.title: Scientists can learn about man by studying animals, such as mice, rats and monkeys
articles.fallbackTitle: Scientists can learn about man by studying animals, such as mice, rats and monkeys

blocks.text: Scientists can learn about man by studying animals, such as mice, rats and monkeys. The scientists in a laboratory are experimenting on mice and they are studying the relationship between diet and health.
blocks.translation: 科学家可以通过研究老鼠、大鼠和猴子等动物来了解人类。实验室里的科学家正在用老鼠做实验，研究饮食与健康之间的关系。

blocks.text: In this experiment, the scientists are studying the relationship between the amount of food the mice can eat and their health. The mice are in three groups. All these groups are receiving the same healthy diet. But the amount of food that each group is receiving is different. The first group is eating one cup of food each day, the second two cups, and the third three cups.
blocks.translation: 在这个实验中，科学家正在研究老鼠能吃的食物量与健康之间的关系。老鼠分为三组。所有组都吃同样的健康食物，但每组获得的食物量不同。第一组每天吃一杯食物，第二组两杯，第三组三杯。

blocks.text: After three years, the healthiest group is the one that is only eating one cup of food each day. The mice in this group are thinner than normal mice but they are more active. Most of the day, they are running, playing with one another, and using the equipment in their cages. Also, they are living longer. Mice usually live for two years, while most of the mice in this group are still alive after three years.
blocks.translation: 三年后，最健康的是每天只吃一杯食物的那一组。这组老鼠比正常老鼠瘦，但更活跃。一天中大部分时间，它们都在跑动、互相玩耍，使用笼子里的设备。而且它们活得更久。老鼠通常活两年，而这组的大多数老鼠三年后仍然活着。

blocks.text: The second group of mice is of normal weight. They are healthy, too. They are active, but not as active as the thinner mice. But they are only living about two years.
blocks.translation: 第二组老鼠体重正常。它们也健康，很活跃，但不如那些较瘦的老鼠活跃。不过它们只活了大约两年。

blocks.text: The last group of mice is receiving more food than the other two groups. Most of the day, these mice are eating or sleeping. They are not active. These mice are living longer than the scientists thought — about a year and a half, but they are not healthy. They are sick more often than the other two groups.
blocks.translation: 最后一组老鼠获得的食物比其他两组多。一天中大部分时间，这些老鼠不是在吃就是在睡。它们不活跃。这些老鼠比科学家预想的活得久——大约一年半，但它们不健康，生病的次数比其他两组多。

articles.title: Athletes of all shapes and sizes need to pay attention to what goes into their bodies, but
articles.fallbackTitle: Athletes of all shapes and sizes need to pay attention to what goes into their bodies, but

blocks.text: Athletes of all shapes and sizes need to pay attention to what goes into their bodies, but sometimes it’s hard to know exactly what’s being consumed.
blocks.translation: 各种体型、各种身材的运动员都需要注意自己摄入体内的东西，但有时很难确切知道自己吃进了什么。

blocks.text: Sugar is one of those substances that you might take too much without knowing. One can of Coke contains about 39 grams of sugar, amounting to a total of 140 calories（卡路里）. Given their complete lack of nutritional（营养的）value, soft drinks aren’t worth your time.
blocks.translation: 糖就是那种你可能在不知不觉中摄入过多的物质之一。一罐可乐含约 39 克糖，总计 140 卡路里。由于软饮料完全没有营养价值，不值得你花时间。

blocks.text: Another problem is that most people love the taste of sugar and often don’t care whether they consume an unhealthy amount. This presents a risk for the general population, but emphatically for young athletes looking to improve their game. Like many things in life, there’s a fine line between too much sugar and just the right amount.
blocks.translation: 另一个问题是，大多数人喜欢糖的味道，往往不在乎自己摄入的量是否不健康。这对普通人群构成风险，对想要提高运动表现的年轻运动员来说尤其如此。和生活中的许多事情一样，糖摄入过多与恰到好处之间只有一线之隔。

blocks.text: Staying within the 40-to-60 grams per day range, athletes can use simple sugars to their advantage, fueling their normal levels of activity. Beyond that, intense physical activity requires athletes to increase their daily sugar intake.
blocks.translation: 只要保持在每天 40 到 60 克的范围内，运动员就可以利用单糖为自己服务，为日常活动提供能量。超过这个范围，剧烈的体育活动要求运动员增加每日糖摄入量。

blocks.text: Some performance-supporting sugars are found in all kinds of healthy fruits. That’s why NBA All-Star Carmelo Anthony has adopted a diet（饮食）filled with fruits to stay within his weight range of 228-230 pounds. He would not be the dominating force if he didn’t pay attention to his diet, specifically his sugar consumption. He limits sugar intake before and after workouts, both fueling his body and satisfying his sweet tooth.
blocks.translation: 一些有助于运动表现的糖存在于各种健康水果中。这就是为什么 NBA 全明星卡梅罗·安东尼采用以水果为主的饮食，以保持 228 至 230 磅的体重范围。如果他不注意饮食，特别是糖的摄入，就不会成为具有统治力的球员。他在锻炼前后限制糖的摄入，既为身体提供能量，又满足自己的甜食欲望。

paragraphs: Athletes of all shapes and sizes need to pay attention to what goes into their bodies, but sometimes it’s hard to know exactly what’s being consumed.

Sugar is one of those substances that you might take too much without knowing. One can of Coke contains about 39 grams of sugar, amounting to a total of 140 calories（卡路里）. Given their complete lack of nutritional（营养的）value, soft drinks aren’t worth your time.

Another problem is that most people love the taste of sugar and often don’t care whether they consume an unhealthy amount. This presents a risk for the general population, but emphatically for young athletes looking to improve their game. Like many things in life, there’s a fine line between too much sugar and just the right amount.

Staying within the 40-to-60 grams per day range, athletes can use simple sugars to their advantage, fueling their normal levels of activity. Beyond that, intense physical activity requires athletes to increase their daily sugar intake.

Some performance-supporting sugars are found in all kinds of healthy fruits. That’s why NBA All-Star Carmelo Anthony has adopted a diet（饮食）filled with fruits to stay within his weight range of 228-230 pounds. He would not be the dominating force if he didn’t pay attention to his diet, specifically his sugar consumption. He limits sugar intake before and after workouts, both fueling his body and satisfying his sweet tooth.

articles.title: Does stress, anger, or sadness drive you to eat
articles.fallbackTitle: Does stress, anger, or sadness drive you to eat

blocks.text: Does stress, anger, or sadness drive you to eat? Do you turn to food for comfort, or when you’re bored? Many people do. If you often eat for emotional reasons instead of because you’re physically hungry, that can be a problem.
blocks.translation: 压力、愤怒或悲伤会驱使你吃东西吗？你会不会在寻求安慰或无聊时转向食物？许多人都这样。如果你经常因为情绪原因而进食，而不是因为身体饥饿，那可能是个问题。

blocks.text: Obeying the urge to eat more than you need is certain to gain weight. It’s an even bigger problem if you already have health conditions like high blood pressure.
blocks.translation: 屈服从多吃一点的冲动，必然会导致体重增加。如果你已经有高血压等健康问题，那就更是个大问题。

blocks.text: You can get back in control of your emotional eating. The surprising part is, it’s not really about food at all. The solution to emotional eating is less about eating than it is about emotions. You can start with a simple step. “Make a list of what is stressing you, and make a plan to take control of the situation,” New York psychologist Patricia Farrell says. If you can change the situation, go for it. If the problem is out of your control, you can manage the way you think about it. If you can notice your stress in the moment, you can choose how you respond, rather than reacting the way you have in the past. It helps to add a delay between the urge to eat and the actual eating. That gives you time to check in with how you’re feeling and why you want to eat.
blocks.translation: 你可以重新控制情绪化进食。令人惊讶的是，这其实与食物无关。解决情绪化进食，与其说关乎吃，不如说关乎情绪。你可以从一个简单的步骤开始。纽约心理学家帕特里夏·法雷尔说：“列出让你有压力的事情，并制定一个控制局面的计划。”如果你能改变现状，就去做。如果问题超出你的控制，你可以调整自己对它的看法。如果你能在当下察觉自己的压力，你就能选择如何回应，而不是像过去那样做出反应。在进食冲动和真正进食之间加一段延迟会有帮助，这让你有时间审视自己的感受以及想吃东西的原因。

blocks.text: When you get the urge to eat a cookie out of sadness or boredom, remember that you have the choice to wait it out. “Tell yourself to have it later,” Farrell says. Even if it doesn’t, successfully delaying the snack helps you feel more in control.
blocks.translation: 当你因为悲伤或无聊而想吃一块饼干时，记住你可以选择等一等。“告诉自己晚点再吃，”法雷尔说。即使最后没吃，成功推迟这份零食也会让你感到更有掌控感。

blocks.text: In addition, consider talking with a doctor so you can better understand what’s going on with you and the best way to handle it.
blocks.translation: 此外，考虑咨询医生，以便更好地了解自己的状况以及最好的应对方法。

If you can change the situation, go for it. If the problem is out of your control, you can manage the way you think about it. If you can notice your stress in the moment, you can choose how you respond, rather than reacting the way you have in the past. It helps to add a delay between the urge to eat and the actual eating. That gives you time to check in with how you’re feeling and why you want to eat.

When you get the urge to eat a cookie out of sadness or boredom, remember that you have the choice to wait it out. “Tell yourself to have it later,” Farrell says. Even if it doesn’t, successfully delaying the snack helps you feel more in control.

blocks.text: There are many factors which may have an influence on adults and children being able to lead a healthy life. Nowadays, people are very busy. Often, both parents work outside the home. Children are expected to take on more responsibility at home to help their parents. They also have sporting and leisure activities as well as school expectations.
blocks.translation: 有许多因素会影响成人和儿童能否过上健康的生活。如今人们非常忙碌。父母常常都在外工作，孩子被期望在家里承担更多责任来帮助父母。他们还要参加体育和休闲活动，也要达到学校的要求。

blocks.text: The busyness also adds another factor: the need to use cars to get from one place to another quickly.
blocks.translation: 忙碌还带来另一个因素：需要用车快速地从一处赶到另一处。

blocks.text: Today, society places a lot of emphasis on technology. Computers, DVDs, CDs, televisions and Playstations have become major leisure activities, rather than traditional more active pursuits. This has led to a more sedentary lifestyle.
blocks.translation: 如今社会非常强调科技。电脑、DVD、CD、电视和游戏机已成为主要的休闲活动，取代了过去更积极的活动。这导致了一种更久坐不动的生活方式。

blocks.text: The media provide entertainment and information. Unfortunately, they also promote fast food which fits easily into busy lifestyles. It is much more convenient at times to buy a quick takeaway rather than prepare a meal. The media constantly bombard (轰炸) their audience with “perfect” body images, the need to buy the most fashionable clothes, the most up-to-date computer games, the best places to visit and the best things to do.
blocks.translation: 媒体提供娱乐和信息。不幸的是，它们也在推广那些容易融入忙碌生活的快餐。有时候买一份快餐比做一顿饭方便得多。媒体不断用“完美”的身材形象轰炸受众，灌输要买最时尚的衣服、最新的电脑游戏、去最好的地方、做最好的事情。

blocks.text: Environments vary. We may be exposed to pollution, such as cigarette smoke. This can be harmful to people who suffer from breathing difficulties. Environments where passive smoking is unavoidable make it difficult to lead a healthy life.
blocks.translation: 环境各不相同。我们可能接触到污染，比如香烟烟雾。这对有呼吸困难的人来说可能有害。在二手烟无法避免的环境里，很难过上健康的生活。

blocks.text: Perhaps the important factor influencing healthy lifestyles is motivation, or the desire to be healthy. Any person who wants to be healthy will find a way to be healthy—if he/she is motivated enough!
blocks.translation: 也许影响健康生活方式最重要的因素是动机，也就是想健康的愿望。任何想健康的人都会找到健康的办法——只要他的动机足够强！

paragraphs: There are many factors which may have an influence on adults and children being able to lead a healthy life. Nowadays, people are very busy. Often, both parents work outside the home. blocks.text: Long ago men learned that the world of nature is built with mathematical exactness according to refined and powerful laws: every bee strokes its wings exactly 440 times a second to propel itself forty miles an hour; the eye of every fly has exactly 7000 lenses; every spider’s thread is composed of 300 single threads.
blocks.translation: 很久以前，人们就发现自然界是按照精确而强大的法则、以数学般的精确性构建的：每只蜜蜂每秒正好振动翅膀 440 次，从而以每小时四十英里的速度前进；每只苍蝇的眼睛正好有 7000 个晶状体；每根蜘蛛丝由 300 根单丝组成。

blocks.text: The progress of civilization itself can be measured by its range of mathematics. The early Egyptians knew enough of geometry to build the pyramids and the Greeks used trigonometry to measure the circumference of the earth two thousand years before Columbus sailed. European civilization combined geometry and trigonometry with the decimal system of the Arabs to produce the maps with which the Europeans explored the world. In a later century, mathematicians studied the pendulum (钟摆) of the newly invented clock and created the language of calculus to measure motion.
blocks.translation: 文明本身的进步可以用其数学的范围来衡量。早期埃及人掌握了几何学，足以建造金字塔；希腊人在哥伦布航行两千年前就用三角学测量地球的周长。欧洲文明把几何学、三角学与阿拉伯人的十进制结合起来，绘制出用于探索世界的地图。再往后，数学家研究新发明的钟摆，创造了描述运动的微积分语言。

blocks.text: The yardstick of measurement today must cover everything from units tinier than atoms to distances of millions of light years. Speed and accuracy are vital. Man can never send a rocket to Mars unless he knows the exact distance to the planet, since the slightest error could mean missing it by 30, 000 miles. In navigating amid planets and stars, man must have the help of some kind of machine calculators for fast and absolutely accurate information.
blocks.translation: 今天的测量尺度必须覆盖从比原子还小的单位到数百万光年的距离。速度和精确性至关重要。人类若不知道到火星的精确距离，就永远无法把火箭送上火星，因为极小的误差就可能意味着偏离目标三万英里。在行星与恒星之间航行，人类必须借助某种计算机器来获得快速而绝对准确的信息。

paragraphs: Long ago men learned that the world of nature is built with mathematical exactness according to refined and powerful laws: every bee strokes its wings exactly 440 times a second to propel itself forty miles an hour; the eye of every fly has exactly 7000 lenses; every spider’s thread is composed of 300 single threads.

The progress of civilization itself can be measured by its range of mathematics. The early Egyptians knew enough of geometry to build the pyramids and the Greeks used trigonometry to measure the circumference of the earth two thousand years before Columbus sailed. European civilization combined geometry and trigonometry with the decimal system of the Arabs to produce the maps with which the Europeans explored the world. In a later century, mathematicians studied the pendulum (钟摆) of the newly invented clock and created the language of calculus to measure motion.

The yardstick of measurement today must cover everything from units tinier than atoms to distances of millions of light years. Speed and accuracy are vital. Man can never send a rocket to Mars unless he knows the exact distance to the planet, since the slightest error could mean missing it by 30, 000 miles. 文明本身的进步可以用其数学的范围来衡量。早期埃及人掌握了几何学，足以建造金字塔；希腊人在哥伦布航行两千年前就用三角学测量地球的周长。欧洲文明把几何学、三角学与阿拉伯人的十进制结合起来，绘制出用于探索世界的地图。再往后，数学家研究新发明的钟摆，创造了描述运动的微积分语言。
今天的测量尺度必须覆盖从比原子还小的单位到数百万光年的距离。速度和精确性至关重要。人类若不知道到火星的精确距离，就永远无法把火箭送上火星，因为极小的误差就可能意味着偏离目标三万英里。在行星与恒星之间航行，人类必须借助某种计算机器来获得快速而绝对准确的信息。

blocks.text: One day five men who were camping in the Perryson Mountains saw a group of huge apelike (类人猿) creatures coming out of the woods. They ran hurriedly to a small house and locked themselves inside. While they were in, the creatures attacked them by throwing rocks against the walls of the house. After several hours, these strange hairy giants went back into the woods, leaving big footprints behind.
blocks.translation: 有一天，五个在佩里森山露营的人看见一群巨大的类人猿生物从树林里出来。他们急忙跑进一座小屋，把自己锁在里面。他们躲在屋里时，那些生物朝房子的墙壁扔石头攻击他们。几个小时后，这些奇怪的毛茸茸巨人回到树林，留下巨大的脚印。

blocks.text: As soon as the men returned to the town, they told the people of their adventure. However, it was only accepted by a few people who heard about footprints of human-like animals.
blocks.translation: 这些人一回到镇上，就把自己的遭遇告诉了人们。然而，只有少数听说过类人动物脚印的人相信了这件事。

blocks.text: The five men, however, were not the first people to have seen Bigfoot. Long before their experience, it was said that a race of apelike animals had been living in the neighboring mountain for centuries. The local people called them Sasquatch.
blocks.translation: 不过，这五个人并不是最早看见大脚怪的人。早在他们经历之前，就传说有一群类人猿生物在邻近的山里生活了几个世纪。当地人把它们叫做“萨斯科奇”。

blocks.text: In 1978, the workmen who were building a road through the jungles (丛林) often found huge footprints in the earth around their camp.
blocks.translation: 1978 年，在丛林中修路的工人常常在营地周围的泥土里发现巨大的脚印。

blocks.text: Then in 1987, Ron Patten, a film maker who was interested in finding Bigfoot, went into the jungles with a friend. While riding, they were suddenly thrown off from their horses. Patten saw a tall apelike animal standing not far away. He managed to shoot seven rolls of film of the hairy creature before it disappeared in the woods. When Patten’s film was shown to the public, not many people believed his story.
blocks.translation: 后来在 1987 年，对寻找大脚怪感兴趣的制片人罗恩·帕滕和一位朋友进入丛林。骑马时，他们突然被从马上甩了下来。帕滕看见一个高大的类人猿生物站在不远处。他设法在那只毛茸茸的生物消失于树林之前拍了七卷胶卷。当帕滕的影片公开放映时，没有多少人相信他的说法。

blocks.text: In another incident, Roy Bruce, a math teacher and also an experienced hunter, spotted a similar creature. He saw the animal clearly through the telescopic lens (望远瞄准器) of his gun. He said the creature looked more like a human than an animal.
blocks.translation: 在另一起事件中，数学老师、也是经验丰富的猎人的罗伊·布鲁斯发现了一个类似的生物。他通过枪上的望远瞄准器清楚地看到了那只动物。他说那生物看起来更像人而不是动物。

blocks.text: Later many other people also found deep footprints in the same area. In spite of regular reports of sightings and footprints, most experts still do not believe that Bigfoot really exists.
blocks.translation: 后来还有许多人在同一地区发现了很深的脚印。尽管经常有目击和脚印的报道，多数专家仍然不相信大脚怪真的存在。

paragraphs: One day five men who were camping in the Perryson Mountains saw a group of huge apelike (类人猿) creatures coming out of the woods. They ran hurriedly to a small house and locked themselves inside. While they were in, the creatures attacked them by throwing rocks against the walls of the house. After several hours, these strange hairy giants went back into the woods, leaving big footprints behind.
As soon as the men returned to the town, they told the people of their adventure. However, it was only accepted by a few people who heard about footprints of human-like animals.

The five men, however, were not the first people to have seen Bigfoot. Long before their experience, it was said that a race of apelike animals had been living in the neighboring mountain for centuries. The local people called them Sasquatch.
In 1978, the workmen who were building a road through the jungles (丛林) often found huge footprints in the earth around their camp.

Then in 1987, Ron Patten, a film maker who was interested in finding Bigfoot, went into the jungles with a friend. While riding, they were suddenly thrown off from their horses. Patten saw a tall apelike animal standing not far away. He managed to shoot seven rolls of film of the hairy creature before it disappeared in the woods. When Patten’s film was shown to the public, not many people believed his story.

In another incident, Roy Bruce, a math teacher and also an experienced hunter, spotted a similar creature. He saw the animal clearly through the telescopic lens (望远瞄准器) of his gun. He said the creature looked more like a human than an animal.
Later many other people also found deep footprints in the same area. In spite of regular reports of sightings and footprints, most experts still do not believe that Bigfoot really exists.

paragraphs: Would it surprise you to learn that, like animals, trees communicate with each other and transmit their wealth to the next generation?

UBC Professor Simard explains how trees are much more complex than most of us ever imagined. Although Charles Darwin thought that trees are competing for survival of the fittest, Simard shows just how wrong he was. In fact, the opposite is true: trees survive through their co-operation and support, passing around necessary nutrition “depending on who needs it”.

Nitrogen (氮) and carbon are shared through miles of underground fungi (真菌) networks, making sure that all trees in the forest ecological system give and receive just the right amount to keep them all healthy. This hidden system works in a very similar way to the networks of neurons (神经元) in our brains, and when one tree is destroyed, it affects all.

Simard talks about “mother trees”, usually the largest and oldest plants on which all other trees depend. She explains how dying trees pass on the wealth to the next generation, transporting important minerals to young trees so they may continue to grow. When humans cut down “mother trees” with no awareness of these highly complex “tree societies” or the networks on which they feed, we are reducing the chances of survival for the entire forest.

“We didn’t take any notice of it” Simard says sadly. “Dying trees move nutrition into the young trees before dying, but we never give them chance.” If we could put across the message to the forestry industry, we could make a huge difference towards our environmental protection efforts for the future.

articles.title: A new study shows that plants are creating frequencies in responses to their surroundings,
articles.fallbackTitle: A new study shows that plants are creating frequencies in responses to their surroundings,

blocks.text: A new study shows that plants are creating frequencies in responses to their surroundings, or in other words, they are reacting. These “reactions” in plants, which we could see as analogous to human senses, are actually nothing new. We have learned over the past few years that plants are capable of seeing, hearing, and smelling.
blocks.translation: 一项新研究表明，植物会因应周围环境产生不同频率，换句话说，它们在做反应。植物这些“反应”可以看作类似人类的感官，其实并不新鲜。过去几年我们已经了解到，植物能够看见、听见和闻到。

blocks.text: And with this newest finding we are just one sense away from completing the five human senses in some plants. For the first time, plants have been recorded making airborne sounds when stressed, which researchers say could open up a new field of precision agriculture where farmers listen for water starved crops.
blocks.translation: 有了这项最新发现，我们在某些植物身上只差一种感官就能凑齐人类的五种感官。研究人员首次记录到植物在受压时发出空气传播的声音，他们说这可能开辟精准农业的新领域，让农民通过“听”来发现缺水的作物。

blocks.text: The researchers found that tomato and tobacco plants made sounds at frequencies humans cannot hear when facing situations such as lack of water or when being cut.
blocks.translation: 研究人员发现，番茄和烟草植物在缺水或被切割等情况下，会发出人类听不到的声音频率。

blocks.text: On average, drought-stressed tomato plants made 35 sounds per hour, while tobacco plants made 11 and unstressed plants produced fewer than one sound per hour.
blocks.translation: 平均而言，受干旱胁迫的番茄植株每小时发出 35 个声音，烟草植株发出 11 个，而未受胁迫的植株每小时发出的声音不到一个。

blocks.text: The researchers trained a machine-learning model to tell difference between the plant’s sounds and the wind, rain, and other surrounding noises of the greenhouse, in order to correctly identify the source of stress. Results showed that drought-stressed plants make significantly more sounds than control plants.
blocks.translation: 研究人员训练了一个机器学习模型，用来区分植物的声音与风、雨以及温室中其他环境噪音，从而正确识别压力来源。结果显示，受干旱胁迫的植物发出的声音明显多于对照植物。

blocks.text: Humans cannot hear the whole range of frequencies around us. If we could, we would likely become absent-minded and anxious by always hearing the frequencies around us including radio frequencies from cell towers near us or even cooking a frozen meal in the microwave. Thankfully, the range of human hearing is typically considered to be only 20 Hz to 20, 000 Hz. That is why humans are not sensitive to the sounds that plants are making.
blocks.translation: 人类无法听到周围所有的频率范围。如果能听到，我们大概会变得心不在焉、焦虑不安，因为会一直听到周围的各种频率，包括附近手机基站的无线电频率，甚至用微波炉加热冷冻食品时的频率。所幸，人类的听觉范围通常被认为只有 20 赫兹到 20,000 赫兹。这就是人类对植物发出的声音不敏感的原因。

paragraphs: A new study shows that plants are creating frequencies in responses to their surroundings, or in other words, they are reacting. These “reactions” in plants, which we could see as analogous to human senses, are actually nothing new. We have learned over the past few years that plants are capable of seeing, hearing, and smelling.

And with this newest finding we are just one sense away from completing the five human senses in some plants. For the first time, plants have been recorded making airborne sounds when stressed, which researchers say could open up a new field of precision agriculture where farmers listen for water starved crops.
The researchers found that tomato and tobacco plants made sounds at frequencies humans cannot hear when facing situations such as lack of water or when being cut.
On average, drought-stressed tomato plants made 35 sounds per hour, while tobacco plants made 11 and unstressed plants produced fewer than one sound per hour.

The researchers trained a machine-learning model to tell difference between the plant’s sounds and the wind, rain, and other surrounding noises of the greenhouse, in order to correctly identify the source of stress. Results showed that drought-stressed plants make significantly more sounds than control plants.

Humans cannot hear the whole range of frequencies around us. If we could, we would likely become absent-minded and anxious by always hearing the frequencies around us including radio frequencies from cell towers near us or even cooking a frozen meal in the microwave. Thankfully, the range of human hearing is typically considered to be only 20 Hz to 20, 000 Hz. That is why humans are not sensitive to the sounds that plants are making.

translations: 一项新研究表明，植物会因应周围环境产生不同频率，换句话说，它们在做反应。植物这些“反应”可以看作类似人类的感官，其实并不新鲜。过去几年我们已经了解到，植物能够看见、听见和闻到。
有了这项最新发现，我们在某些植物身上只差一种感官就能凑齐人类的五种感官。研究人员首次记录到植物在受压时发出空气传播的声音，他们说这可能开辟精准农业的新领域，让农民通过“听”来发现缺水的作物。
研究人员发现，番茄和烟草植物在缺水或被切割等情况下，会发出人类听不到的声音频率。

人类无法听到周围所有的频率范围。如果能听到，我们大概会变得心不在焉、焦虑不安，因为会一直听到周围的各种频率，包括附近手机基站的无线电频率，甚至用微波炉加热冷冻食品时的频率。所幸，人类的听觉范围通常被认为只有 20 赫兹到 20,000 赫兹。这就是人类对植物发出的声音不敏感的原因。

articles.title: Half of the world's coral reefs (珊瑚礁) have died in the last 30 years

blocks.text: Half of the world's coral reefs (珊瑚礁) have died in the last 30 years. Now scientists are racing to ensure that the rest survive. Even if global warming were to stop right now, scientists predict that more than 90% of corals will die by 2050. If no major steps are taken to address the problem, the reefs may be headed for total extinction (灭绝).
blocks.translation: 过去 30 年里，世界上一半的珊瑚礁已经死亡。如今科学家正争分夺秒，确保其余的珊瑚礁存活下来。即使全球变暖此刻停止，科学家仍预测到 2050 年将有超过 90% 的珊瑚死亡。如果不采取重大措施解决这个问题，珊瑚礁可能走向彻底灭绝。

blocks.text: The planet's health depends on the survival of coral reefs. They are often described as "the rainforests of the sea", because they provide shelter for a wide variety of sea life. In addition, the reefs serve as barriers that protect coastlines from the full force of powerful storms.
blocks.translation: 地球的健康有赖于珊瑚礁的存续。它们常被称作“海洋中的雨林”，因为它们为种类繁多的海洋生物提供栖息之所。此外，珊瑚礁还像屏障一样，保护海岸线免受强风暴的全部威力。

blocks.text: Corals are used in medical research for cures to diseases. They are key to local economies as well, since the reefs attract tourists, the fishing industry, and other businesses, bringing in billions of dollars.
blocks.translation: 珊瑚被用于医学研究，以寻找疾病的疗法。它们对地方经济也至关重要，因为珊瑚礁吸引游客、渔业和其他产业，带来数十亿美元的收入。

blocks.text: Corals are particularly sensitive to changes in temperature. A rise of just 1 to 2 degrees can force the corals to drive out the algae (水藻). Then the corals turn white in a process called "bleaching". Corals can recover from short-term bleaching, but long-term bleaching can cause permanent damage. In 1998, when sea surface temperatures were the highest in recorded history, coral reefs around the world suffered the most severe bleaching. It is estimated that even under the best of conditions, many of these coral reefs will need decades to recover.
blocks.translation: 珊瑚对温度变化特别敏感。仅仅升高 1 至 2 度，就能迫使珊瑚排出水藻。随后珊瑚会变白，这一过程称为“白化”。珊瑚可以从短期白化中恢复，但长期白化会造成永久损伤。1998 年海面温度是有记录以来最高的，世界各地的珊瑚礁经历了最严重的白化。据估计，即使在最好的条件下，其中许多珊瑚礁也需要数十年才能恢复。

blocks.text: Although reefs face other threats from pollution, industrial activities, and overfishing, it is global climate change that most concerns scientists. Scientists remain hopeful that it's not too late to save the reefs, and some are moving ahead on experiments to accomplish that goal.
blocks.translation: 尽管珊瑚礁还面临污染、工业活动和过度捕捞等其他威胁，但最令科学家担忧的是全球气候变化。科学家仍抱有希望，认为拯救珊瑚礁为时未晚，一些人正在推进实验以实现这一目标。

paragraphs: Half of the world's coral reefs (珊瑚礁) have died in the last 30 years. Now scientists are racing to ensure that the rest survive. Even if global warming were to stop right now, scientists predict that more than 90% of corals will die by 2050. If no major steps are taken to address the problem, the reefs may be headed for total extinction (灭绝).

The planet's health depends on the survival of coral reefs. They are often described as "the rainforests of the sea", because they provide shelter for a wide variety of sea life. In addition, the reefs serve as barriers that protect coastlines from the full force of powerful storms.

Corals are used in medical research for cures to diseases. They are key to local economies as well, since the reefs attract tourists, the fishing industry, and other businesses, bringing in billions of dollars.

Corals are particularly sensitive to changes in temperature. A rise of just 1 to 2 degrees can force the corals to drive out the algae (水藻). Then the corals turn white in a process called "bleaching". Corals can recover from short-term bleaching, but long-term bleaching can cause permanent damage. In 1998, when sea surface temperatures were the highest in recorded history, coral reefs around the world suffered the most severe bleaching. It is estimated that even under the best of conditions, many of these coral reefs will need decades to recover.

Although reefs face other threats from pollution, industrial activities, and overfishing, it is global climate change that most concerns scientists. Scientists remain hopeful that it's not too late to save the reefs, and some are moving ahead on experiments to accomplish that goal.

articles.title: Chokwe Selassie is on a mission to help drivers avoid potholes(路面坑洼)
articles.fallbackTitle: Chokwe Selassie is on a mission to help drivers avoid potholes(路面坑洼)

blocks.text: Chokwe Selassie is on a mission to help drivers avoid potholes(路面坑洼). The eighth-grader got his inspiration on a recent morning, when his mother was driving him to school. Their car was damaged as it went over a huge pothole in the middle of the street in their hometown of Jackson, Mississippi. “I decided I was going to do something about the pothole problem in my city,” said Chokwe. His solution: an app that warns drivers when there is a pothole ahead.
blocks.translation: 乔克韦·塞拉西正在执行一项任务：帮助司机避开路面坑洼。这位八年级学生的灵感来自最近的一个早晨，当时母亲开车送他上学。他们的车在家乡密西西比州杰克逊市一条街道中间碾过一个巨大的坑洼，损坏了。“我决定要为这座城市的坑洼问题做点什么，”乔克韦说。他的解决方案是：一款在前方有坑洼时提醒司机的应用。

blocks.text: Chokwe developed the app with his friends. “When the app detects a pothole, it is highlighted in red,” Chokwe says. “And if you get close to the pothole, your phone will warn you with a beep.” Drivers can also use the app to report any potholes they encounter, and to look for other routes they can take to avoid roads that have them.
blocks.translation: 乔克韦和朋友们一起开发了这款应用。“当应用检测到坑洼时，它会用红色标出，”乔克韦说。“如果你接近坑洼，手机会发出蜂鸣声提醒你。”司机还可以用这款应用报告他们遇到的任何坑洼，并查找可以避开有坑洼道路的其他路线。

blocks.text: The app relies on current available information about the streets of Jackson. “It works by using the city’s 311 call system, so it uses information already stored in a database,” Chokwe says. Through the call system, citizens dial 311 to report non-emergency problems—which include potholes. As Chokwe and his friends worked on the app, they also went street by street throughout the city. They determined that focusing on the 10 busiest streets in Jackson would give them a large enough sample size to test it.
blocks.translation: 这款应用依赖杰克逊市街道现有的信息。“它利用该市的 311 呼叫系统运作，因此使用的是已经存储在数据库中的信息，”乔克韦说。通过这个呼叫系统，市民拨打 311 报告非紧急问题——其中包括坑洼。乔克韦和朋友们开发应用时，还走遍了全城一条街一条街地考察。他们确定，聚焦杰克逊最繁忙的 10 条街道，就能获得足够大的样本来测试。

blocks.text: Although the app isn’t yet available for sale, Chokwe is already looking for ways to improve it. The app remains limited to 10 streets in Jackson, but he hopes to add more, so that it includes every street in the city. And then he wants to go even farther. “I want to keep working on the app until it’s nationwide,” Chokwe says.
blocks.translation: 虽然这款应用尚未发售，乔克韦已经在寻找改进的方法。应用目前仍只覆盖杰克逊的 10 条街道，但他希望增加更多，最终包含全城每一条街。然后他还想走得更远。“我想继续改进这款应用，直到它推广到全国，”乔克韦说。

Chokwe developed the app with his friends. “When the app detects a pothole, it is highlighted in red,” Chokwe says. “And if you get close to the pothole, your phone will warn you with a beep.” Drivers can also use the app to report any potholes they encounter, and to look for other routes they can take to avoid roads that have them.

The app relies on current available information about the streets of Jackson. “It works by using the city’s 311 call system, so it uses information already stored in a database,” Chokwe says. Through the call system, citizens dial 311 to report non-emergency problems—which include potholes. As Chokwe and his friends worked on the app, they also went street by street throughout the city. They determined that focusing on the 10 busiest streets in Jackson would give them a large enough sample size to test it.

Although the app isn’t yet available for sale, Chokwe is already looking for ways to improve it. The app remains limited to 10 streets in Jackson, but he hopes to add more, so that it includes every street in the city. And then he wants to go even farther. “I want to keep working on the app until it’s nationwide,” Chokwe says.

blocks.text: In what now seems like the prehistoric times of computer history, the earth’s post-war era, there was a quite widespread concern that computers would take over the world from man one day. Already today, less than forty years later, as computers are relieving us of more and more of the routine tasks in business and in our personal lives, we are faced with a less dramatic but also less foreseen problem. People tend to be over-trusting of computers and are reluctant to challenge their authority. Indeed, they behave as if they were hardly aware that wrong buttons may be pushed, or that a computer may simply malfunction.
blocks.translation: 在如今看来像是计算机史前时代的战后时期，人们普遍担心电脑有一天会从人类手中接管世界。而今天，不到四十年后，当电脑替我们承担商业和个人生活中越来越多的日常事务时，我们面对着一个不那么戏剧化、却也较少被预见的问题。人们往往过度信任电脑，不愿质疑它的权威。事实上，他们的表现仿佛几乎没有意识到可能按错按钮，或者电脑可能干脆出故障。

blocks.text: Obviously, there would be no point in investing in a computer if you had to check all its answers, but people should also rely on their own internal computers and check the machine when they have the feeling that something has gone wrong. Questioning and routine double checks must continue to be as much a part of good business as they were in pre-computer days. Maybe each computer should come with the following warning: for all the help this computer may provide, it should not be seen as a substitute for fundamental thinking and reasoning skills.
blocks.translation: 显然，如果你必须核对电脑的所有答案，投资电脑就没有意义；但人们也应当依靠自己的“内部计算机”，在感觉出了问题的时候核查机器。质疑和例行的复核必须继续成为良好商业的一部分，就像前电脑时代一样。也许每台电脑都该附带这样一条警告：无论这台电脑能提供多少帮助，都不应被视为基本思考与推理能力的替代品。

blocks.text: During the past few years, the popularization of the Internet, by lowering the cost of global communication to moderate levels, is leading to a near-perfect market for information. It has bred enterprises that grow and change with astonishing speed, creating millionaires and invigorating (振兴) the economy. The Net has brought to even poor libraries a wealth of resources at very low cost. It has enabled individuals to speak in forums small and large, with an ease and fluency that would delight the founders of this nation, if they could see email, the World Wide Web, Usenet, and online chat.
blocks.translation: 过去几年，互联网的普及把全球通讯成本降到中等水平，正在带来一个近乎完美的信息市场。它催生了以惊人速度成长和变化的企业，造就了百万富翁，也振兴了经济。网络以极低的成本把丰富的资源带给了甚至很穷的图书馆。它让个人能够在大大小小的论坛上发言，那种轻松流畅会让这个国家的缔造者们欣喜——如果他们能看到电子邮件、万维网、Usenet 和在线聊天的话。

blocks.text: The tremendous good done by the popularization of the Internet has caused some problems, of course. Chief among these are a weakening of privacy, greater exposure for matters that most people would prefer were absent from society, such as hate speech and child pornography, and an increased risk of one’s children (or oneself) being confronted by an image or text that better might have been left unseen. The Internet has brought the entire world into the living room, but some people are finding that there are certain parts of the world they would prefer not to have anywhere in their home. An example that has become an everyday displeasure for many is junk email, also called “spam”. On a bad day, up to 30% of the email processed by major Internet service providers is spam, much of it promoting sex sites and get-rich-quick schemes. Many people have had to abandon their email accounts, as they become filled with trash. Left unchecked, spam could spoil the great public good of the Internet.
blocks.translation: 当然，互联网普及带来的巨大好处也造成了一些问题。其中主要是隐私被削弱，多数人宁愿社会中不存在的东西（如仇恨言论和儿童色情）更容易暴露，以及自己的孩子（或自己）更可能接触到本不该看到的图像或文字。互联网把整个世界带进了客厅，但有些人发现，世界某些部分他们宁愿家里任何地方都不要有。对许多人来说已成为日常烦恼的一个例子是垃圾邮件，也叫“spam”。在糟糕的日子里，主要互联网服务商处理的邮件中多达 30% 是垃圾邮件，其中许多在推销色情网站和快速致富方案。许多人不得不放弃自己的电子邮箱，因为里面塞满了垃圾。如果放任不管，垃圾邮件可能毁掉互联网这一伟大的公共财富。

blocks.text: Television has changed the lifestyle of people in every industrialized country in the world. In the United States, where sociologists have studied the effects, some interesting observations have been made.
blocks.translation: 电视改变了世界上每个工业化国家人们的生活方式。在美国，社会学家研究了其影响，得出了一些有趣的观察。

blocks.text: Television, although not essential, has become an important part of most people's lives. It alters people's ways of seeing the world; in many ways, it supports and sustains (维持) modern life.
blocks.translation: 电视虽然不是必需品，却已成为大多数人生活的重要部分。它改变了人们看世界的方式；在许多方面，它支撑并维持着现代生活。

blocks.text: Television has become a baby-sitter, an introducer of conversations, the major transmitter of culture and a keeper of tradition. Yet when what can be seen on TV in one day is critically analyzed, it becomes evident that television is not a teacher but a sustainer; the poor quality of programming does not elevate (提高) people into greater understanding, but rather maintains and encourages the life as it exists.
blocks.translation: 电视已成为保姆、话题的引子、文化的主要传播者和传统的守护者。然而，当仔细分析一天中电视上能看到的内容时，就会发现电视不是老师，而是维持者；低劣的节目质量并不能把人提升到更高的理解，反而维持并鼓励生活维持原样。

blocks.text: The primary reason for the lack of quality in American television is related to both the history of TV programming development and the economics of TV. Television in America began with the radio. Radio companies and their sponsors first experimented with television. Therefore, the close relationship which the advertisers had with radio programs became the system for American TV. Sponsors not only paid money for time within programs, but many actually produced the programs. Thus, in American society, television is primarily concerned with reflecting and attracting society rather than experimenting with new ideas. Advertisers want to attract the largest viewing audience possible. To do so requires that the programs be entertaining rather than educational, attractive rather than challenging.
blocks.translation: 美国电视质量不高的主要原因，既与电视节目发展的历史有关，也与电视的经济学有关。美国的电视始于广播。广播公司及其赞助商最早尝试电视。因此，广告商与广播节目之间的密切关系，成了美国电视的体制。赞助商不仅花钱买节目时段，许多还实际制作节目。于是，在美国社会，电视主要关心的是反映和吸引社会，而不是尝试新想法。广告商想吸引尽可能多的观众。要做到这一点，节目就必须是娱乐性的而非教育性的，是吸引人的而非具有挑战性的。

blocks.text: Television in America today remains, to a large extent, with the same organization and standards as it had thirty years ago. The hope for further development and true achievement toward improving society will require a change in the entire system.
blocks.translation: 今天的美国电视在很大程度上仍保持着三十年前的体制和标准。要进一步发展、真正在改善社会方面取得成就，就需要改变整个体制。

Television has become a baby-sitter, an introducer of conversations, the major transmitter of culture and a keeper of tradition. Radio companies and their sponsors first experimented with television. Therefore, the close relationship which the advertisers had with radio programs became the system for American TV. Sponsors not only paid money for time within programs, but many actually produced the programs. Thus, in American society, television is primarily concerned with reflecting and attracting society rather than experimenting with new ideas. Advertisers want to attract the largest viewing audience possible. To do so requires that the programs be entertaining rather than educational, attractive rather than challenging.

Television in America today remains, to a large extent, with the same organization and standards as it had thirty years ago. The hope for further development and true achievement toward improving society will require a change in the entire system.

translations: 电视改变了世界上每个工业化国家人们的生活方式。在美国，社会学家研究了其影响，得出了一些有趣的观察。
电视虽然不是必需品，却已成为大多数人生活的重要部分。它改变了人们看世界的方式；在许多方面，它支撑并维持着现代生活。
电视已成为保姆、话题的引子、文化的主要传播者和传统的守护者。然而，当仔细分析一天中电视上能看到的内容时，就会发现电视不是老师，而是维持者；低劣的节目质量并不能把人提升到更高的理解，反而维持并鼓励生活维持原样。

美国电视质量不高的主要原因，既与电视节目发展的历史有关，也与电视的经济学有关。美国的电视始于广播。广播公司及其赞助商最早尝试电视。因此，广告商与广播节目之间的密切关系，成了美国电视的体制。赞助商不仅花钱买节目时段，许多还实际制作节目。于是，在美国社会，电视主要关心的是反映和吸引社会，而不是尝试新想法。广告商想吸引尽可能多的观众。要做到这一点，节目就必须是娱乐性的而非教育性的，是吸引人的而非具有挑战性的。
今天的美国电视在很大程度上仍保持着三十年前的体制和标准。要进一步发展、真正在改善社会方面取得成就，就需要改变整个体制。

blocks.text: Ask someone what they have done to help the environment recently and they, will almost certainly mention recycling. Recycling in the home is very important of course. However, being forced to recycle often means we already have more material than we need. We are dealing with the results of that over-consumption in the greenest way possible, but it would be far better if we did not need to bring so much material home in the first place.
blocks.translation: 问别人最近为环境做了什么，他们几乎肯定会提到回收。当然，家庭回收很重要。然而，被迫回收往往意味着我们拥有的材料已超过所需。我们正用最环保的方式处理过度消费的结果，但如果一开始就不把这么多材料带回家，那会好得多。

blocks.text: The total amount of packaging increased by 12% between 2010 and 2017. It now makes up a third of a typical household’s waste in the UK. In many supermarkets nowadays food items are packaged twice with plastic and cardboard.
blocks.translation: 2010 年至 2017 年间，包装总量增长了 12%。它现在占英国家庭典型垃圾的三分之一。如今许多超市的食品都用塑料和纸板包装两层。

blocks.text: Too much packaging is doing serious damage to the environment. The UK, for example, is running out of it for carrying this unnecessary waste. If such packaging is burnt, it gives off greenhouse gases which go on to cause the greenhouse effect. Recycling helps, but the process itself uses energy. The solution is not to produce such items in the first place. Food waste is a serious problem, too. Too many supermarkets encourage customers to buy more than they need. However, a few of them are coming round to the idea that this cannot continue, encouraging customers to reuse their plastic bags, for example.
blocks.translation: 过多包装正在严重损害环境。例如，英国正越来越没有地方堆放这些不必要的废物。如果这些包装被焚烧，会释放温室气体，进而造成温室效应。回收有帮助，但回收过程本身也消耗能源。解决办法是一开始就不生产这样的物品。食物浪费也是个严重问题。太多超市鼓励顾客购买超过所需的东西。不过，少数超市开始接受这种局面不能继续下去的想法，例如鼓励顾客重复使用塑料袋。

blocks.text: But this is not just about supermarkets. It is about all of us. We have learned to associate packaging with quality. We have learned to think that something unpackaged is of poor quality. This is especially true of food. blocks.text: There are signs of hope. As more of us recycle, we are beginning to realize just how much unnecessary material we are collecting. We need to face the wastefulness of our consumer culture, but we have a mountain to climb.

articles.title: Are some people born clever and others born stupid
articles.fallbackTitle: Are some people born clever and others born stupid

blocks.text: Are some people born clever and others born stupid? Or is intelligence developed by our environment and our experience? Strangely enough, the answer to these questions is yes. To some extent our intelligence is given to us at birth, and no amount of special education can make a genius out of a child born with low intelligence. On the other hand, a child who lives in a boring environment will develop his intelligence less than one who lives in rich and varied surroundings. Thus the limits of a person’s intelligence are fixed at birth, whether or not he reaches those limits will depend on his environment. This view, now held by most experts, can be supported in a number of ways.
blocks.translation: 有些人生来聪明，有些人生来愚笨吗？还是智力由环境和经历发展而来？奇怪的是，这两个问题的答案都是“是”。在某种程度上，智力是出生时就被赋予的，再多的特殊教育也无法让一个天生智力低下的孩子变成天才。另一方面，生活在枯燥环境中的孩子，其智力发展会不如生活在丰富多样环境中的孩子。因此，一个人智力的上限在出生时就已确定，但他能否达到这个上限，则取决于环境。这一观点如今为大多数专家所接受，并有多方面的支持。

blocks.text: It is easy to show that intelligence is to some extent something we are born with. The closer the blood relationship between two people is, the closer they are likely to be in intelligence. Thus if we take two unrelated people at random from the population, it is likely that their degree of intelligence will be completely different. If, on the other hand, we take two identical twins, they will very likely be as intelligent as each other. Relations like brothers and sisters, parents and children, usually have similar intelligence, and this clearly suggests that intelligence depend on birth.
blocks.translation: 很容易证明，智力在某种程度上是与生俱来的。两个人的血缘关系越近，他们的智力水平往往越接近。因此，如果从人群中随机选取两个没有亲属关系的人，他们的智力水平很可能完全不同。反过来，如果选取一对同卵双胞胎，他们的智力很可能不相上下。兄弟姐妹、父母子女等亲属通常智力相近，这清楚地表明智力与出生有关。

blocks.text: Imagine now that we take two identical twins and put them in different environments. We might send one, for example, to a university and the other to a factory where the work is boring. We would soon find differences in their intelligence developing, and this indicates that environment as well as birth plays a part. This conclusion is also suggested by the fact that people who live in close contact with each other, but who are not related at all are likely to have similar degree of intelligence.
blocks.translation: 现在设想我们把一对同卵双胞胎放到不同环境中：比如送一个上大学，送另一个去工作枯燥的工厂。很快就会发现他们的智力发展出现差异，这说明环境和出生一样起作用。这一结论还有一个佐证：彼此密切接触但完全没有亲属关系的人，智力水平也可能相似。

articles.title: Wyatt Baldwin has been playing rock, paper, scissors(剪刀)since he was a kid.The game helped
articles.fallbackTitle: Wyatt Baldwin has been playing rock, paper, scissors(剪刀)since he was a kid.The game helped

blocks.text: Wyatt Baldwin has been playing rock, paper, scissors(剪刀)since he was a kid.The game helped him settle disagreements with his three older sisters. “I never got the chance to pick what we watched on TV until I learned the sport of rock, paper, scissors,” he says.
blocks.translation: 怀亚特·鲍德温从小就开始玩石头剪刀布。这个游戏帮他解决与三个姐姐之间的分歧。他说：“在学会石头剪刀布这项‘运动’之前，我从来没有机会决定我们看电视看什么。”

blocks.text: Baldwin is president of the World Rock Paper Scissors Association.He has played in and hosted competitions all around the globe.He once had a 43-game winning streak.What is the secret to his success? “Look for patterns in either your opponent’s moves or behavior,” he says.As all serious rock, paper, scissors players know, there is more to the game than luck.
blocks.translation: 鲍德温是世界石头剪刀布协会主席。他参加过并主持过世界各地的比赛，曾创下 43 连胜。他成功的秘诀是什么？“观察对手出拳或行为中的模式。”他说。所有认真的石头剪刀布玩家都知道，这个游戏靠的不只是运气。

blocks.text: People have been playing rock, paper, scissors for about 2, 000 years.It is played everywhere.Some cultures use different hand symbols, but the idea is the same.You and an opponent each “throw” one of three hand symbols.You win, lose, or tie (不分胜负).Many people think the game is all luck.It seems that your chances of winning and losing are about the same, but the outcome of the game is not random.That is because human behavior is not random.There are patterns in how people make decisions.
blocks.translation: 人们玩石头剪刀布已有约两千年，世界各地都有人玩。有些文化使用不同的手势，但游戏理念相同：你和对手各“出”三种手势之一，然后获胜、失败或平局。许多人认为这个游戏全凭运气，输赢机会似乎大致相同，但结果并非随机，因为人的行为不是随机的——人们做决定时存在模式。

blocks.text: A study at Zhejiang University in China looked at how people play rock, paper, scissors. It followed 360 students in a competition.Researchers found two key patterns.Winners tended to repeat their winning hand symbols.Losers tended to go from rock to paper to scissors.
blocks.translation: 中国浙江大学的一项研究观察了人们玩石头剪刀布的方式，追踪了 360 名参加比赛的学生。研究者发现两个关键模式：赢家倾向于重复自己获胜的手势；输家则倾向于按石头→布→剪刀的顺序变化。

blocks.text: Knowing the psychology of the game is not a sure ticket to winning, but it can help.Ken Watson is one of the world’s best rock, paper, scissors players.He says winning takes skill. “You have to size up your opponent.” Luck and chance play a part, but “you have to be prepared and have a strategy, ” he says, “Part of my strategy is being confident.”
blocks.translation: 了解这个游戏的心理机制并不能保证获胜，但会有帮助。肯·沃森是世界顶尖的石头剪刀布玩家之一。他说获胜需要技巧：“你必须掂量你的对手。”运气和偶然确实起作用，但“你必须做好准备、有策略”，他说，“我策略的一部分就是保持自信。”

blocks.text: According to Baldwin, “practice, practice, practice” is the key to success. “You can try practicing against yourself in front of a mirror, ” he says.
blocks.translation: 鲍德温认为，“练习、练习、再练习”是成功的关键。他说：“你可以试着对着镜子和自己练。”

A study at Zhejiang University in China looked at how people play rock, paper, scissors. It followed 360 students in a competition.Researchers found two key patterns.Winners tended to repeat their winning hand symbols.Losers tended to go from rock to paper to scissors.

Knowing the psychology of the game is not a sure ticket to winning, but it can help.Ken Watson is one of the world’s best rock, paper, scissors players.He says winning takes skill. “You have to size up your opponent.” Luck and chance play a part, but “you have to be prepared and have a strategy, ” he says, “Part of my strategy is being confident.”
According to Baldwin, “practice, practice, practice” is the key to success. “You can try practicing against yourself in front of a mirror, ” he says.

鲍德温是世界石头剪刀布协会主席。他参加过并主持过世界各地的比赛，曾创下 43 连胜。他成功的秘诀是什么？“观察对手出拳或行为中的模式。”他说。所有认真的石头剪刀布玩家都知道，这个游戏靠的不只是运气。
人们玩石头剪刀布已有约两千年，世界各地都有人玩。有些文化使用不同的手势，但游戏理念相同：你和对手各“出”三种手势之一，然后获胜、失败或平局。许多人认为这个游戏全凭运气，输赢机会似乎大致相同，但结果并非随机，因为人的行为不是随机的——人们做决定时存在模式。
中国浙江大学的一项研究观察了人们玩石头剪刀布的方式，追踪了 360 名参加比赛的学生。研究者发现两个关键模式：赢家倾向于重复自己获胜的手势；输家则倾向于按石头→布→剪刀的顺序变化。

鲍德温认为，“练习、练习、再练习”是成功的关键。他说：“你可以试着对着镜子和自己练。”

articles.title: Faces, like fingerprints, are unique

blocks.text: Faces, like fingerprints, are unique. Have you ever wondered how it is possible for us to recognize people? Even a skilled writer probably could not describe all the features that make one face different from another. Yet a very young child — or even an animal, such as a pigeon — can learn to recognize faces. We all take this ability for granted. We also tell people apart by how they behave. When we talk about someone’s personality, we mean the ways in which he or she acts, speaks, thinks and feels that make that individual different from others. Like the human face, human personality is very complex. But describing someone’s personality in words is somewhat easier than describing his face. If you were asked to describe what a “nice face” looked like, you probably would have a difficult time doing so. But if you were asked to describe a “nice person”, you might begin to think about someone who was kind, considerate, friendly, warm, and so forth.
blocks.translation: 人脸像指纹一样独一无二。你是否想过，我们为什么能够认出别人？即使是一位技艺高超的作家，恐怕也无法描述出使每张脸彼此不同的全部特征。然而，一个很小的孩子——甚至鸽子这样的动物——都能学会认脸。我们都把这种能力视为理所当然。我们也通过行为方式来区分人。当我们谈论某人的“人格”时，指的是他或她行动、说话、思考和感受的方式，这些方式使这个人区别于他人。人的脸很复杂，人格同样复杂；但用语言描述一个人的人格，比描述他的脸要容易一些。如果让你描述一张“好看的脸”是什么样，你大概会很为难；但如果让你描述一个“好人”，你可能会想到善良、体贴、友好、温暖等等。

blocks.text: There are many words to describe how a person thinks, feels and acts. Gordon, an American psychologist, found nearly 18, 000 English words characterizing differences in people’s behavior. And many of us use this information as a basis for describing, or typing his personality.
blocks.translation: 有许多词可以描述一个人如何思考、感受和行动。美国心理学家戈登发现，英语中近 18,000 个词可以刻画人们行为上的差异。我们许多人就以这些信息为基础来描述或归类一个人的人格。

blocks.text: Bookworms, conservatives (保守派), military (军人或军事的) types — people are described with such terms. People have always tried to “type” each other. Actors in early Greek drama wore masks to show the audience whether they played the villain’s or the hero’s role. In fact, the words “person” and “personality” come from the Latin persona, meaning “mask”. Today, most television and movie actors do not wear masks. But we can easily tell the “good guys” from the “bad guys” because the two types differ in appearance as well as in actions.
blocks.translation: 书虫、保守派、军人型——人们用这类词相互描述。人总是试图给彼此“归类”。早期希腊戏剧中的演员戴面具，让观众看出他们演的是反派还是英雄。事实上，“person”和“personality”这两个词都来自拉丁语 persona，意为“面具”。如今大多数影视演员不再戴面具，但我们仍能轻易分辨“好人”和“坏人”，因为这两类人不仅行为不同，外表也不同。

articles.title: The $11 billion self-help industry is built on the idea that you should turn negative thou
articles.fallbackTitle: The $11 billion self-help industry is built on the idea that you should turn negative thou

blocks.text: The $11 billion self-help industry is built on the idea that you should turn negative thoughts like “I never do anything right” into positive ones like “I can succeed.” But was positive thinking advocate Norman Vincent Peale right? Is there power in positive thinking?
blocks.translation: 这个价值 110 亿美元的自助产业建立在一个观念上：你应当把“我什么事都做不好”这类消极想法转变成“我能成功”这类积极想法。但积极思维的倡导者诺曼·文森特·皮尔说得对吗？积极思维真的有力量吗？

blocks.text: Researchers in Canada just published a study in the journal Psychological Science that says trying to get people to think more positively can actually have the opposite effect: it can simply highlight how unhappy they are.
blocks.translation: 加拿大的研究人员刚在《心理科学》杂志上发表了一项研究，指出试图让人们更积极地思考，实际上可能产生相反效果：它只会让人更清楚地看到自己有多不快乐。

blocks.text: The study’s authors, Joanne Wood and John Lee of the University of Waterloo and Elaine Perunovic of the University of New Brunswick, begin by citing (引证) older research showing that when people get feedback which they believe is overly positive, they actually feel worse, not better. If you tell your friend who is slow to learn that he has the potential of an Einstein, you’re just underlining his faults. In one 1990s experiment, a team including psychologist Joel Cooper of Princeton asked participants to write essays opposing funding for the disabled. When the essayists were later praised for their sympathy, they felt even worse about what they had written.
blocks.translation: 该研究的作者——滑铁卢大学的乔安妮·伍德、约翰·李和新不伦瑞克大学的伊莱恩·佩鲁诺维奇——首先引用了较早的研究：当人们收到自认为过于正面的反馈时，他们实际上感觉更糟，而不是更好。如果你对一个学得慢的朋友说他有一爱因斯坦的潜力，你只是在强调他的缺陷。在 20 世纪 90 年代的一项实验中，包括普林斯顿大学心理学家乔尔·库珀在内的团队让参与者写文章反对资助残疾人。后来当这些作者因富有同情心而受到表扬时，他们对自己所写的内容感觉更糟。

blocks.text: In this experiment, Wood, Lee and Perunovic measured 68 students’ self-esteem. The participants were then asked to write down their thoughts and feelings for four minutes. Every 15 seconds, one group of students heard a bell. When it rang, they were supposed to tell themselves, “I am lovable.”
blocks.translation: 在这项实验中，伍德、李和佩鲁诺维奇测量了 68 名学生的自尊。然后要求参与者在四分钟内写下自己的想法和感受。每 15 秒，一组学生会听到一声铃响。铃响时，他们应当对自己说：“我是可爱的。”

blocks.text: Those with low self-esteem didn’t feel better after the forced self-affirmation (自我肯定). In fact, their moods turned significantly darker than those of members of the control group, who weren’t urged to think of positive thoughts.
blocks.translation: 自尊心低的人在被迫自我肯定之后并没有感觉更好。事实上，他们的情绪比对照组明显更低落，而对照组并没有被要求想积极的事情。

blocks.text: The paper provides support for newer forms of psychotherapy (心理治疗) that urge people to accept their negative thoughts and feelings rather than fight them. In the fighting, we not only often fail but can make things worse. Meditation (静思) techniques, in contrast, can teach people to put their shortcomings into a larger, more realistic viewpoint. Call it the power of negative thinking.
blocks.translation: 这篇论文为较新的心理治疗形式提供了支持，这些疗法鼓励人们接纳自己的消极想法和感受，而不是与之对抗。在对抗中，我们不仅常常失败，还可能把事情弄得更糟。相比之下，静思技巧可以教人把自身缺点放进一个更大、更现实的视角中。不妨称之为消极思维的力量。

paragraphs: The $11 billion self-help industry is built on the idea that you should turn negative thoughts like “I never do anything right” into positive ones like “I can succeed.” But was positive thinking advocate Norman Vincent Peale right? Is there power in positive thinking?

Researchers in Canada just published a study in the journal Psychological Science that says trying to get people to think more positively can actually have the opposite effect: it can simply highlight how unhappy they are.

The study’s authors, Joanne Wood and John Lee of the University of Waterloo and Elaine Perunovic of the University of New Brunswick, begin by citing (引证) older research showing that when people get feedback which they believe is overly positive, they actually feel worse, not better. If you tell your friend who is slow to learn that he has the potential of an Einstein, you’re just underlining his faults. In one 1990s experiment, a team including psychologist Joel Cooper of Princeton asked participants to write essays opposing funding for the disabled. When the essayists were later praised for their sympathy, they felt even worse about what they had written.

In this experiment, Wood, Lee and Perunovic measured 68 students’ self-esteem. The participants were then asked to write down their thoughts and feelings for four minutes. Every 15 seconds, one group of students heard a bell. When it rang, they were supposed to tell themselves, “I am lovable.”

Those with low self-esteem didn’t feel better after the forced self-affirmation (自我肯定). In fact, their moods turned significantly darker than those of members of the control group, who weren’t urged to think of positive thoughts.

The paper provides support for newer forms of psychotherapy (心理治疗) that urge people to accept their negative thoughts and feelings rather than fight them. In the fighting, we not only often fail but can make things worse. Meditation (静思) techniques, in contrast, can teach people to put their shortcomings into a larger, more realistic viewpoint. Call it the power of negative thinking.

It is based on the concept of positive thinking.
It has yielded positive results.

questions.stem: What is the finding of the Canadian researchers?

The power of positive thinking is limited.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the last paragraph?

该研究的作者——滑铁卢大学的乔安妮·伍德、约翰·李和新不伦瑞克大学的伊莱恩·佩鲁诺维奇——首先引用了较早的研究：当人们收到自认为过于正面的反馈时，他们实际上感觉更糟，而不是更好。如果你对一个学得慢的朋友说他有一爱因斯坦的潜力，你只是在强调他的缺陷。在 20 世纪 90 年代的一项实验中，包括普林斯顿大学心理学家乔尔·库珀在内的团队让参与者写文章反对资助残疾人。后来当这些作者因富有同情心而受到表扬时，他们对自己所写的内容感觉更糟。
在这项实验中，伍德、李和佩鲁诺维奇测量了 68 名学生的自尊。然后要求参与者在四分钟内写下自己的想法和感受。每 15 秒，一组学生会听到一声铃响。铃响时，他们应当对自己说：“我是可爱的。”
自尊心低的人在被迫自我肯定之后并没有感觉更好。事实上，他们的情绪比对照组明显更低落，而对照组并没有被要求想积极的事情。
这篇论文为较新的心理治疗形式提供了支持，这些疗法鼓励人们接纳自己的消极想法和感受，而不是与之对抗。在对抗中，我们不仅常常失败，还可能把事情弄得更糟。相比之下，静思技巧可以教人把自身缺点放进一个更大、更现实的视角中。不妨称之为消极思维的力量。

articles.title: Beware of those who use the truth to deceive
articles.fallbackTitle: Beware of those who use the truth to deceive

blocks.text: Beware of those who use the truth to deceive. When someone tells you something that is true, but leaves out important information that should be included, he can create a false impression.
blocks.translation: 当心那些用真相来欺骗的人。当某人告诉你一件真实的事，却省略了本应包含的重要信息时，他就能制造出虚假的印象。

blocks.text: For example, someone might say, “I just won a hundred dollars on the lottery. It was great. I took that dollar ticket back to the store and turned it in for one hundred dollars!”
blocks.translation: 例如，有人可能会说：“我刚中了一百美元彩票。太棒了。我把那张一美元的彩票拿回店里，换了一百美元！”

blocks.text: This guy’s a winner, right? Maybe, maybe not. We then discover that he bought two hundred tickets, and only one was a winner. He’s really a big loser!
blocks.translation: 这家伙是个赢家，对吧？也许是，也许不是。我们随后发现他买了两百张彩票，只有一张中奖。他其实是个大输家！

blocks.text: He didn’t say anything that was false, but he deliberately omitted important information. That’s called a half-truth. Half-truths are not technically lies, but they are just as dishonest.
blocks.translation: 他没有说任何假话，但故意省略了重要信息。这叫做半真半假。半真半假严格来说不是谎言，但同样不诚实。

blocks.text: Untrustworthy candidates in political campaigns often use this tactic. Let’s say that during Governor Smith’s last term, her state lost one million jobs and gained three million jobs. Then she seeks another term. One of her opponents ran an advertisement, saying “During Governor Smith’s term, the state lost one million jobs!” That’s true. However, an honest statement would have been, “During Governor Smith’s term, the state had a net gain of two million jobs.”
blocks.translation: 政治竞选中不可靠的候选人常用这种手法。假设史密斯州长上个任期内，本州失去了一百万个工作岗位，又增加了三百万个。然后她寻求连任。她的一位对手打广告说：“史密斯州长任期内，本州失去了一百万个工作岗位！”这是真的。然而，诚实的说法应是：“史密斯州长任期内，本州净增了两百万个工作岗位。”

blocks.text: Advertisers will sometimes use half-truths. It’s against the law to make false claims so they try to mislead you with the truth. An advertisement might boast, “Nine out of ten doctors recommend Yucky Pills to cure nose pimples.” It fails to mention that they only asked ten doctors and nine of them work for the Yucky Corporation.
blocks.translation: 广告商有时也会使用半真半假。做虚假宣传是违法的，所以他们试图用真相误导你。一则广告可能吹嘘：“十分之九的医生推荐 Yucky 药片治疗鼻痘。”它没有提到，他们只问了十位医生，其中九位为 Yucky 公司工作。

blocks.text: This kind of deception happens too often. It’s a sad fact of life: Lies are lies, and sometimes the truth can lie as well.
blocks.translation: 这种欺骗发生得太频繁了。这是生活中令人悲哀的事实：谎言就是谎言，而有时真相也会说谎。
