articles.heading: Step 1: Use open-ended questions
articles.title: Step 1: Use open-ended questions
articles.fallbackTitle: For a conversation to flow well, it’s important to ask open questions; these often start w

blocks.text: For a conversation to flow well, it’s important to ask open questions; these often start with “how”, “when”, “why”, etc. Try to avoid asking closed questions that can be answered with yes or no answers, because closed questions tend to kill the conversation.
blocks.translation: 要让对话顺畅进行，提出开放式问题很重要；这类问题常以“如何”“何时”“为什么”等开头。尽量避免问可以用是或否回答的封闭式问题，因为封闭式问题往往会扼杀对话。

blocks.text: Step 2: Listen actively
blocks.translation: 第 2 步：积极倾听

blocks.text: People speak at 100 to 175 words per minute, but they can listen intelligently at up to 300 words per minute. Since only a part of our mind is paying attention, it is easy to go into mind drift — thinking about other things while listening to someone. The cure for this is active listening, which involves listening with a purpose.
blocks.translation: 人们说话的速度是每分钟 100 到 175 个词，但我们可以每分钟听懂多达 300 个词。由于我们只动用了一部分注意力，很容易走神——在听别人说话时想着别的事情。解决办法是积极倾听，也就是有目的地听。

blocks.text: Step 3: Create a “cocoon”
blocks.translation: 第 3 步：营造一个“茧”

blocks.text: If you’re finding it particularly difficult to concentrate on what someone is saying, try to imagine a “cocoon” around you and the person you’re listening to. Imagine that the cocoon is blocking out all outside distractions（干扰）, so you can really focus on what they are saying.
blocks.translation: 如果你发现自己特别难以集中注意力听别人说话，试着想象一个“茧”把你自己和你正在听的人包围起来。想象这个茧挡住了所有外界干扰，这样你就能真正专注于对方说的话。

blocks.text: Step 4: Engage with the other person
blocks.translation: 第 4 步：与对方互动

blocks.text: When someone is trying to get your attention, or engage you in a conversation, don’t turn your back on them or answer over your shoulder. Instead, turn and face them, engage with them. Good communication is when you really engage. When you are talking to people, observe your body language and your tone of voice. Remember to use gestures, look people in the eye and smile when you talk unless you are complaining about something.
blocks.translation: 当有人想引起你的注意或让你参与对话时，不要背对着他们，也不要头也不回地应付。相反，要转过身面对他们，与他们互动。良好的沟通在于真正的投入。与人交谈时，注意你的肢体语言和语气。记住在说话时使用手势、看着对方的眼睛并微笑，除非你是在抱怨某事。

blocks.text: When we talk about intelligence we do not mean the ability to get good scores on certain kinds of tests or even the ability to do well in school. By intelligence we mean a way of living and behaving, especially in a new or upsetting situation. If we want to test intelligence, we need to find out how a person acts instead of how much he knows what to do.
blocks.translation: 我们谈智力时，指的不是在某些测试中取得好成绩的能力，甚至也不是在学校表现良好的能力。我们所说的智力，是一种生活和行为方式，尤其是在新的或令人不安的处境中。如果我们要测试智力，就需要了解一个人如何行动，而不是他懂多少该怎么做。

blocks.text: For instance, when in a new situation, an intelligent person thinks about the situation, not about himself or what might happen to him. He tries to find out all he can, and then he acts immediately and tries to do something about it. He probably isn't sure how it will all work out, but at least he tries. And, if he can't make things work out right, he doesn't feel ashamed that he failed; he just tries to learn from his mistakes. An intelligent person, even if he is very young, has a special outlook on life, a special feeling about life, and knows how he fits into it.
blocks.translation: 例如，面对新情况时，聪明的人思考的是这个处境，而不是他自己或他可能遭遇什么。他尽可能弄清情况，然后立即行动，设法做点什么。他也许不确定结果会怎样，但至少他去尝试了。而且，如果事情没能办好，他不会因失败而羞愧，只会努力从错误中学习。一个聪明的人，即使年纪很小，也对生活有独特的看法、独特的感受，并知道自己如何融入其中。

blocks.text: If you look at children, you'll see great difference between what we call "bright" children and "not-bright" children. They are actually two different kinds of people, not just the same kind with different amount of intelligence. For example, the bright child really wants to find out about life and he tries to get in touch with everything around him. But, the unintelligent child keeps more to himself and his own dream-world; he seems to have a wall between him and life in general.
blocks.translation: 如果你观察孩子，就会发现我们所说的“聪明”孩子和“不聪明”孩子之间差别很大。他们实际上是两种不同的人，而不只是智力多少不同的同一类人。比如，聪明的孩子真心想了解生活，努力与周围的一切建立联系。而不聪明的孩子更多地封闭在自己和幻想的世界里；他似乎与整个生活之间隔着一堵墙。

For instance, when in a new situation, an intelligent person thinks about the situation, not about himself or what might happen to him. He tries to find out all he can, and then he acts immediately and tries to do something about it. He probably isn't sure how it will all work out, but at least he tries. And, if he can't make things work out right, he doesn't feel ashamed that he failed; he just tries to learn from his mistakes. An intelligent person, even if he is very young, has a special outlook on life, a special feeling about life, and knows how he fits into it.

If you look at children, you'll see great difference between what we call "bright" children and "not-bright" children. They are actually two different kinds of people, not just the same kind with different amount of intelligence. articles.title: Impatience has been around for a long time

blocks.text: Impatience has been around for a long time. There is nothing new about people losing their patience while stuck in traffic or waiting in line. But some experts believe that people are less patient today than in the past.
blocks.translation: 急躁由来已久。人们堵车或排队时失去耐心，并不是什么新鲜事。但一些专家认为，如今的人比过去更没有耐心。

blocks.text: Some analysts suggest that in recent years many people are less patient because of technology. They suggest that "digital technology, from cellphones to e-mails to iPads, is changing our lives. The instant results we get from this technology have in turn increased our desire for instant satisfaction in other aspects of our lives."
blocks.translation: 一些分析人士认为，近年来许多人更没耐心是技术造成的。他们认为，“从手机到电子邮件再到 iPad，数字技术正在改变我们的生活。我们从这项技术中获得的即时结果，反过来又增强了我们在生活其他方面对即时满足的渴望。”

blocks.text: Psychologist Jennifer Hartstein makes some observations. She explains that "we have become an immediate satisfaction culture, and we expect things to move quickly, efficiently and in the way we want. When that doesn't happen, we tend to become increasingly frustrated and unsatisfied."
blocks.translation: 心理学家珍妮弗·哈特斯坦有一些观察。她解释说：“我们已经变成一种即时满足的文化，我们期待事情快速、高效、按我们想要的方式推进。当事情不是这样时，我们往往变得越来越沮丧、不满。”

blocks.text: Some believe that e-mail is losing popularity and could soon become outdated. Why? Because many people who send message do not have the patience to wait hours, or even minutes, for a response. Also with e-mails, as with letter writing, introductory and concluding greetings are often expected. But many people consider such formalities(客套) to be boring and time-consuming. They prefer instant messaging. Many people do not take the time to proofread what they put in writing. As a result, letters and e-mails contain numerous grammatical and spelling errors.
blocks.translation: 有些人认为电子邮件正在失去人气，可能很快过时。为什么？因为许多发消息的人没有耐心等上几小时甚至几分钟才得到回复。此外，电子邮件和写信一样，通常需要开头和结尾的问候。但许多人认为这些客套既无聊又费时。他们更喜欢即时通讯。许多人不花时间校对写下的内容。结果，信件和电子邮件里满是语法和拼写错误。

blocks.text: The thirst for immediate results is not limited to the digital communications. People seem to be losing their ability to wait in other areas of life. For instance, do you ever find yourself talking too fast, eating too fast, driving too fast, or spending money too fast? The few moments it takes to wait for an elevator to come, for a traffic light to change, or for a computer to start may seem like too long a time.
blocks.translation: 对即时结果的渴望不只限于数字通讯。人们在生活的其他方面似乎也在失去等待的能力。例如，你是否发现自己说话太快、吃饭太快、开车太快、花钱太快？等电梯、等红绿灯、等电脑启动的那几秒钟，似乎都显得太漫长。

blocks.text: Our minds may wander during boring tasks because daydreaming is actually the brain's normal state, rather than a pointless distraction, according to a new U.S. study.
blocks.translation: 根据美国一项新研究，我们在做无聊任务时走神，是因为白日梦实际上是大脑的正常状态，而不是毫无意义的干扰。

blocks.text: The researchers, reporting their findings today in the U.S. journal, Science, found that daydreaming could be the result of the brain thinking over important—but not immediately relevant—issues when the external environment ceases posing interesting and engaging problems.
blocks.translation: 研究人员今天在美国《科学》杂志上报告了研究结果。他们发现，当外部环境不再提出有趣、引人投入的问题时，白日梦可能是大脑在思考重要但并不紧急的问题的结果。

blocks.text: “For the most part psychologists have sort of assumed that we spend most of our time engaged in goal-directed thought and that, every so often, we have blips(光点) of irrelevant thoughts that pop up on the radar," said Malia Mason of Harvard University. "However, it could very well be the case that most of the time we are engaged in less directed, unintended thought and that this state is routinely interrupted by periods of goal-directed thought."
blocks.translation: “大多数情况下，心理学家多少假设我们大部分时间都在进行有目标的思考，只是偶尔会有一些不相关念头的光点出现在雷达上，”哈佛大学的玛莉亚·梅森说。“然而，很可能真实情况是，我们大部分时间都在进行指向性较弱、非刻意的思考，而这种状态经常被有目标的思考打断。”

blocks.text: Daydreaming or mind-wandering is more precisely defined as a state of mind where thoughts that are experienced by an individual are unrelated to what is going on in the environment around them, according to Mason. When wandering, the brain flits from one thought to the next, generating images, voices, thoughts and feelings.
blocks.translation: 据梅森说，白日梦或走神更准确的定义是：一个人所体验到的想法与周围环境中正在发生的事无关的一种心理状态。走神时，大脑从一个念头跳到另一个念头，产生图像、声音、想法和感受。

blocks.text: When deciding how best to encourage daydreaming in order to study it, the researchers recognized that our minds often wander while we are engaged in familiar tasks, such as making a sandwich, because we don't need to concentrate on it. They trained study subjects to become proficient on certain tasks so that their minds would be able to wander when they performed them, but would have to concentrate when given something new.
blocks.translation: 在决定如何最好地鼓励白日梦以便研究它时，研究人员意识到，我们常常在做熟悉的任务（比如做三明治）时走神，因为我们不需要专注于此。他们训练研究受试者熟练掌握某些任务，这样他们在执行这些任务时大脑能够走神，而在面对新任务时则必须集中注意力。

translations: 根据美国一项新研究，我们在做无聊任务时走神，是因为白日梦实际上是大脑的正常状态，而不是毫无意义的干扰。
研究人员今天在美国《科学》杂志上报告了研究结果。他们发现，当外部环境不再提出有趣、引人投入的问题时，白日梦可能是大脑在思考重要但并不紧急的问题的结果。
“大多数情况下，心理学家多少假设我们大部分时间都在进行有目标的思考，只是偶尔会有一些不相关念头的光点出现在雷达上，”哈佛大学的玛莉亚·梅森说。“然而，很可能真实情况是，我们大部分时间都在进行指向性较弱、非刻意的思考，而这种状态经常被有目标的思考打断。”
据梅森说，白日梦或走神更准确的定义是：一个人所体验到的想法与周围环境中正在发生的事无关的一种心理状态。走神时，大脑从一个念头跳到另一个念头，产生图像、声音、想法和感受。
在决定如何最好地鼓励白日梦以便研究它时，研究人员意识到，我们常常在做熟悉的任务（比如做三明治）时走神，因为我们不需要专注于此。他们训练研究受试者熟练掌握某些任务，这样他们在执行这些任务时大脑能够走神，而在面对新任务时则必须集中注意力。

articles.title: The faces of elderly, happily-married people sometimes resemble each other
articles.fallbackTitle: The faces of elderly, happily-married people sometimes resemble each other

blocks.text: The faces of elderly, happily-married people sometimes resemble each other. Dr. Aiken studied a number of couples who had been married for at least twenty-five years. Each couple provided four photographs—one photo of each partner at the time of their marriage and another photo of each partner twenty-five or more years later. All background was cut from the photos to remove any clues. The photos were then displayed in groups: a random grouping of the persons at the time of their marriage and another random grouping of the same persons who took photographs later. Some testees were asked to pick out the partners. They failed totally with the first group. Their judgments were no better than chance. But with the photos taken twenty-five or more years after the marriage, the testees were quite successful with the most happily-married couples.
blocks.translation: 上了年纪、婚姻幸福的夫妻，面孔有时会彼此相似。艾肯博士研究了许多结婚至少二十五年的夫妻。每对夫妻提供四张照片——一张是结婚时双方各自的照片，另一张是二十五年或更久之后双方各自的照片。所有照片的背景都被剪掉，以消除任何线索。然后照片被分组展示：一组随机排列结婚时的照片，另一组随机排列同一些人后来拍的照片。一些受试者被要求找出夫妻配对。面对第一组照片，他们完全失败，判断并不比瞎猜强。但面对结婚二十五年或更久之后拍的照片，受试者在最幸福的夫妻身上相当成功。

blocks.text: Dr. Aiken believes there are several reasons why couples grow alike. One reason has something to do with imitation. One person tends to copy or do the same as someone else without knowing it. He says human begins to imitate the expressions of the faces of their loved ones. “Another possible reason,” he says, “is the common experience of the couples.” There is a tendency for people who have the same life experience to change their faces in similar ways. For example, if a couple have suffered from a lot of sad experiences, their faces are likely to change in a similar way.
blocks.translation: 艾肯博士认为夫妻越长越像有几个原因。一个原因与模仿有关。一个人会不自觉地照另一个人的样子做。他说，人开始模仿所爱之人面部表情。“另一个可能的原因，”他说，“是夫妻的共同经历。”有相同生活经历的人，面孔往往会以相似的方式改变。例如，如果一对夫妻经历了许多悲伤的事，他们的面容很可能以相似的方式变化。

articles.title: Why do we laugh
articles.fallbackTitle: Why do we laugh

blocks.text: Why do we laugh? For years scientists have asked themselves this question. No animals laugh and smile—only human beings do. So does laughing help us to live longer? The answer seems to lie in that smiling and laughing help us to become less worried and calm, preventing illnesses that are caused by stress. Laughing is really the best medicine.
blocks.translation: 我们为什么笑？多年来科学家一直在问自己这个问题。没有动物会笑和微笑——只有人类会。那么笑能帮助我们活得更久吗？答案似乎在于，微笑和大笑帮助我们减少忧虑、平静下来，预防由压力引起的疾病。笑确实是最好的药。

blocks.text: But if you're unhappy, it can't do you any good to smile, can it? That's not true. It is clear that smiling works just in the same way whether you feel like smiling or not. Scientists in California asked a group of students to act five different feelings: happiness, sadness, anger, surprise and fear—just using their faces. Changes in their heart rate, blood pressure and temperature were recorded. Most of the feelings they acted didn't cause changes, but when the students smiled, their heart rate and their blood pressure went down. That happened even though they were only acting! So even if we feel sad inside, smiling seems to make us feel better.
blocks.translation: 但如果你不快乐，微笑对你不可能有好处，不是吗？事实并非如此。很明显，无论你想不想笑，微笑都以同样的方式起作用。加利福尼亚的科学家让一组学生用面部表演五种不同情绪：快乐、悲伤、愤怒、惊讶和恐惧。他们记录了学生心率、血压和体温的变化。他们表演的大多数情绪并未引起变化，但当学生微笑时，他们的心率和血压下降了。即使他们只是在表演！所以即使内心悲伤，微笑似乎也能让我们感觉好一些。

blocks.text: Now, what makes us laugh? It seems that the answer to the question is far from simple. Everyone likes jokes, but we don't laugh at the same ones. It depends largely on how old we are. There are some jokes, for example, that children love but older people might not find funny.
blocks.translation: 那么，是什么让我们发笑？这个问题的答案似乎远非简单。每个人都喜欢笑话，但我们不会对同样的笑话发笑。这在很大程度上取决于我们的年龄。例如，有些笑话孩子很喜欢，年纪大的人却可能不觉得好笑。

articles.title: Blind people can “see” things by using other parts of their bodies
articles.fallbackTitle: Blind people can “see” things by using other parts of their bodies

blocks.text: Blind people can “see” things by using other parts of their bodies. This fact may help us to understand our feelings about color. If blind people can sense color differences, then perhaps we, too, are affected by color unconsciously (无意识地).
blocks.translation: 盲人能用身体的其他部位“看见”东西。这一事实或许有助于我们理解自己对颜色的感受。如果盲人能感知颜色的差异，那么也许我们也会无意识地受到颜色的影响。

blocks.text: Manufacturers (生产商) have discovered by experience that sugar sells badly in green wrappers, that blue foods are considered unpleasant, and that cosmetics (化妆品) should never be packaged in brown. These discoveries have grown into a branch of color psychology.
blocks.translation: 生产商凭经验发现，糖用绿色包装就卖得不好，蓝色食品被认为令人不快，化妆品绝不该用棕色包装。这些发现已发展成色彩心理学的一个分支。

blocks.text: Color psychology now finds application in everything from fashion to decoration. Some of our preferences are clearly psychological. Dark blue is the color of the night sky and therefore associated with calm, which yellow is a day color with associations of energy and incentive (刺激). For a primitive man, activity during the day meant hunting and attacking, while he soon saw red as the color of blood and anger and the heat that came with effort.
blocks.translation: 色彩心理学如今从时装到装饰都有应用。我们的一些偏好显然是心理因素造成的。深蓝色是夜空的颜色，因而与平静联系在一起；黄色是白天的颜色，让人联想到能量和刺激。对原始人来说，白天的活动意味着狩猎和攻击，而他很快把红色看作血、愤怒以及用力时伴随的热。

blocks.text: And green is associated with passive defense and self-protection.
blocks.translation: 而绿色则与消极防御和自我保护联系在一起。

blocks.text: Experiments have shown that colors, partly because of their psychological associations, also have a direct psychological effect. People exposed to bright red show an increase in breath, in heartbeat and in blood pressure; red is exciting. Similar exposure to pure blue has exactly the opposite effect; it is a calming color. Because of its exciting meaning, red is chosen as the signal for danger, but closer analysis shows that a vivid yellow can produce a more basic state of alarm. So fire engines and ambulances in some advanced communities are now rushing around in bright yellow colors that stop the traffic dead.
blocks.translation: 实验表明，颜色部分由于心理联想，也会产生直接的心理影响。接触鲜红色的人呼吸、心跳和血压都会上升；红色令人兴奋。同样接触纯蓝色则产生完全相反的效果；蓝色是令人平静的颜色。由于红色的兴奋含义，它被选作危险的信号；但进一步分析表明，鲜艳的黄色能产生更基本的警觉状态。因此，一些发达社区的消防车和救护车如今闪着亮黄色疾驰，让交通戛然而止。

Manufacturers (生产商) have discovered by experience that sugar sells badly in green wrappers, that blue foods are considered unpleasant, and that cosmetics (化妆品) should never be packaged in brown. These discoveries have grown into a branch of color psychology.

Color psychology now finds application in everything from fashion to decoration. Some of our preferences are clearly psychological. Dark blue is the color of the night sky and therefore associated with calm, which yellow is a day color with associations of energy and incentive (刺激). For a primitive man, activity during the day meant hunting and attacking, while he soon saw red as the color of blood and anger and the heat that came with effort.
And green is associated with passive defense and self-protection.

Experiments have shown that colors, partly because of their psychological associations, also have a direct psychological effect. People exposed to bright red show an increase in breath, in heartbeat and in blood pressure; red is exciting. Similar exposure to pure blue has exactly the opposite effect; it is a calming color. Because of its exciting meaning, red is chosen as the signal for danger, but closer analysis shows that a vivid yellow can produce a more basic state of alarm. So fire engines and ambulances in some advanced communities are now rushing around in bright yellow colors that stop the traffic dead.

实验表明，颜色部分由于心理联想，也会产生直接的心理影响。接触鲜红色的人呼吸、心跳和血压都会上升；红色令人兴奋。同样接触纯蓝色则产生完全相反的效果；蓝色是令人平静的颜色。由于红色的兴奋含义，它被选作危险的信号；但进一步分析表明，鲜艳的黄色能产生更基本的警觉状态。因此，一些发达社区的消防车和救护车如今闪着亮黄色疾驰，让交通戛然而止。

blocks.text: People who multitask all the time may be the worst at doing two things at once, a new research suggests. The findings, based on performances and self-evaluation by about 275 college students, indicate that many people multitask not out of a desire to increase productivity, but because they are easily distracted (分心的) and can't focus on one activity. And "those people turn out to be the worst at handling different things," said David Sanbonmatsu, a psychologist at the University of Utah.
blocks.translation: 一项新研究表明，总是同时处理多项任务的人，可能最不擅长同时做两件事。这些基于约 275 名大学生表现和自我评估的发现表明，许多人同时处理多项任务并非出于提高效率的愿望，而是因为他们容易分心，无法专注于一项活动。“结果这些人在处理不同事情时表现最差，”犹他大学心理学家戴维·桑邦马祖说。

blocks.text: Sanbonmatsu and his colleagues gave the students a set of tests and asked them to report how often they multitasked, how good they thought they were at it, and how sensation-seeking (寻求刺激的) or impulsive (冲动的) they were. They then evaluated the participants' multitasking ability with a tricky mental task that required the students to do simple mathematical calculations while remembering a set of letters.
blocks.translation: 桑邦马祖和同事给学生做了一组测试，让他们报告自己多常同时处理多项任务、自认为做得有多好，以及他们有多追求刺激或冲动。然后，他们用一项棘手的脑力任务评估参与者的多任务能力，要求学生在记住一组字母的同时做简单数学计算。

blocks.text: Not surprisingly, the scientists said, most people thought they were better than average at multitasking, and those who thought they were better at it were more likely to report using a cellphone while driving or viewing multiple kinds of media at once. But those who frequently deal with many things at the same time were found to perform the worst at the actual multitasking test. They also were more likely to admit sensation-seeking and impulsive behavior, which connects with how easily people get bored and distracted.
blocks.translation: 科学家说，毫不意外，多数人认为自己多任务能力高于平均水平，而那些自认更擅长的人更可能报告自己边开车边用手机或同时浏览多种媒体。但在实际多任务测试中，频繁同时处理许多事情的人表现最差。他们也更可能承认有寻求刺激和冲动的行为，这与人们多容易感到无聊和分心有关。

blocks.text: "People multitask not because it's going to lead to greater productivity, but because they are distractible, and they get sucked into things that are not as important." Sanbonmatsu said.
blocks.translation: “人们同时处理多项任务，不是因为它能带来更高效率，而是因为他们容易分心，被不那么重要的事情吸引进去，”桑邦马祖说。

blocks.text: Adam Gazzaley, a researcher at the University of California, San Francisco, who was not a member of the research group, said one limitation of the study was that it couldn't find out whether people who start out less focused tend toward multitasking or whether people's recognizing and understanding abilities change as a result of multitasking.
blocks.translation: 加州大学旧金山分校研究员亚当·加扎利未参与该研究小组，他说这项研究的一个局限是无法确定，是一开始注意力较差的人倾向于多任务，还是人们的识别与理解能力因多任务而改变。

blocks.text: The findings do suggest, however, why the sensation-seeker who multitask the most may enjoy risky distracted driving. "People who are multitasking are generally less sensitive to risky situations." said Paul Atchley, another researcher not in the group. "This may partly explain why people go in for these situations even though they're dangerous."
blocks.translation: 不过，这些发现确实说明了为什么最爱寻求刺激的多任务者可能享受危险的分心驾驶。“同时处理多项任务的人一般对危险情境不太敏感，”另一位未参与该研究的研究者保罗·阿奇利说。“这可能部分解释了为什么人们会投身这些情境，即使它们很危险。”

paragraphs: People who multitask all the time may be the worst at doing two things at once, a new research suggests. The findings, based on performances and self-evaluation by about 275 college students, indicate that many people multitask not out of a desire to increase productivity, but because they are easily distracted (分心的) and can't focus on one activity. And "those people turn out to be the worst at handling different things," said David Sanbonmatsu, a psychologist at the University of Utah.

Sanbonmatsu and his colleagues gave the students a set of tests and asked them to report how often they multitasked, how good they thought they were at it, and how sensation-seeking (寻求刺激的) or impulsive (冲动的) they were. They then evaluated the participants' multitasking ability with a tricky mental task that required the students to do simple mathematical calculations while remembering a set of letters.

Not surprisingly, the scientists said, most people thought they were better than average at multitasking, and those who thought they were better at it were more likely to report using a cellphone while driving or viewing multiple kinds of media at once. But those who frequently deal with many things at the same time were found to perform the worst at the actual multitasking test. They also were more likely to admit sensation-seeking and impulsive behavior, which connects with how easily people get bored and distracted.
"People multitask not because it's going to lead to greater productivity, but because they are distractible, and they get sucked into things that are not as important." Sanbonmatsu said.

Adam Gazzaley, a researcher at the University of California, San Francisco, who was not a member of the research group, said one limitation of the study was that it couldn't find out whether people who start out less focused tend toward multitasking or whether people's recognizing and understanding abilities change as a result of multitasking.

The findings do suggest, however, why the sensation-seeker who multitask the most may enjoy risky distracted driving. "People who are multitasking are generally less sensitive to risky situations." said Paul Atchley, another researcher not in the group. "This may partly explain why people go in for these situations even though they're dangerous."

articles.title: When something goes wrong, it can be very satisfying to say, “Well, it’s so-and-so’s fault
articles.fallbackTitle: When something goes wrong, it can be very satisfying to say, “Well, it’s so-and-so’s fault

blocks.text: When something goes wrong, it can be very satisfying to say, “Well, it’s so-and-so’s fault.” or “I know I’m late, but it’s not my fault; the car broke down.” It is probably not your fault, but once you form the habit of blaming somebody or something else for a bad situation, you are a loser. You have no power and could do nothing that helps change the situation. However, you can have great power over what happens to you if you stop focusing on whom to blame and start focusing on how to remedy the situation. This is the winner’s key to success.
blocks.translation: 当事情出错时，说“嗯，这是某某的错”或“我知道我迟到了，但这不是我的错，车坏了”，会让人很满足。这也许确实不是你的错，但一旦你养成把糟糕处境归咎于某人或某事的习惯，你就是个失败者。你没有力量，也做不了任何有助于改变处境的事。然而，如果你不再专注于该怪谁，而开始专注于如何补救局面，你就能对自己身上发生的事拥有巨大的力量。这就是赢家成功的关键。

blocks.text: Winners are great at overcoming problems. For example, if you were late because your car broke down, maybe you have your car examined. Or, you might start to carry along with you the useful phone numbers, so you could call for help when in need. For another example, if your colleague causes you problems on the job for lack of responsibility or ability, find ways of dealing with his irresponsibility or inability rather than simply blame the person. Ask to work with a different person, or don’t rely on this person. You should accept that the person is not reliable and find creative ways to work successfully regardless of how your colleague fails to do his job well.
blocks.translation: 赢家非常善于克服问题。例如，如果你因为车坏了而迟到，也许你会去检查车子。或者，你可能会随身带上一些有用的电话号码，以便需要时求助。再比如，如果同事因缺乏责任心或能力而给你带来问题，要想办法应对他的不负责任或无能，而不是简单地责怪他。请求与另一个人合作，或者不要依赖这个人。你应该接受这个人不可靠，并找到有创意的办法，无论同事多么不能把工作做好，你都能成功。

blocks.text: This is what being a winner is all about——creatively using your skills and talents so that you are successful no matter what happens. Winners don’t have fewer problems in their lives; they have just as many difficult situations to face as anybody else. They are just better at seeing those problems as challenges and opportunities to develop their own talents. So, stop focusing on “whose mistake it is.” Once you are confident about your power over bad situations, problems are just the steps on the road to success.
blocks.translation: 这就是做赢家的意义——创造性地运用你的技能和才干，无论发生什么都能成功。赢家生活中的问题并不比别人少；他们要面对的困难处境和别人一样多。他们只是更善于把这些问题看作挑战，看作发展自身才能的机会。所以，不要再专注于“这是谁的错”。一旦你对自己掌控糟糕处境的能力有了信心，问题就只是通往成功路上的台阶。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?

A Winner’s Problem
A Winner’s Opportunity
A Winner’s Achievement
questions.explanation: 全文揭示赢家与输家的根本差别：不推责、专注补救，这正是“赢家的秘诀”。
questions.evidence: This is the winner's key to success.

translations: 当事情出错时，说“嗯，这是某某的错”或“我知道我迟到了，但这不是我的错，车坏了”，会让人很满足。这也许确实不是你的错，但一旦你养成把糟糕处境归咎于某人或某事的习惯，你就是个失败者。你没有力量，也做不了任何有助于改变处境的事。然而，如果你不再专注于该怪谁，而开始专注于如何补救局面，你就能对自己身上发生的事拥有巨大的力量。这就是赢家成功的关键。
赢家非常善于克服问题。例如，如果你因为车坏了而迟到，也许你会去检查车子。或者，你可能会随身带上一些有用的电话号码，以便需要时求助。再比如，如果同事因缺乏责任心或能力而给你带来问题，要想办法应对他的不负责任或无能，而不是简单地责怪他。请求与另一个人合作，或者不要依赖这个人。你应该接受这个人不可靠，并找到有创意的办法，无论同事多么不能把工作做好，你都能成功。
这就是做赢家的意义——创造性地运用你的技能和才干，无论发生什么都能成功。赢家生活中的问题并不比别人少；他们要面对的困难处境和别人一样多。他们只是更善于把这些问题看作挑战，看作发展自身才能的机会。所以，不要再专注于“这是谁的错”。一旦你对自己掌控糟糕处境的能力有了信心，问题就只是通往成功路上的台阶。

blocks.text: Daniel Anderson, a famous psychologist, believes it’s important to distinguish television’s influences on children from those of the family. We tend to blame TV, he says, for problems it doesn’t really cause, overlooking our own roles in shaping children’s minds.
blocks.translation: 著名心理学家丹尼尔·安德森认为，有必要把电视对儿童的影响与家庭对儿童的影响区分开来。他说，我们往往把并非由电视造成的问题归咎于电视，却忽视了自己在塑造孩子心灵中的作用。

blocks.text: One traditional belief about television is that it reduces a child’s ability to think and to understand the world. While watching TV, children do not merely absorb words and images(影像). Instead, they learn both explicit and hidden meanings from what they see. Actually, children learn early the psychology of characters in TV shows. Furthermore, as many teachers agree, children understand far more when their parents watch TV with them, explaining new words and ideas. Yet, most parents use an educational program as a chance to sit their kids in front of the TV set and do something in another room.
blocks.translation: 关于电视的一种传统看法是，它会削弱孩子思考和理解世界的能力。但孩子看电视时并不只是吸收文字和图像，他们会从所见内容中学到显性和隐性的含义。事实上，孩子很早就学会了电视节目中人物的心理。此外，许多老师也认同，当父母陪着孩子看电视、解释新词和新观点时，孩子理解得更多。然而，大多数父母只是把教育节目当作把孩子放在电视机前的机会，自己则去另一个房间做事。

blocks.text: Another argument against television is that it replaces reading as a form of entertainment. But according to Anderson, the amount of time spent watching television is not related to reading ability. TV doesn’t take the place of reading for most children; it takes the place of similar sorts of recreation, such as listening to the radio and playing sports. Things like parents’ educational background have a stronger influence on a child’s reading. “A child’s reading ability is best predicted by how much a parent reads.” Anderson says.
blocks.translation: 另一种反对电视的观点是，它取代了阅读这种娱乐方式。但安德森认为，看电视的时间长短与阅读能力无关。对大多数孩子来说，电视并没有取代阅读，而是取代了听广播、做运动等类似的娱乐活动。父母的教育背景等因素对孩子阅读的影响更大。安德森说：“孩子阅读能力的最佳预测指标，是父母读多少书。”

blocks.text: Traditional wisdom also has believed that heavy television-watching lowers children’s IQ scores and affects their school performance. But here, too, Anderson notes that no studies have proved it. In fact, research suggests that it’s the other way around. “If you’re smart young, you’ll watch less TV when you’re older.” Anderson says. Yet, people of lower IQ tend to be lifelong television viewers.
blocks.translation: 传统观念还认为，长时间看电视会降低孩子的智商分数并影响学业表现。但安德森指出，同样没有研究能证明这一点。事实上，研究显示情况可能恰恰相反。安德森说：“如果你小时候聪明，长大后就会少看电视。”而智商较低的人往往一辈子都是电视观众。

blocks.text: For years, researchers have attempted to show that television is dangerous to children. However, by showing that television promotes none of the dangerous effects as conventionally (传统地) believed, Anderson suggests that television cannot be blamed without considering other influences.
blocks.translation: 多年来，研究人员一直试图证明电视对儿童有害。然而，安德森通过证明电视并不会产生人们传统上认为的那些危险影响，提示我们不能在不考虑其他影响因素的情况下把责任都推给电视。

paragraphs: Daniel Anderson, a famous psychologist, believes it’s important to distinguish television’s influences on children from those of the family. We tend to blame TV, he says, for problems it doesn’t really cause, overlooking our own roles in shaping children’s minds.

One traditional belief about television is that it reduces a child’s ability to think and to understand the world. While watching TV, children do not merely absorb words and images(影像). Instead, they learn both explicit and hidden meanings from what they see. Actually, children learn early the psychology of characters in TV shows. Furthermore, as many teachers agree, children understand far more when their parents watch TV with them, explaining new words and ideas. Yet, most parents use an educational program as a chance to sit their kids in front of the TV set and do something in another room.

Another argument against television is that it replaces reading as a form of entertainment. But according to Anderson, the amount of time spent watching television is not related to reading ability. TV doesn’t take the place of reading for most children; it takes the place of similar sorts of recreation, such as listening to the radio and playing sports. Things like parents’ educational background have a stronger influence on a child’s reading. “A child’s reading ability is best predicted by how much a parent reads.” Anderson says.

Traditional wisdom also has believed that heavy television-watching lowers children’s IQ scores and affects their school performance. But here, too, Anderson notes that no studies have proved it. In fact, research suggests that it’s the other way around. “If you’re smart young, you’ll watch less TV when you’re older.” Anderson says. Yet, people of lower IQ tend to be lifelong television viewers.

For years, researchers have attempted to show that television is dangerous to children. However, by showing that television promotes none of the dangerous effects as conventionally (传统地) believed, Anderson suggests that television cannot be blamed without considering other influences.

多年来，研究人员一直试图证明电视对儿童有害。然而，安德森通过证明电视并不会产生人们传统上认为的那些危险影响，提示我们不能在不考虑其他影响因素的情况下把责任都推给电视。

blocks.text: As any homemaker who has tried to keep order at the dinner table knows, there is far more to a family meal than food. Sociologist Michael Lewis has been studying 50 families to find out just how much more.
blocks.translation: 任何试图维持餐桌秩序的家庭主妇都知道，一顿家庭晚餐远不止食物那么简单。社会学家迈克尔·刘易斯研究了 50 个家庭，想弄清楚它究竟还包含什么。

blocks.text: Lewis and his co-workers carried out their study by videotaping (录像) the families while they ate ordinary meals in their own homes. They found that parents with small families talk actively with each other and their children. But as the number of children gets larger, conversation gives way to the parents’ efforts to control the loud noise they make. That can have an important effect on the children. “In general the more question-asking the parents do, the higher the children’s IQ scores, ” Lewis says, “And the more children there are, the less question-asking there is.”
blocks.translation: 刘易斯和同事在家庭成员于家中吃普通晚餐时进行录像。他们发现，孩子少的家庭中，父母会积极与彼此和孩子交谈。但随着孩子数量增加，交谈会让位于父母控制孩子大声喧闹的努力。这会对孩子产生重要影响。刘易斯说：“一般来说，父母提问越多，孩子的智商分数越高；而孩子越多，提问就越少。”

blocks.text: The study also provides an explanation for why middle children often seem to have a harder time in life than their siblings (兄弟姐妹). Lewis found that in families with three or four children, dinner conversation is likely to center on the oldest child, who has the most to talk about, and the youngest, who needs the most attention. “Middle children are invisible, ” says Lewis. “When you see someone get up from the table and walk around during dinner, chances are it’s the middle child.” There is, however, one thing that stops all conversation and prevents anyone from having attention: “When the TV is on”, Lewis says, “dinner is a non-event.”
blocks.translation: 这项研究也解释了为什么中间的孩子似乎比兄弟姐妹在生活中更艰难。刘易斯发现，在三四个孩子的家庭里，晚餐谈话往往围绕最年长的孩子（最有话可说）和最年幼的孩子（最需要关注）展开。刘易斯说：“中间的孩子是隐形的。如果你看到有人在吃饭时起身在桌边走动，那多半是中间的孩子。”不过，有一件事能终止所有谈话、让任何人都得不到关注：“电视一开，”刘易斯说，“晚餐就形同虚设。”

They found that parents with small families talk actively with each other and their children. That can have an important effect on the children. “In general the more question-asking the parents do, the higher the children’s IQ scores, ” Lewis says, “And the more children there are, the less question-asking there is.”

articles.title: From the very beginning of school we make books and reading a constant source of possible
articles.fallbackTitle: From the very beginning of school we make books and reading a constant source of possible

blocks.text: From the very beginning of school we make books and reading a constant source of possible failure and public shame. When children are little, we make them read aloud before the teacher and other children, so that we can be sure that they "know" all the words they are reading. This means that when they don’t know a word, they are going to make a mistake, right in front of everyone. After having taught fifth-grade classes for four years, I decided to try at all costs to rid them of their fear and dislike of books, and to get them to read more often and more adventurously.
blocks.translation: 从上学第一天起，我们就让书本和阅读成为可能的失败与当众羞辱的来源。孩子还小时，我们让他们在老师和别的孩子面前大声朗读，以确保他们“认识”所读的每个词。这意味着，一旦他们不认识某个词，就会在所有人面前犯错。教了四年五年级之后，我决定不惜一切代价消除他们对书本的恐惧和厌恶，让他们更经常、更勇敢地阅读。

blocks.text: One day soon after school had started, I said to them, "Now I’m going to say something about reading that you have probably never heard a teacher say before. I would like you to read a lot of books this year, but I want you to read them only for pleasure. If you understand enough of a book to enjoy it and want to go on reading it, that’s enough for me. Also I am not going to ask you what words mean."
blocks.translation: 开学不久的一天，我对他们说：“现在我要说一些关于阅读的话，你们可能从没听老师说过。我希望你们今年读很多书，但只为乐趣而读。如果你能读懂到享受一本书并想继续读下去，对我来说就够了。另外，我不会问你们单词是什么意思。”

blocks.text: The children sat stunned（惊呆）and silent. Was this a teacher talking? One girl, who had just come to us from a school where she had had a very hard time, looked at me steadily for a long time after I had finished. Then, still looking at me, she said slowly and seriously, "Mr. Holt, do you really mean that?" I said just as seriously, "I mean every word of it."
blocks.translation: 孩子们惊呆了，一言不发。这是一个老师在说话吗？一个刚从一所让她过得很艰难的学校转来的女孩，在我讲完后久久地凝视着我。然后，她仍看着我，缓慢而认真地说：“霍尔特先生，你真是这个意思吗？”我同样认真地回答：“我每个字都是认真的。”

blocks.text: During the spring she really astonished me. One day, she was reading Moby Dick! "Don’t you find parts of it rather difficult?" I asked. "Oh, sure, but I just skip over those parts and go on to the next good part," she answered.
blocks.translation: 那年春天，她真的让我吃惊。有一天，她正在读《白鲸》！“你不觉得有些部分很难吗？”我问。“哦，当然，但我跳过那些部分，直接读下一个精彩的部分。”她回答。

blocks.text: This is exactly what reading should be and in school so seldom is — an exciting, joyous adventure. Find something, dive into it, take the good parts, skip the bad parts, get what you can out of it, and go on to something else.
blocks.translation: 这正是阅读应有的样子，而学校里却很少如此——一场令人兴奋、充满欢乐的冒险。找到一本书，投入进去，取走精彩的部分，跳过糟糕的部分，尽可能从中汲取，然后再去读别的。

paragraphs: From the very beginning of school we make books and reading a constant source of possible failure and public shame. When children are little, we make them read aloud before the teacher and other children, so that we can be sure that they "know" all the words they are reading. This means that when they don’t know a word, they are going to make a mistake, right in front of everyone. After having taught fifth-grade classes for four years, I decided to try at all costs to rid them of their fear and dislike of books, and to get them to read more often and more adventurously.

One day soon after school had started, I said to them, "Now I’m going to say something about reading that you have probably never heard a teacher say before. I would like you to read a lot of books this year, but I want you to read them only for pleasure. If you understand enough of a book to enjoy it and want to go on reading it, that’s enough for me. Also I am not going to ask you what words mean."

The children sat stunned（惊呆）and silent. Was this a teacher talking? One girl, who had just come to us from a school where she had had a very hard time, looked at me steadily for a long time after I had finished. Then, still looking at me, she said slowly and seriously, "Mr. Holt, do you really mean that?" I said just as seriously, "I mean every word of it."

During the spring she really astonished me. One day, she was reading Moby Dick! "Don’t you find parts of it rather difficult?" I asked. "Oh, sure, but I just skip over those parts and go on to the next good part," she answered.

This is exactly what reading should be and in school so seldom is — an exciting, joyous adventure. Find something, dive into it, take the good parts, skip the bad parts, get what you can out of it, and go on to something else.

questions.stem: According to the passage, children’s fear and dislike of books may result from ______.
options: being made to read too much
reading little and thinking little
reading often and adventurously
being made to read aloud before others
questions.explanation: 第一段说孩子从小被要求当众大声朗读，一旦不认识单词就会在所有人面前出错，这种公开羞辱让他们害怕并讨厌书本。
questions.evidence: we make them read aloud before the teacher and other children

questions.stem: The teacher told the students to read ______.
options: for enjoyment
for knowledge

questions.explanation: 老师明确说“I want you to read them only for pleasure”，只要读懂到能享受并愿意继续读就够了，不考单词意思。
questions.evidence: I want you to read them only for pleasure.

questions.stem: Upon hearing the teacher’s talk, the children probably felt that ______.
options: it was too good to be true

questions.explanation: 孩子们“sat stunned and silent”，一个女孩还反复确认“Do you really mean that?”，说明他们觉得老师的话好得难以置信。
questions.evidence: The children sat stunned and silent.

questions.stem: From the teacher’s point of view, ______.
options: children cannot tell good parts from bad parts while reading
children should be left to decide what to read and how to read
reading is never a pleasant and inspiring experience in school
reading involves understanding every little piece of information
questions.explanation: 老师主张让孩子为乐趣阅读、跳过难懂部分、自己选择读什么和怎么读；她并不要求理解每个细节，也不认为阅读永远不快乐。
questions.evidence: skip over those parts and go on to the next good part

translations: 从上学第一天起，我们就让书本和阅读成为可能的失败与当众羞辱的来源。孩子还小时，我们让他们在老师和别的孩子面前大声朗读，以确保他们“认识”所读的每个词。这意味着，一旦他们不认识某个词，就会在所有人面前犯错。教了四年五年级之后，我决定不惜一切代价消除他们对书本的恐惧和厌恶，让他们更经常、更勇敢地阅读。
开学不久的一天，我对他们说：“现在我要说一些关于阅读的话，你们可能从没听老师说过。我希望你们今年读很多书，但只为乐趣而读。如果你能读懂到享受一本书并想继续读下去，对我来说就够了。另外，我不会问你们单词是什么意思。”
孩子们惊呆了，一言不发。这是一个老师在说话吗？一个刚从一所让她过得很艰难的学校转来的女孩，在我讲完后久久地凝视着我。然后，她仍看着我，缓慢而认真地说：“霍尔特先生，你真是这个意思吗？”我同样认真地回答：“我每个字都是认真的。”
那年春天，她真的让我吃惊。有一天，她正在读《白鲸》！“你不觉得有些部分很难吗？”我问。“哦，当然，但我跳过那些部分，直接读下一个精彩的部分。”她回答。
这正是阅读应有的样子，而学校里却很少如此——一场令人兴奋、充满欢乐的冒险。找到一本书，投入进去，取走精彩的部分，跳过糟糕的部分，尽可能从中汲取，然后再去读别的。

articles.title: Ideas about education are changing in the United States
articles.fallbackTitle: Ideas about education are changing in the United States

blocks.text: Ideas about education are changing in the United States. Education today is not just a high school diploma or a college degree. Many adults are not interested in going to college. They are interested in other kinds of learning. For them, learning does not end with a diploma.
blocks.translation: 在美国，关于教育的观念正在发生变化。今天的教育不只是一张高中文凭或大学学位。许多成年人对上大学不感兴趣，他们感兴趣的是其他种类的学习。对他们来说，学习并不会随着拿到文凭而结束。

blocks.text: Continuing education gives these adults the opportunity to increase their knowledge about their own field or to learn about a new field. It also gives them a chance to improve their old skills or to learn new ones.
blocks.translation: 继续教育让这些成年人有机会增进本领域的知识，或学习一个新的领域。它也给他们机会提高旧技能或学习新技能。

blocks.text: Scientists, mechanics and barbers can take classes to improve their work skills. If they know more or learn more, they can get a better job or earn more money.
blocks.translation: 科学家、机械师和理发师都可以上课来提高工作技能。如果他们懂得更多、学得更多，就能得到更好的工作或挣更多的钱。

blocks.text: Continuing education classes give more adults the chances to learn new skills. There is usually a large variety of classes to choose from: typing, foreign cooking, photography, auto repair, furniture repair, or swimming. These are only some of the classes available.
blocks.translation: 继续教育课程让更多成年人有机会学习新技能。通常有各种各样的课程可供选择：打字、外国烹饪、摄影、汽车修理、家具修理或游泳。这些只是可选课程中的一部分。

blocks.text: Some adults take classes for fun or because the class will be useful for them. Other adults take continuing education classes to improve their own lives because they want to feel better about themselves.
blocks.translation: 有些成年人上课是为了好玩，或因为课程对他们有用。另一些成年人参加继续教育课程是为了改善自己的生活，因为他们想对自己感觉更好。

blocks.text: Almost any community college or public school system has a continuing education program. There are classes in schools, community buildings or churches. Most classes are in the evening, so working people can attend. The classes are usually small, and they are inexpensive.
blocks.translation: 几乎任何社区学院或公立学校系统都有继续教育项目。课程设在学校、社区活动中心或教堂里。大多数课程在晚上进行，以便上班族参加。班级通常很小，费用也不高。

paragraphs: Ideas about education are changing in the United States. Education today is not just a high school diploma or a college degree. Many adults are not interested in going to college. They are interested in other kinds of learning. For them, learning does not end with a diploma.

Continuing education gives these adults the opportunity to increase their knowledge about their own field or to learn about a new field. It also gives them a chance to improve their old skills or to learn new ones.

Continuing education classes give more adults the chances to learn new skills. There is usually a large variety of classes to choose from: typing, foreign cooking, photography, auto repair, furniture repair, or swimming. These are only some of the classes available.

Some adults take classes for fun or because the class will be useful for them. Other adults take continuing education classes to improve their own lives because they want to feel better about themselves.

Almost any community college or public school system has a continuing education program. There are classes in schools, community buildings or churches. Most classes are in the evening, so working people can attend. The classes are usually small, and they are inexpensive.

questions.stem: The new idea about education in the U.S. is that ______.

questions.stem: What’s the purpose for adults to continue their education?

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is true?

articles.title: If we take a close look at successful language learners, we may discover a few techniques
articles.fallbackTitle: If we take a close look at successful language learners, we may discover a few techniques

blocks.text: If we take a close look at successful language learners, we may discover a few techniques which make language learning easier for them.
blocks.translation: 如果我们仔细观察成功的语言学习者，可能会发现一些让语言学习对他们来说更容易的技巧。

blocks.text: First of all, successful language learners are independent learners. They do not depend on books or teachers; they discover their own way to learn the language. Instead of waiting for the teacher to explain everything, they try to find the patterns and the rules for themselves. They are good guessers who look for clues and form their own conclusions.
blocks.translation: 首先，成功的语言学习者是独立的学习者。他们不依赖书本或老师，而是自己摸索学习语言的方法。他们不等老师解释一切，而是自己努力找出模式和规则。他们善于猜测，会寻找线索并形成自己的结论。

blocks.text: Successful language learning is active learning. Therefore, successful learners do not wait for a chance to use the language; they look for such a chance. They find people who speak the language and ask these people to correct them when they make a mistake. They will try anything to communicate. When communication is difficult, they can accept information that is neither exact nor complete. It is more important for them to learn to think in the language than to know the meaning of every word.
blocks.translation: 成功的语言学习是主动的学习。因此，成功的学习者不会等待使用语言的机会，而是主动寻找这样的机会。他们找到说这种语言的人，并请这些人在自己犯错时纠正自己。他们会尝试一切办法来交流。当交流困难时，他们能够接受既不精确也不完整的信息。对他们来说，学会用这种语言思考，比知道每个词的意思更重要。

blocks.text: Finally, successful language learners are learners with a purpose. They want to learn the language because they are interested in the language and the people who speak it. It is necessary for them to learn the language in order to communicate with these people and to learn from them.
blocks.translation: 最后，成功的语言学习者是有目的的学习者。他们想学这门语言，是因为他们对这门语言以及说这种语言的人感兴趣。为了与这些人交流并向他们学习，他们有必要学会这门语言。

paragraphs: If we take a close look at successful language learners, we may discover a few techniques which make language learning easier for them.

First of all, successful language learners are independent learners. They do not depend on books or teachers; they discover their own way to learn the language. Instead of waiting for the teacher to explain everything, they try to find the patterns and the rules for themselves. They are good guessers who look for clues and form their own conclusions.

Successful language learning is active learning. Therefore, successful learners do not wait for a chance to use the language; they look for such a chance. They find people who speak the language and ask these people to correct them when they make a mistake. They will try anything to communicate. When communication is difficult, they can accept information that is neither exact nor complete. It is more important for them to learn to think in the language than to know the meaning of every word.

Finally, successful language learners are learners with a purpose. They want to learn the language because they are interested in the language and the people who speak it. It is necessary for them to learn the language in order to communicate with these people and to learn from them.

首先，成功的语言学习者是独立的学习者。他们不依赖书本或老师，而是自己摸索学习语言的方法。他们不等老师解释一切，而是自己努力找出模式和规则。他们善于猜测，会寻找线索并形成自己的结论。
成功的语言学习是主动的学习。因此，成功的学习者不会等待使用语言的机会，而是主动寻找这样的机会。他们找到说这种语言的人，并请这些人在自己犯错时纠正自己。他们会尝试一切办法来交流。当交流困难时，他们能够接受既不精确也不完整的信息。对他们来说，学会用这种语言思考，比知道每个词的意思更重要。

articles.heading: How to Help Kids Grow
articles.title: How to Help Kids Grow
articles.fallbackTitle: All parents have sky-high hopes for their children

blocks.text: All parents have sky-high hopes for their children. We want them to be confident and content. What can parents do to help their kids grow up to lead happy and productive lives? Experts advise:
blocks.translation: 所有父母都对孩子抱有极高的期望。我们希望他们自信、满足。父母能做些什么来帮助孩子长大后过上快乐而富有成效的生活？专家建议：

blocks.text: Helping them find their talents. In order to succeed, children need to feel they’re good at something. So expose your children to as many interests as possible; then let them choose those they like best!
blocks.translation: 帮助他们发现自己的才能。为了成功，孩子需要感到自己擅长某件事。所以让孩子接触尽可能多的兴趣，然后让他们选择最喜欢的！

blocks.text: Applauding their accomplishments. A study found that students whose parents fussed over their abilities were far more likely to do well in school—and in life—than students whose parents didn’t show such support. So celebrate your kids’ achievements, no matter how small they are.
blocks.translation: 称赞他们的成就。一项研究发现，父母对孩子的能力大加赞赏的学生，在学校和生活中表现好的可能性远高于父母不这样支持的学生。所以，庆祝孩子的成就，无论多小。

blocks.text: Giving them responsibilities. Responsibilities help youngsters grow into mature and self-motivated adults. So assign your children household chores when they are young. Four-year-olds can pitch in by picking up their dirty clothes and helping to set the table.
blocks.translation: 给他们责任。责任帮助年轻人成长为成熟、有自我驱动力的成年人。所以趁孩子小的时候给他们分配家务。四岁的孩子可以帮忙捡起脏衣服、摆餐桌。

blocks.text: Letting them make decisions and mistakes. Making their own decisions increases a child’s self-control and boosts their self-esteem. And allowing kids to make wrong decisions—as long as doing so won’t harm them—helps kids learn from their mistakes.
blocks.translation: 让他们做决定、犯错误。自己做决定能增强孩子的自我控制、提升自尊。允许孩子做错误的决定——只要不会伤害他们——能帮助孩子从错误中学习。

blocks.text: Encouraging them to solve their own problems. As they grow, children need practice in communicating, standing up for themselves and compromising. One of the best places to learn these skills is at home. So the next time your child runs to you complaining that her brother picks on her, step back and let them work it out.
blocks.translation: 鼓励他们自己解决问题。随着成长，孩子需要在沟通、为自己争取和妥协方面得到练习。学习这些技能最好的地方之一就是家里。所以下次孩子跑来向你抱怨哥哥或姐姐欺负她时，退后一步，让他们自己解决。

paragraphs: All parents have sky-high hopes for their children. We want them to be confident and content. What can parents do to help their kids grow up to lead happy and productive lives? Experts advise:

questions.stem: What should parents do so that their children are likely to do well in school?
options: Have high expectations on them.
Appreciate their achievements.
Put great pressure on them.
Expand their range of interest.
questions.explanation: 研究显示，父母对孩子的能力大加赞赏的学生更可能在学校表现好，因此父母应称赞孩子的成就。
questions.evidence: students whose parents fussed over their abilities were far more likely to do well in school

questions.stem: What is the parents’ purpose to assign their children housework?
options: To spare some time to relax.
To relieve themselves.
To enhance children’s sense of responsibility.
To share the heavy housework.
questions.explanation: 分配家务的目的是让责任帮助孩子成长为成熟、有自我驱动力的成年人，即增强责任感。
questions.evidence: Responsibilities help youngsters grow into mature and self-motivated adults.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Parents should stand up for children whenever they are needed.

Parents should stay out of any conflict among children.
Parents should encourage children to communicate with each other.
questions.explanation: 专家建议孩子抱怨时家长退后一步，让他们自己解决，即鼓励孩子相互沟通、自行化解矛盾。
questions.evidence: step back and let them work it out

questions.stem: What should children do as advised by experts?

Be entitled to make family decisions.

Learn to make good decisions at an early age.
questions.explanation: 专家五条建议中明确有一条是鼓励孩子自己解决问题，C 与之一致。

blocks.text: Nationwide, only about three percent of early childhood teachers are male in the U.S.. Experts say this can have an impact on young children whose understanding of gender roles and identity are rapidly forming. Research has found that having access to diverse teachers is beneficial for children. For the youngest learners, it means they are more likely to get exposed to different varieties of play and communication. It also helps them develop healthy ideas around gender.
blocks.translation: 在全美范围内，美国只有约 3% 的幼儿教师是男性。专家说，这会影响那些性别角色与身份认知正在迅速形成的幼儿。研究发现，接触多元化的教师对孩子有益。对最小的学习者来说，这意味着他们更可能接触不同种类的游戏与交流方式。这也有助于他们形成健康的性别观念。

blocks.text: “In our world and our society, we have very specific stereotypes (模式化形象) of gender roles,” said Mindi Reich-Shapiro, an assistant professor in the teacher education department of the Borough of Manhattan Community College, and one of the authors of a recent study. “It’s important for children to see other possibilities and other paths they can take.”
blocks.translation: “在我们的世界和社会里，我们对性别角色有非常刻板的印象，”曼哈顿社区学院教师教育系助理教授、最近一项研究的作者之一明迪·赖希-夏皮罗说。“让孩子看到其他可能性、看到他们可以走的其他道路，这很重要。”

blocks.text: Despite mostly feeling supported by colleagues and family members, many of the male educators surveyed in the study reported facing social or cultural resistance in their careers as early education teachers. Some also reported that there were parents surprised or concerned that their child had a male teacher. And they had been advised by colleagues or other staff not to hug children.
blocks.translation: 尽管多数受访的男性教育工作者感到同事和家人支持自己，但他们在幼儿教育职业生涯中仍遭遇社会或文化上的阻力。一些人还提到，有家长对孩子的老师是男性感到惊讶或担忧。还有同事或其他员工建议他们不要拥抱孩子。

blocks.text: Reich-Shapiro and fellow researchers made several recommendations to increase male representation in the field. Low pay has long been acknowledged as a major issue in the early childhood field. Over 70% of male educators who said they intended to stay in the early education workforce noted an increased salary was a major motivating factor for them to commit to the career long-term. The report suggests paying all early childhood educators the way elementary school teachers are paid.
blocks.translation: 赖希-夏皮罗和其他研究者提出了几项建议，以增加该领域的男性比例。低薪长期以来被认为是幼儿教育领域的主要问题。超过 70% 表示打算留在幼儿教育行业的男性教育工作者指出，加薪是他们长期投身这一职业的主要动力。报告建议，让所有幼儿教育工作者获得与小学教师相同的薪酬。

blocks.text: Cities and programs should establish support groups for male early childhood educators and provide mentoring and professional development advice for male educators and their program leaders.

blocks.text: The authors also suggest that traditional recruitment approaches for early childhood educators “do not address the gender gap in the field.” They recommend providing young men opportunities to work with children through training and volunteer programs, targeting groups of men who are considering a career change, such as fathers.

blocks.text: Choosing a college requires that you ask yourself many questions. Who do you want to be? What do you want to do? Where do you want to go in life? How do you get there? Perhaps the best way to find those answers is to look at our college on Long Island.
blocks.translation: 选择大学需要你问自己许多问题。你想成为什么样的人？你想做什么？你想在人生中走向何方？你如何到达那里？也许找到这些答案的最好方法，是来看看我们这所位于长岛的大学。

blocks.text: Think about it. Private colleges on Long Island charge an average of $25, 000 a year on overall costs, an average total of $100, 000 over four years. Our college’s cost is just over $13, 000 or about $53, 000 over four years. That means, because of the investment of the State of New York in our public college, you pay nearly half what students at those private colleges pay. That’s the money you can use later for graduate school, travel, or whatever you choose.
blocks.translation: 想一想：长岛私立大学的总体费用平均每年 25,000 美元，四年平均总计 100,000 美元。而我们大学的费用仅略高于 13,000 美元，四年约 53,000 美元。这意味着，由于纽约州对我们这所公立大学的投入，你支付的费用几乎是那些私立大学学生的一半。这笔钱你以后可以用于读研究生、旅行或任何你选择的事情。

articles.title: There has been an ongoing debate on whether school uniforms should be completely abolished
articles.fallbackTitle: There has been an ongoing debate on whether school uniforms should be completely abolished

blocks.text: There has been an ongoing debate on whether school uniforms should be completely abolished in all schools, both private and public. Despite both pros and cons（赞同和反对意见）of any uniform, personally I stick to the idea that school uniforms should be introduced in all public and private schools.
blocks.translation: 关于是否应在所有学校（包括私立和公立学校）彻底废除校服，一直存在争论。尽管校服有利有弊，但我个人坚持认为，所有公立和私立学校都应引入校服。

blocks.text: There are certainly many factors that should be taken into account when discussing the issue of school uniforms. While most private schools already have established a particular school uniform to be worn at all times and by all students, public schools mostly remain more liberal and only have a more or less strict dress code. In public schools, some kids have parents with rather high incomes who can afford to buy fashionable and costly clothes for their kids. But there are also those teens who are forced to buy low-cost outfits at discount retail stores. If all students wear identical clothes, no one will be hurt by the comparison.
blocks.translation: 讨论校服问题时，当然有许多因素需要考虑。大多数私立学校已经规定所有学生在任何时候都必须穿某种特定的校服，而公立学校大多更为自由，只有或多或少严格的着装规定。在公立学校，有些孩子的父母收入相当高，能给孩子买时髦昂贵的衣服；但也有一些青少年不得不在折扣零售店购买廉价服装。如果所有学生都穿同样的衣服，就不会有人因攀比而受到伤害。

blocks.text: Another point to consider is, of course, the way teenagers try to express their feelings. If from an early age children get used to paying too much attention to the way people dress and look instead of enriching their inner being and acquiring new skills, we should expect a very materialistic（物质至上的）society in the nearest future. Wearing a uniform would help in having people pay more attention to one’s personality, rather than looks. The main idea is to help a child understand that they should develop their inner beauty and not get involved with bad company and false friends.
blocks.translation: 当然，另一点需要考虑的是青少年表达情感的方式。如果孩子从小就习惯于过分关注人们的穿着和外表，而不是充实内在、学习新技能，那么我们预计在不久的将来会看到一个非常物质至上的社会。穿校服有助于让人们更多关注一个人的品格，而不是外表。其核心思想是帮助孩子明白，他们应该发展内在美，不要与不良伙伴和虚假的朋友混在一起。

blocks.text: All in all, wearing school uniforms is a great solution to these arguments. What counts most is that school uniforms teach children a certain discipline — the qualities they will later in life make use of when they have to obey certain social norms and laws.
blocks.translation: 总而言之，穿校服是解决这些争论的好办法。最重要的是，校服教会孩子一定的纪律——这些品质在他们以后必须遵守社会规范和律法时会派上用场。

There are certainly many factors that should be taken into account when discussing the issue of school uniforms. While most private schools already have established a particular school uniform to be worn at all times and by all students, public schools mostly remain more liberal and only have a more or less strict dress code. In public schools, some kids have parents with rather high incomes who can afford to buy fashionable and costly clothes for their kids. But there are also those teens who are forced to buy low-cost outfits at discount retail stores. If all students wear identical clothes, no one will be hurt by the comparison.

Another point to consider is, of course, the way teenagers try to express their feelings. If from an early age children get used to paying too much attention to the way people dress and look instead of enriching their inner being and acquiring new skills, we should expect a very materialistic（物质至上的）society in the nearest future. Wearing a uniform would help in having people pay more attention to one’s personality, rather than looks. The main idea is to help a child understand that they should develop their inner beauty and not get involved with bad company and false friends.

All in all, wearing school uniforms is a great solution to these arguments. What counts most is that school uniforms teach children a certain discipline — the qualities they will later in life make use of when they have to obey certain social norms and laws.

translations: 关于是否应在所有学校（包括私立和公立学校）彻底废除校服，一直存在争论。尽管校服有利有弊，但我个人坚持认为，所有公立和私立学校都应引入校服。
讨论校服问题时，当然有许多因素需要考虑。大多数私立学校已经规定所有学生在任何时候都必须穿某种特定的校服，而公立学校大多更为自由，只有或多或少严格的着装规定。在公立学校，有些孩子的父母收入相当高，能给孩子买时髦昂贵的衣服；但也有一些青少年不得不在折扣零售店购买廉价服装。如果所有学生都穿同样的衣服，就不会有人因攀比而受到伤害。

blocks.text: The number of international students at colleges and universities in the United States has increased continually for the fifth year.

blocks.text: The Institute of International Education in New York released its annual “Open Doors” report this week. It says a record of more than 720, 000 students from other countries were studying in America during the last school year. The number was 5% higher than the year before and almost one-third higher than ten years ago.

blocks.text: There were big increases from China, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam, Iran and Venezuela. Almost 22% of international students were Chinese, with increases especially at the undergraduate level. Together, almost half of all international students came from China, India and South Korea.

blocks.text: Peggy Blumenthal at the institute says that Chinese students are now studying throughout the United States. blocks.text: More international students study in California than in any other state. For ten years in a row, the University of Southern California in Los Angeles led the country, with more than 8, 600 foreign students.

blocks.text: There is a measurable relation between how much a person learns and his attitude toward the subject to be learned. When faced with a difficult learning task, one path to success is to concentrate on the positive aspects of the subject matter. If a student has a boring teacher, one solution is to look for the positive aspects of completing the course, regardless of how boring the teacher happens to be. To accomplish this might require a private tutor or some independent reading, but with the right attitude, success is possible.
blocks.translation: 一个人学到多少，与他对待所学内容的态度之间存在着可测量的关系。面对困难的学习任务时，通往成功的一条路是专注于这门学科的积极方面。如果学生遇到一位枯燥的老师，一个解决办法是寻找完成这门课程的积极面，无论这位老师多么枯燥。做到这一点可能需要请家教或自主阅读，但只要有正确的态度，成功是可能的。

blocks.text: Over-achievers—students who do better than their test scores show—usually have a positive interest toward learning. They may learn some things more slowly, and they may make more efforts, but, to compensate(补偿), they are often better at applying what they have learned. As long as they do not have emotional problems, they are successful.
blocks.translation: 高成就者——表现优于其考试成绩所显示的学生——通常对学习有积极的兴趣。他们学某些东西可能更慢，也可能付出更多努力，但作为补偿，他们往往更善于运用所学。只要没有情绪问题，他们就是成功的。

blocks.text: Under-achievers—those who function below their ability shown by test scores—often tend to allow a few negative factors to affect them. Because of their negative attitudes, they sometimes become unfairly critical of teachers. They allow themselves to get bored when it is not necessary. In short, their attitudes often cause them to learn less than over-achievers.
blocks.translation: 低成就者——实际表现低于考试成绩所显示能力的人——往往让一些消极因素影响自己。由于态度消极，他们有时会对老师做出不公平的批评。他们让自己在不必要的时候感到厌倦。总之，他们的态度常常使他们学得比高成就者少。

blocks.text: If you learn to replace a negative attitude toward learning with something more positive, you are on the road to achieving almost any goal you desire. For example, if you realize a personal computer with a word processor would improve your performance, but have an attitude that keeps telling you that a computer is difficult to operate, you tend to make all kinds of excuses. In short, you resist making full use of a terrific tool, simply because your negative attitude prevents you from learning.
blocks.translation: 如果你学会用更积极的东西取代对学习的消极态度，你就走上了实现几乎任何目标的路。例如，如果你意识到装有文字处理软件的个人电脑能提升你的表现，却带着“电脑很难操作”的态度，你就会找各种借口。总之，你抗拒充分利用一件极好的工具，只是因为消极态度阻碍了你学习。

blocks.text: In the same way that a child must be able to move his arms and legs before he can learn to walk, the child must physiologically be capable of producing and experiencing particular emotions before these emotions can be modified through learning. Psychologists have found that there are two basic processes by which learning takes place. One kind of learning is called “classical conditioning”. This occurs when one event or stimulus is consistently paired with or followed by, a reward or punishment. It is through classical conditioning that a child learns to associates his mother’s face and voice with happiness and love, for he learns that this person provides food and comfort. Negative emotions are learned in a similar fashion.
blocks.translation: 正如孩子必须先能活动手臂和腿才能学会走路，孩子在生理上必须先能够产生和体验某些情绪，这些情绪才能通过学习被改变。心理学家发现，学习有两种基本过程。一种叫“经典条件作用”。当一个事件或刺激持续与奖励或惩罚配对或紧随其后时，就会发生这种学习。正是通过经典条件作用，孩子学会把母亲的面孔和声音与幸福和爱联系起来，因为他知道这个人提供食物和安慰。消极情绪也以类似方式习得。

blocks.text: The second kind of learning is called “operant conditioning”. This occurs when an individual learns to do things that produce rewards in his environment and learns not to do things that produce punishments. For example, if a mother always attends to her baby when he cries and cuddles him until he is quiet, she may teach him that if he cries he will get attention from mother. Thus, the baby will learn to increase his crying in order to have his mother more.
blocks.translation: 第二种学习叫“操作性条件作用”。当一个人学会做出在其环境中产生奖励的行为，并学会不做产生惩罚的行为时，就会发生这种学习。例如，如果一位母亲总是在婴儿哭闹时照料他、抱他直到他安静，她可能教会他：只要哭就能得到母亲的关注。于是，婴儿会学会哭得更多，以获得母亲更多的陪伴。

blocks.text: Every day, we grow and have new experiences. We constantly learn by reading, watching television, interacting with other people, and so forth. This learning affects our emotions. Why is it that we learn to like some people and dislike others? If a person is nice to us, cares about us, we learn to associate this person with positive feelings, such as joy, happiness, and friendliness. On the other hand, if a person is mean to us, does not care about us, and even deliberately does things to harm us, we learn to associate this person with negative feelings, such as unhappiness, discomfort, and anger.
blocks.translation: 每一天我们都在成长，都有新的经历。我们不断通过阅读、看电视、与人交往等方式学习。这种学习影响我们的情绪。为什么我们会喜欢某些人而不喜欢另一些人？如果一个人对我们好、关心我们，我们就会把这个人同喜悦、幸福、友好等积极情感联系起来。反之，如果一个人对我们刻薄、不关心我们，甚至故意做伤害我们的事，我们就会把这个人同不快、不适、愤怒等消极情感联系起来。

paragraphs: In the same way that a child must be able to move his arms and legs before he can learn to walk, the child must physiologically be capable of producing and experiencing particular emotions before these emotions can be modified through learning. Psychologists have found that there are two basic processes by which learning takes place. One kind of learning is called “classical conditioning”. This occurs when one event or stimulus is consistently paired with or followed by, a reward or punishment. It is through classical conditioning that a child learns to associates his mother’s face and voice with happiness and love, for he learns that this person provides food and comfort. Negative emotions are learned in a similar fashion.

The second kind of learning is called “operant conditioning”. This occurs when an individual learns to do things that produce rewards in his environment and learns not to do things that produce punishments. For example, if a mother always attends to her baby when he cries and cuddles him until he is quiet, she may teach him that if he cries he will get attention from mother. Thus, the baby will learn to increase his crying in order to have his mother more.

Every day, we grow and have new experiences. We constantly learn by reading, watching television, interacting with other people, and so forth. This learning affects our emotions. Why is it that we learn to like some people and dislike others? If a person is nice to us, cares about us, we learn to associate this person with positive feelings, such as joy, happiness, and friendliness. On the other hand, if a person is mean to us, does not care about us, and even deliberately does things to harm us, we learn to associate this person with negative feelings, such as unhappiness, discomfort, and anger.

blocks.text: Do you believe that only boys do well in science? Does it seem to you that girls have better vocabularies than boys? In your opinion, are boys better at building things? If your answer to each of those questions is “Yes”, you are right.
blocks.translation: 你相信只有男孩擅长科学吗？在你看来，女孩的词汇量比男孩大吗？你认为男孩更擅长动手建造东西吗？如果你对每个问题的回答都是“是”，那你说对了。

blocks.text: On the average, males score higher on tests that measure mathematical reasoning, mechanical ability, and problem-solving skills. Females show superior ability in tests measuring vocabulary, spelling, and memory.
blocks.translation: 平均而言，男性在测量数学推理、机械能力和解决问题的测试中得分更高。女性在测量词汇、拼写和记忆的测试中表现出更强的能力。

blocks.text: It is known that bones, muscles and nerves develop faster in baby girls. Usually, too, baby girls talk at an earlier age than boys do. Scientists think there is a physical reason for this. They believe that the nerve endings in the left side of the brain develop faster in girls than in boys. And it is this side of the brain that strongly influences an individual’s ability to use words, to spell, and to remember things.
blocks.translation: 众所周知，女婴的骨骼、肌肉和神经发育得更快。通常女婴也比男婴更早开口说话。科学家认为这有生理原因。他们认为女孩大脑左侧的神经末梢比男孩发育得更快。而正是大脑这一侧强烈影响着一个人使用词语、拼写和记忆事物的能力。

blocks.text: By the time they start to school, therefore, little girls have an advantage that boys do not have. Girls are physically more ready to remember facts, to spell, and to read. These, of course, are skills that are important in elementary school.
blocks.translation: 因此，到上学时，小女孩已经拥有男孩没有的优势。女孩在身体上更准备好记忆事实、拼写和阅读。当然，这些正是小学阶段重要的技能。

blocks.text: But what have the boys been doing in the years before starting school? They have been developing something called aggression. An aggressive person has courage and energy. He feels strong and independent. He is often the first one to start fight.
blocks.translation: 但男孩在入学前的那些年里都在做什么呢？他们一直在发展一种叫做“攻击性”的东西。有攻击性的人有勇气和精力。他感到自己强壮而独立。他常常是第一个动手打架的人。

paragraphs: Do you believe that only boys do well in science? Does it seem to you that girls have better vocabularies than boys? In your opinion, are boys better at building things? If your answer to each of those questions is “Yes”, you are right.

articles.title: Today, there is no such thing as a “typical” college student
articles.fallbackTitle: Today, there is no such thing as a “typical” college student

blocks.text: Today, there is no such thing as a “typical” college student. People of all ages are enrolled in colleges.
blocks.translation: 如今，已没有所谓“典型”的大学生。各个年龄段的人都在上大学。

blocks.text: Though the concept of college may be the same for all students, the stress and future goals are different. The college students most people think of usually range in age from 18 to 21, and are most often away from home for the first time. As a result, they now have choices and no parent to tell them what to do. They are responsible for their own lives, needing to learn to manage their time and find a job, while attending school. They enter this new world with the anticipation of freedom, fun and a good job after graduation.
blocks.translation: 尽管大学的概念对所有学生可能相同，但压力和未来目标却不同。大多数人想到的大学生通常年龄在 18 到 21 岁之间，而且往往是第一次离家。因此，他们现在有了选择，却没有父母告诉他们该怎么做。他们要为自己的生活负责，需要学会管理时间，并在上学的同时找工作。他们带着对自由、乐趣和毕业后找到好工作的期待进入这个新世界。

blocks.text: The new faces in the college are usually 30 years old or older, and are returning to school after several years away. They are starting their college education, after raising a family and now ready to do something for themselves. Their lives are considerably different from their younger classmates. They have been on their own for a while, and are concerned about family, responsibilities, work, and the adjustment of being back in school after some years. Most important to them are the hopes of a new career or a job promotion after they graduate.
blocks.translation: 校园里的新面孔通常是 30 岁或更大的人，在离开学校几年后重返校园。他们在养大一个家庭之后开始大学教育，现在准备为自己做点什么。他们的生活与年轻同学相当不同。他们已经独立生活了一段时间，关心家庭、责任、工作，以及多年后重返学校需要做出的调整。对他们最重要的是毕业后获得新职业或职位晋升的希望。

blocks.text: Though they may come to college for different reasons, the result is the same. It is their chance to make a better life for themselves or their families. As the younger generation is looking for freedom in their lives, those who are returning to school also see freedom. The same opportunities were not available 20 years ago.
blocks.translation: 尽管他们来上大学的原因可能不同，结果却是一样的。这是他们为自己或家人创造更好生活的机会。年轻一代在生活中寻找自由，而重返校园的人也同样看到了自由。二十年前并没有这样的机会。

blocks.text: So in our college and universities, there is a new sense of hope and dreams. Where once stood only the youth of our future, they are now joined by people of all ages who share the dreams of a better life.
blocks.translation: 因此，在我们的大学里，有一种新的希望与梦想。过去只有未来的青年站在这里，如今各个年龄段、怀着更好生活梦想的人也加入了他们。

They enter this new world with the anticipation of freedom, fun and a good job after graduation.

The new faces in the college are usually 30 years old or older, and are returning to school after several years away. They are starting their college education, after raising a family and now ready to do something for themselves. Their lives are considerably different from their younger classmates. They have been on their own for a while, and are concerned about family, responsibilities, work, and the adjustment of being back in school after some years. articles.title: In the United States elementary education begins at the age of six
articles.fallbackTitle: In the United States elementary education begins at the age of six

blocks.text: In the United States elementary education begins at the age of six. At this stage nearly all the teachers are women, mostly married. The atmosphere is usually very friendly, and the teachers have now accepted the idea that the important thing is to make the children happy and interested. The old authoritarian (要绝对服从的) methods of education were discredited (不被认可的) rather a long time ago—so much so that many people now think that they have gone too far in the direction of trying to make children happy and interested rather than giving them actual instruction.
blocks.translation: 在美国，小学教育从六岁开始。在这个阶段，几乎所有教师都是女性，大多已婚。氛围通常非常友好，教师们如今已接受这样的观念：重要的是让孩子快乐、有兴趣。旧的专制教育方法很久以前就被否定了——以至于许多人现在认为，在让孩子快乐、有兴趣这件事上走得太远，反而没有给孩子真正的知识传授。

blocks.text: The social education of young children tries to make them accept the idea that human beings in a society need to work together for their common good. So the emphasis is on cooperation rather than competition throughout most of this process. This may seem curious, in view of the fact that American society is highly competitive; however, the need for making people sociable in this sense has come to be regarded as one of the functions of education. Most Americans do grow up with competitive ideas, and obviously quite a few as criminals, but it is not fair to say that the educational system fails. It probably does succeed in making most people sociable and ready to help one another both in material ways and through kindness and friendliness.

paragraphs: In the United States elementary education begins at the age of six. At this stage nearly all the teachers are women, mostly married. The atmosphere is usually very friendly, and the teachers have now accepted the idea that the important thing is to make the children happy and interested. The old authoritarian (要绝对服从的) methods of education were discredited (不被认可的) rather a long time ago—so much so that many people now think that they have gone too far in the direction of trying to make children happy and interested rather than giving them actual instruction.

The social education of young children tries to make them accept the idea that human beings in a society need to work together for their common good. So the emphasis is on cooperation rather than competition throughout most of this process. This may seem curious, in view of the fact that American society is highly competitive; however, the need for making people sociable in this sense has come to be regarded as one of the functions of education. Most Americans do grow up with competitive ideas, and obviously quite a few as criminals, but it is not fair to say that the educational system fails. It probably does succeed in making most people sociable and ready to help one another both in material ways and through kindness and friendliness.

blocks.text: It seems obvious that you don’t give away your product for free but this is exactly what indie rock group The Crimea did earlier this year. The band’s reasoning goes like this: more people will download the free album than would pay for it. Therefore, more people will hear the Crimea’s music. These people will then pay money for concerts by the band and perhaps buy a T-shirt or other merchandise. If the band play regular concerts to crowds of 200 or 300 people they can make more money than they would from sales of CDs. There will always be some people who want something they can hold in their hands so they will release the CD into the shops too—but making money through sales of their music isn’t the top priority.
blocks.translation: 不免费赠送产品似乎是理所当然的，但这正是独立摇滚乐队 The Crimea 今年早些时候做的事。乐队的逻辑是：免费下载专辑的人会比付费购买的人多，因此会有更多人听到 The Crimea 的音乐。这些人随后会花钱看乐队演出，也许还会买 T 恤或其他周边。如果乐队定期为两三百人的观众演出，他们赚的钱会比卖 CD 更多。总有一些人想要能拿在手里的东西，所以他们也会把 CD 放进商店销售——但通过销售音乐赚钱并不是他们的首要目标。

blocks.text: The story illustrates the creative thinking going on in the music business in response to dramatic changes over the last few years in the way that people buy music. Sales of music digitally—to computer, MP3 players and mobile phones—reached nearly 52 billion dollars in 2006—an increase of almost 100% on the previous year. People are simply not buying CDs in the way they used to, and by the time they stop buying them entirely, the music industry wants to make sure they are buying music in another form.
blocks.translation: 这个故事说明了音乐行业正在进行的创造性思考，以应对过去几年人们购买音乐方式的剧烈变化。2006 年，数字音乐（面向电脑、MP3 播放器和手机）销售额达到近 520 亿美元，比上一年增长近 100%。人们就是不再像过去那样购买 CD 了；等到他们完全不买 CD 时，音乐行业希望确保他们正在以另一种形式购买音乐。

blocks.text: This trend looks set to continue so the big question for the music industry is whether they can successfully manage the move to being primarily a digital industry without profits falling to unacceptable levels.

blocks.text: There are both positive and negative signs. On the plus side, more and more people are buying music online. At present, teenagers buy a lot of music on mobile phones. blocks.text: The bad news for the record companies, however, is the opportunity to illegally download music. blocks.translation: 然而，对唱片公司来说，坏消息是非法下载音乐的机会。盗版——通常以廉价复制的 CD 形式出现——长期困扰音乐行业，但互联网让盗版者通过文件分享网站和大型盗版下载网站自由而广泛地传播。

blocks.text: In this situation there is a danger that bands may give away their music for free and promote it in the next few years, a very interesting thing to start observing in the music business.
blocks.translation: 在这种情况下，未来几年乐队可能会免费赠送音乐来宣传自己，这是音乐行业一个非常值得开始观察的现象。

paragraphs: It seems obvious that you don’t give away your product for free but this is exactly what indie rock group The Crimea did earlier this year. These people will then pay money for concerts by the band and perhaps buy a T-shirt or other merchandise. If the band play regular concerts to crowds of 200 or 300 people they can make more money than they would from sales of CDs. There will always be some people who want something they can hold in their hands so they will release the CD into the shops too—but making money through sales of their music isn’t the top priority.

The story illustrates the creative thinking going on in the music business in response to dramatic changes over the last few years in the way that people buy music. Sales of music digitally—to computer, MP3 players and mobile phones—reached nearly 52 billion dollars in 2006—an increase of almost 100% on the previous year. People are simply not buying CDs in the way they used to, and by the time they stop buying them entirely, the music industry wants to make sure they are buying music in another form.

This trend looks set to continue so the big question for the music industry is whether they can successfully manage the move to being primarily a digital industry without profits falling to unacceptable levels.

There are both positive and negative signs. On the plus side, more and more people are buying music online. At present, teenagers buy a lot of music on mobile phones.
