articles.fallbackTitle: In 1939 two brothers, Mac and Dick McDonald, started a drive-in restaurant in San Bernadin

blocks.text: In 1939 two brothers, Mac and Dick McDonald, started a drive-in restaurant in San Bernadino, California. They carefully chose a busy corner for their location. They had run their own businesses for years, first a theater, then a barbecue (烤肉) restaurant, then another drive-in. But in their new operation, they offered a new, shortened menu: French fries, hamburgers, and sodas. To this small selection they added one new concept: quick service, no waiters or waitresses, and no tips. Their hamburgers sold for fifteen cents. Cheese was another four cents. Their French fries and hamburgers had a remarkable uniformity, for the brothers had developed a strict routine for the preparation of their food, and they insisted on their cooks’ sticking to their routine. Their new drive-in became incredibly popular, particularly for lunch. People drove up by the hundreds during the busy noon time. The self-service restaurant was so popular that the brothers had allowed ten copies of their restaurant to be opened. They were content with this modest success until they met Ray Kroc.
blocks.translation: 1939 年，麦克和迪克·麦当劳两兄弟在加利福尼亚州圣贝纳迪诺开了一家汽车餐厅。他们精心挑选了一个繁忙的街角作为店址。他们经营自己的生意已有多年，先是一家剧院，然后是烤肉餐厅，再后来又是一家汽车餐厅。但在新的事业中，他们提供了一份新的、精简的菜单：炸薯条、汉堡包和汽水。在这个小小的选择之外，他们还加入了一个新理念：快速服务，没有服务员，也不收小费。他们的汉堡卖 15 美分，加奶酪再加 4 美分。他们的炸薯条和汉堡包有着惊人的一致性，因为兄弟俩为食物制作制定了严格的流程，并坚持让厨师严格遵守。他们的新汽车餐厅变得极其受欢迎，尤其是午餐时间。忙碌的中午，成百上千的人开车前来。这家自助餐厅如此受欢迎，以至于兄弟俩允许开设了十家分店。他们对这种小小的成功很满足，直到遇见了雷·克罗克。

blocks.text: Kroc was a salesman who met the McDonald brothers in 1954, when he was selling milk shake-mixing machines. He quickly saw the unique appeal of the brothers’ fast-food restaurants and bought the right to franchise（特许经营）other copies of their restaurants. The agreement struck included the right to duplicate the menu, the equipment, even their red and white buildings with the golden arches（拱门）.
blocks.translation: 克罗克是一名推销员，1954 年他在推销奶昔搅拌机时结识了麦当劳兄弟。他很快看出了兄弟俩快餐店的独特吸引力，并买下了特许经营其他分店的权利。双方达成的协议包括复制菜单、设备，甚至包括他们那带有金色拱门的红白建筑的权利。

blocks.text: Today McDonald’s is really a household name. Its names for its sandwiches have come to mean hamburger in the decades since the day Ray Kroc watched people rush up to order fifteen-cent hamburgers. In 1976, McDonald’s had over $1 billion in total sales. Its first twenty-two years is one of the most incredible success stories in modern American business history.
blocks.translation: 如今，麦当劳真的成了一个家喻户晓的名字。自从雷·克罗克看着人们蜂拥而来购买 15 美分汉堡的那天起，几十年间，麦当劳对其三明治的称呼已经成了汉堡包的代名词。1976 年，麦当劳的总销售额超过 10 亿美元。它最初的二十二年是现代美国商业史上最不可思议的成功故事之一。

paragraphs: In 1939 two brothers, Mac and Dick McDonald, started a drive-in restaurant in San Bernadino, California. They carefully chose a busy corner for their location. They had run their own businesses for years, first a theater, then a barbecue (烤肉) restaurant, then another drive-in. But in their new operation, they offered a new, shortened menu: French fries, hamburgers, and sodas. To this small selection they added one new concept: quick service, no waiters or waitresses, and no tips. Their hamburgers sold for fifteen cents. Cheese was another four cents. Their French fries and hamburgers had a remarkable uniformity, for the brothers had developed a strict routine for the preparation of their food, and they insisted on their cooks’ sticking to their routine. Their new drive-in became incredibly popular, particularly for lunch. People drove up by the hundreds during the busy noon time. The self-service restaurant was so popular that the brothers had allowed ten copies of their restaurant to be opened. They were content with this modest success until they met Ray Kroc.

Kroc was a salesman who met the McDonald brothers in 1954, when he was selling milk shake-mixing machines. He quickly saw the unique appeal of the brothers’ fast-food restaurants and bought the right to franchise（特许经营）other copies of their restaurants. The agreement struck included the right to duplicate the menu, the equipment, even their red and white buildings with the golden arches（拱门）.

In 1976, McDonald’s had over $1 billion in total sales. Its first twenty-two years is one of the most incredible success stories in modern American business history.

translations: 1939 年，麦克和迪克·麦当劳两兄弟在加利福尼亚州圣贝纳迪诺开了一家汽车餐厅。他们精心挑选了一个繁忙的街角作为店址。他们经营自己的生意已有多年，先是一家剧院，然后是烤肉餐厅，再后来又是一家汽车餐厅。但在新的事业中，他们提供了一份新的、精简的菜单：炸薯条、汉堡包和汽水。在这个小小的选择之外，他们还加入了一个新理念：快速服务，没有服务员，也不收小费。他们的汉堡卖 15 美分，加奶酪再加 4 美分。他们的炸薯条和汉堡包有着惊人的一致性，因为兄弟俩为食物制作制定了严格的流程，并坚持让厨师严格遵守。他们的新汽车餐厅变得极其受欢迎，尤其是午餐时间。忙碌的中午，成百上千的人开车前来。这家自助餐厅如此受欢迎，以至于兄弟俩允许开设了十家分店。他们对这种小小的成功很满足，直到遇见了雷·克罗克。
克罗克是一名推销员，1954 年他在推销奶昔搅拌机时结识了麦当劳兄弟。他很快看出了兄弟俩快餐店的独特吸引力，并买下了特许经营其他分店的权利。双方达成的协议包括复制菜单、设备，甚至包括他们那带有金色拱门的红白建筑的权利。
如今，麦当劳真的成了一个家喻户晓的名字。自从雷·克罗克看着人们蜂拥而来购买 15 美分汉堡的那天起，几十年间，麦当劳对其三明治的称呼已经成了汉堡包的代名词。1976 年，麦当劳的总销售额超过 10 亿美元。它最初的二十二年是现代美国商业史上最不可思议的成功故事之一。

blocks.text: When young people get their first real jobs, they face a lot of new and confusing situations. They may find that everything is different from the way things were at school. It is also possible that they will feel uncomfortable and insecure in both professional and social situations. Eventually, they realize that university classes can’t be the only preparation for all of the different situations that arise in the working world.
blocks.translation: 年轻人找到第一份真正的工作时，会面临许多新情况，令人困惑。他们可能会发现，一切都与学校里的情况不同。他们也可能会在职业场合和社交场合感到不自在、缺乏安全感。最终，他们意识到，大学课程不可能是为职场中出现的各种不同情况所做的唯一准备。

blocks.text: Perhaps the best way to learn how to behave in the working world is to identify a worker you admire and observe his behavior. By doing so, you will be able to see what it is that you admire in this person. For example, you will observe how he acts in a crisis. Perhaps even more importantly, you will be able to see what his approach to day-to-day situations is.
blocks.translation: 也许，学习如何在职场中行事的最好方法，是找一位你钦佩的同事，观察他的行为。这样做，你就能看清自己究竟钦佩这个人的什么。例如，你会观察他在危机中如何行事。也许更重要的是，你能看到他对日常情况采取什么方式。

blocks.text: While you are observing your colleague, you should be asking yourself whether his behavior is like yours and how you can learn from his responses to a variety of situations. By watching and learning from a model, you will probably begin to identify and adopt good working habits.
blocks.translation: 在观察同事的同时，你应该问自己：他的行为是否与你相似？你能如何从他应对各种情况的反应中学习？通过观察榜样并向其学习，你大概会开始识别并养成好的工作习惯。

paragraphs: When young people get their first real jobs, they face a lot of new and confusing situations. They may find that everything is different from the way things were at school. It is also possible that they will feel uncomfortable and insecure in both professional and social situations. Eventually, they realize that university classes can’t be the only preparation for all of the different situations that arise in the working world.

Perhaps the best way to learn how to behave in the working world is to identify a worker you admire and observe his behavior. By doing so, you will be able to see what it is that you admire in this person. For example, you will observe how he acts in a crisis. Perhaps even more importantly, you will be able to see what his approach to day-to-day situations is.

While you are observing your colleague, you should be asking yourself whether his behavior is like yours and how you can learn from his responses to a variety of situations. By watching and learning from a model, you will probably begin to identify and adopt good working habits.

blocks.text: Most American people hate repeating the same work endlessly, especially those who live in the west of America. They try their best to make their life colorful and their work interesting. If they have to do the same regular work, they’ll try to do it in different ways. Repetition and Monotony(单调) are what they can’t stand.
blocks.translation: 大多数美国人讨厌无休止地重复同样的工作，尤其是住在美国西部的人。他们尽力让自己的生活丰富多彩、工作充满乐趣。如果不得不做同样的常规工作，他们会尝试用不同的方式去做。重复和单调是他们无法忍受的。

blocks.text: In the west of America, there is a beautiful old mountain village which is well known for its straw hats. The villagers there can make different styles of hats — hats for old gentlemen, for sweet and playful children, and for beautiful young ladies. People often go there to buy hats.
blocks.translation: 在美国西部，有一个美丽的古老山村，以草帽闻名。那里的村民能制作不同款式的帽子——给老年绅士的、给可爱顽皮孩子的，还有给漂亮年轻女士的。人们常去那里买帽子。

blocks.text: One day, there came a young tourist who entered a millinery(女士帽子)shop and found a very nice hat costing five dollars. He said to the shopkeeper, “If you agree to sell at a cheaper price, I’d like to buy two hundred hats of this style.” “No, you should pay me at least ten dollars each if you wish to get so many hats of the same style.” The tourist could not understand.
blocks.translation: 一天，来了一位年轻游客，他走进一家女帽店，看中了一顶非常漂亮的帽子，售价五美元。他对店主说：“如果你同意便宜点卖，我想买两百顶这种款式的帽子。”“不，如果你想买这么多同款帽子，至少得每顶付我十美元。”游客不明白。

blocks.text: “How’s that?”
blocks.translation: “怎么会这样？”

blocks.text: “Well, ” said the shopkeeper, “If you buy only one hat of this style, I can make it easily. If you order two hundred hats of different styles, I can also manage the business without much difficulty. However, it will almost bore me to death if you want me to make two hundred hats of the same style. So you at least pay me double price.”
blocks.translation: “嗯，”店主说，“如果你只买一顶这种款式的帽子，我做起来很容易。如果你订两百顶不同款式的帽子，我也能不太费力地应付。可是，如果你要我做出两百顶一模一样的帽子，那几乎会把我烦死。所以你至少得付我双倍的价钱。”

In the west of America, there is a beautiful old mountain village which is well known for its straw hats. The villagers there can make different styles of hats — hats for old gentlemen, for sweet and playful children, and for beautiful young ladies. People often go there to buy hats.

He said to the shopkeeper, “If you agree to sell at a cheaper price, I’d like to buy two hundred hats of this style.” “No, you should pay me at least ten dollars each if you wish to get so many hats of the same style.” The tourist could not understand.

articles.title: It is exciting to apply for a job that really interests you
articles.fallbackTitle: It is exciting to apply for a job that really interests you

blocks.text: It is exciting to apply for a job that really interests you. In making your application, there are a number of points for you to observe.
blocks.translation: 申请一份你真正感兴趣的工作是令人兴奋的。在提出申请时，有几点需要注意。

blocks.text: In your letter of application, aim to say just enough to introduce yourself. If you are answering an advertisement, any information for which it asks must, of course, be given. This will usually cover your school record and any further education and training. You may also be asked to give the names of one or two persons to supply reference. For this purpose you should choose people who know enough about your character and ability; and you should also ask for their permission to be named as referees.
blocks.translation: 在求职信中，要力求恰到好处地介绍自己。如果你是在回应一则招聘广告，那么广告所要求的任何信息当然都必须提供。这通常包括你的在校成绩以及任何进一步的教育和培训经历。他们还可能要求你提供一两位证明人的姓名。为此，你应选择足够了解你品格和能力的人，并且应先征得他们同意，将其列为证明人。

blocks.text: It will depend on circumstances how much you can usefully add about yourself. Your purpose is to bring to the notice of the boss any good reason why you rather than any of the other applicants (申请人) should be chosen for the job. If you feel you have any special skill for the work or, for example, any particular interest in the line of the business, let this be known.
blocks.translation: 你能有效地补充多少关于自己的信息，要视情况而定。你的目的是让老板注意到你而非其他申请人、应当被选中担任这份工作的任何充分理由。如果你觉得自己在这项工作上有特殊技能，或者例如对这类行业有特别的兴趣，就应该让雇主知道。

blocks.text: Finally there is your use of language. You cannot go wrong if you keep your sentences and paragraphs short, making sure the sense is clear and well expressed. Choose plain words so long as they can express your meaning.
blocks.translation: 最后是语言的运用。只要你保持句子和段落简短，确保意思清楚、表达得体，就不会出错。只要能够表达你的意思，就选择朴实的词语。

paragraphs: It is exciting to apply for a job that really interests you. In making your application, there are a number of points for you to observe.

In your letter of application, aim to say just enough to introduce yourself. If you are answering an advertisement, any information for which it asks must, of course, be given. This will usually cover your school record and any further education and training. You may also be asked to give the names of one or two persons to supply reference. For this purpose you should choose people who know enough about your character and ability; and you should also ask for their permission to be named as referees.

It will depend on circumstances how much you can usefully add about yourself. Your purpose is to bring to the notice of the boss any good reason why you rather than any of the other applicants (申请人) should be chosen for the job. If you feel you have any special skill for the work or, for example, any particular interest in the line of the business, let this be known.

Finally there is your use of language. You cannot go wrong if you keep your sentences and paragraphs short, making sure the sense is clear and well expressed. Choose plain words so long as they can express your meaning.

articles.title: Most Americans switch careers at least three times throughout their lives
articles.fallbackTitle: Most Americans switch careers at least three times throughout their lives

blocks.text: Most Americans switch careers at least three times throughout their lives. Gone are the days when people retired from the company where they first worked. The progressive mentality (心态) regarding business and technology often ensures that people move from position to position as they try to find the right career for them.
blocks.translation: 大多数美国人一生中至少换三次职业。从第一份工作的公司退休的时代已经过去。关于商业和技术的进步心态，往往使人们在寻找适合自己的职业时不断从一个职位转向另一个职位。

blocks.text: Recent college graduates ask “what career is right for me?” many times in the months before and after graduation. Now more than ever, people are also asking “what career is right for me?” into their thirties, forties and fifties. Even baby boomers (生育高峰期出生的人) are asking “what job is right for me?” as they retire and reenter the workforce in their sixties and seventies. It seems that every employee in America is wondering which career path fits him or her best.
blocks.translation: 刚毕业的大学生在毕业前后几个月里会多次问“什么职业适合我？”。如今比以往任何时候都多的人，在三十多岁、四十多岁和五十多岁时也在问“什么职业适合我？”。甚至婴儿潮一代在六七十岁退休并重返职场时，也在问“什么工作适合我？”。似乎美国的每个雇员都在想哪条职业道路最适合自己。

blocks.text: When you find yourself asking “what career is best for me?”, follow some of these simple tips to set yourself straight on the best path for you.
blocks.translation: 当你发现自己问“什么职业最适合我？”时，遵循以下一些简单建议，让自己走上最适合的道路。

blocks.text: Consult a website and take its test to see which career path might be right for you.
blocks.translation: 咨询一个网站，做它的测试，看看哪条职业道路可能适合你。

blocks.text: Think about whether you are happy with your current job.
blocks.translation: 想想你对目前的工作是否满意。

blocks.text: Emphasize your skills in your resume.
blocks.translation: 在简历中突出你的技能。

blocks.text: Do more research about the new career.
blocks.translation: 对新职业做更多研究。

paragraphs: Most Americans switch careers at least three times throughout their lives. Gone are the days when people retired from the company where they first worked. The progressive mentality (心态) regarding business and technology often ensures that people move from position to position as they try to find the right career for them.

Recent college graduates ask “what career is right for me?” many times in the months before and after graduation. Now more than ever, people are also asking “what career is right for me?” into their thirties, forties and fifties. Even baby boomers (生育高峰期出生的人) are asking “what job is right for me?” as they retire and reenter the workforce in their sixties and seventies. It seems that every employee in America is wondering which career path fits him or her best.
When you find yourself asking “what career is best for me?”, follow some of these simple tips to set yourself straight on the best path for you.

刚毕业的大学生在毕业前后几个月里会多次问“什么职业适合我？”。如今比以往任何时候都多的人，在三十多岁、四十多岁和五十多岁时也在问“什么职业适合我？”。甚至婴儿潮一代在六七十岁退休并重返职场时，也在问“什么工作适合我？”。似乎美国的每个雇员都在想哪条职业道路最适合自己。

articles.title: I knew a man who was asked to be the new dean(院长) of the College of Business of a large un
articles.fallbackTitle: I knew a man who was asked to be the new dean(院长) of the College of Business of a large un

blocks.text: I knew a man who was asked to be the new dean(院长) of the College of Business of a large university. When he first arrived, he studied the situation the college faced and felt that what it needed most was money. He recognized that he had a unique capacity to raise money, and he developed a real sense of vision about fund-raising as his primary function.
blocks.translation: 我认识一个人，他被聘为一所大型大学商学院的新院长。刚到任时，他研究了学院面临的处境，认为学院最需要的是钱。他意识到自己有独特的筹款能力，并把筹款作为自己的首要职能，对此形成了清晰的愿景。

blocks.text: This created a problem in the college because past deans had focused mainly on meeting day-to-day faculty needs. This new dean was never there. He was running around the country trying to raise money for research. But he was not attending to the day-to-day things as the previous dean had. The faculty, who were used to working with the person at the top, had to work through his administrative assistant.
blocks.translation: 这在学院里造成了问题，因为历任院长主要关注满足教师的日常需求。这位新院长从不在办公室。他跑遍全国，努力为研究筹款。但他不像前任院长那样处理日常事务。习惯与最高负责人直接打交道的教师们，只能通过他的行政助理来办事。

blocks.text: The faculty became so upset with his absence that they sent a delegation to the president of the university to demand a new dean or a fundamental change in his leadership style. The president, who knew what the dean was doing, said, "Relax. He has a good administrative assistant. Give him some more time."
blocks.translation: 教师们对他的缺席非常不满，于是派代表团去找大学校长，要求换一位院长，或者从根本上改变他的领导方式。校长知道这位院长在做什么，说：“放心吧。他有一位很能干的行政助理。再给他一些时间。”

blocks.text: Within a short time, the money started pouring in and the faculty began to recognize the vision. It wasn't long until every time they saw the dean, they would say, “Get out of here! We don’t want to see you. Go out and bring in more funds. Your administrative assistant runs this office better than anyone else.”
blocks.translation: 没过多久，钱开始源源不断地进来，教师们也逐渐认可了他的愿景。很快，他们一见到院长就说：“走开！我们不想见到你。出去多弄些资金回来。你的行政助理把这个办公室管理得比谁都好。”

blocks.text: This man admitted to me later that the mistake he made was not doing enough team building, enough explaining, enough educating about what he was trying to accomplish. From him I learned a powerful lesson. We need to constantly be asking ourselves, “What is needed out there, and what is my unique strength?”
blocks.translation: 这个人后来向我承认，他犯的错误是团队建设做得不够，解释得不够，对自己想做成的事宣传得不够。从他身上我学到了深刻的一课。我们需要不断问自己：“外面需要什么，而我独特的优势又是什么？”

paragraphs: I knew a man who was asked to be the new dean(院长) of the College of Business of a large university. When he first arrived, he studied the situation the college faced and felt that what it needed most was money. He recognized that he had a unique capacity to raise money, and he developed a real sense of vision about fund-raising as his primary function.

This created a problem in the college because past deans had focused mainly on meeting day-to-day faculty needs. This new dean was never there. He was running around the country trying to raise money for research. But he was not attending to the day-to-day things as the previous dean had. The faculty, who were used to working with the person at the top, had to work through his administrative assistant.

The faculty became so upset with his absence that they sent a delegation to the president of the university to demand a new dean or a fundamental change in his leadership style. The president, who knew what the dean was doing, said, "Relax. He has a good administrative assistant. Give him some more time."

Within a short time, the money started pouring in and the faculty began to recognize the vision. It wasn't long until every time they saw the dean, they would say, “Get out of here! We don’t want to see you. Go out and bring in more funds. Your administrative assistant runs this office better than anyone else.”

This man admitted to me later that the mistake he made was not doing enough team building, enough explaining, enough educating about what he was trying to accomplish. From him I learned a powerful lesson. We need to constantly be asking ourselves, “What is needed out there, and what is my unique strength?”

articles.title: Your boss holds your future prospects in his hands
articles.fallbackTitle: Your boss holds your future prospects in his hands

blocks.text: Your boss holds your future prospects in his hands. Some bosses are hard to get along with. Some have excellent qualifications but no idea when it comes to dealing with people. Of course, not all bosses are like that.
blocks.translation: 你的老板掌握着你的前途。有些老板很难相处。有些资历出色，却不懂得如何与人打交道。当然，并非所有老板都是这样。

blocks.text: The relationship you have with your boss can be a major factor in determining your rise up the career ladder. Your boss is not only your leader, he is also the person best equipped to help you do the job you are paid to do. He can inform you of company direction that may affect your professional development.
blocks.translation: 你与老板的关系，可能是决定你在职业阶梯上能爬多高的重要因素。老板不仅是你的领导，也是最有可能帮助你做好本职工作的人。他能告诉你可能影响你职业发展的公司方向。

blocks.text: Your boss also needs you to perform at your best in order to accomplish his objectives. He needs your feedback in order to provide realistic and useful reports to upper management. But how does this help you establish a meaningful working relationship with your boss?
blocks.translation: 你的老板也需要你发挥最佳水平，才能实现他的目标。他需要你的反馈，才能向上级管理层提供真实有用的报告。但这对你与老板建立有意义的工作关系有什么帮助呢？

blocks.text: The key is communication. Learn and understand his goals and priorities. Observe and understand your boss's work style. If you have not been clear with his expectations, ask! Likewise, ask for feedback and accept criticism gracefully. And if he understands that you do not view your job as just something to fill the hours between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., he may be more likely to help you.
blocks.translation: 关键在于沟通。了解并理解他的目标和优先事项。观察并理解老板的工作风格。如果你不清楚他的期望，就问！同样，主动寻求反馈，并坦然接受批评。如果他知道你不把工作看成只是填满上午九点到下午五点这段时间的事，他就更可能帮助你。

blocks.text: In short, getting along with your boss requires getting to know his likes and dislikes and learning to work with his personality and management style.
blocks.translation: 总之，与老板相处需要了解他的好恶，并学会适应他的性格和管理风格。

paragraphs: Your boss holds your future prospects in his hands. Some bosses are hard to get along with. Some have excellent qualifications but no idea when it comes to dealing with people. Of course, not all bosses are like that.

The relationship you have with your boss can be a major factor in determining your rise up the career ladder. Your boss is not only your leader, he is also the person best equipped to help you do the job you are paid to do. He can inform you of company direction that may affect your professional development.

Your boss also needs you to perform at your best in order to accomplish his objectives. He needs your feedback in order to provide realistic and useful reports to upper management. But how does this help you establish a meaningful working relationship with your boss?

The key is communication. Learn and understand his goals and priorities. Observe and understand your boss's work style. If you have not been clear with his expectations, ask! And if he understands that you do not view your job as just something to fill the hours between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., he may be more likely to help you.
In short, getting along with your boss requires getting to know his likes and dislikes and learning to work with his personality and management style.

你的老板也需要你发挥最佳水平，才能实现他的目标。他需要你的反馈，才能向上级管理层提供真实有用的报告。但这对你与老板建立有意义的工作关系有什么帮助呢？
关键在于沟通。了解并理解他的目标和优先事项。观察并理解老板的工作风格。如果你不清楚他的期望，就问！同样，主动寻求反馈，并坦然接受批评。如果他知道你不把工作看成只是填满上午九点到下午五点这段时间的事，他就更可能帮助你。
总之，与老板相处需要了解他的好恶，并学会适应他的性格和管理风格。

articles.title: The appeal of advertising to buying motives can have both negative and positive effects
articles.fallbackTitle: The appeal of advertising to buying motives can have both negative and positive effects

blocks.text: The appeal of advertising to buying motives can have both negative and positive effects. Consumers may be convinced to buy a product of poor quality or high price because of an advertisement. For example, some advertisements have appealed to people’s desire for better fuel economy for their cars by advertising automotive products that improve gasoline mileage. Some of the products work. Others are worthless and a waste of consumers’ money.
blocks.translation: 广告诉诸购买动机，既能产生积极影响，也能产生消极影响。消费者可能因为一则广告而被说服去购买质量差或价格高的产品。例如，一些广告宣传能提高汽油里程的汽车产品，以此迎合人们希望汽车更省油的愿望。有些产品确实有效，另一些则毫无价值，只是浪费消费者的钱。

blocks.text: Sometimes advertising is intentionally misleading. A few years ago, a brand of bread was offered to dieters (节食者) with the message that there were fewer calories (卡路里) in every slice. It turned out that the bread was not dietetic, but just regular bread. There were fewer calories because it was sliced very thin, but there were the same number of calories in every loaf.
blocks.translation: 有时广告是故意误导的。几年前，一个面包品牌向节食者宣传，说每片面包的热量更少。结果这种面包并不是减肥食品，只是普通面包。热量之所以更少，是因为切得很薄，但一整条面包的热量并没有减少。

blocks.text: On the positive side, emotional appeals may respond to a consumer’s real concerns. Consider fire insurance. Fire insurance may be sold by appealing to fear of loss. But fear of loss is the real reason for fire insurance. The security of knowing that property is protected by insurance makes the purchase of fire insurance a worthwhile investment for most people. If consumers consider the quality of the insurance plans as well as the message in the ads, they will benefit from the advertising.
blocks.translation: 从积极的一面看，情感诉求可能回应消费者的真实关切。以火灾保险为例。火灾保险可以诉诸对损失的恐惧来销售。但对损失的恐惧正是购买火灾保险的真正原因。知道财产受保险保护所带来的安全感，使火灾保险对大多数人来说成为值得的投资。如果消费者既考虑保险方案的质量，也考虑广告传递的信息，他们就会从广告中受益。

blocks.text: Each consumer must evaluate her or his own situation. Are the benefits of the product important enough to justify buying it? Advertising is intended to appeal to consumers, but it does not force them to buy the product. Consumers still control final buying decision.
blocks.translation: 每个消费者都必须评估自己的情况。产品的好处是否重要到值得购买？广告意在吸引消费者，但并不能强迫他们购买。消费者仍然掌握着最终的购买决定。

articles.title: There is much discussion today about whether economic growth is desirable
articles.fallbackTitle: There is much discussion today about whether economic growth is desirable

blocks.text: There is much discussion today about whether economic growth is desirable. At an earlier period, our desire for material wealth may have been justified. Now, however, this desire for more than we need is causing serious problems. Even though we have good intentions, we may be producing too much, too fast.
blocks.translation: 如今有许多关于经济增长是否可取的讨论。在更早的时期，我们对物质财富的渴望或许是有道理的。然而现在，对超出所需之物的渴望正在造成严重问题。即使我们怀着良好意图，也可能生产得太多、太快。

blocks.text: Those who criticize economic growth argue that we must slow down. They believe the society is approaching certain limits on growth. These include the fixed supply of natural resources, the possible negative effects of industry on the natural environment and the continuing increase in the world's population. As society reaches these limits, economic growth can no longer continue, and the quality of life will decrease.
blocks.translation: 批评经济增长的人认为我们必须放慢速度。他们相信社会正在接近增长的某些极限。这些极限包括自然资源供给固定、工业对自然环境的潜在负面影响，以及世界人口的持续增长。当社会达到这些极限时，经济增长便无法继续，生活质量将会下降。

blocks.text: People who want more economic growth, on the other hand, argue that even at the present growth rate there are still many poor people in the world. These proponents of economic growth believe that only more growth can create the capital needed to improve the quality of life in the world. Furthermore, they argue that only continued growth can provide the financial resources required to protect our natural surroundings from industrialization.
blocks.translation: 另一方面，希望更多经济增长的人认为，即使按目前的增长率，世界上仍有许多穷人。这些经济增长的支持者相信，只有更多增长才能创造提高世界生活品质所需的资本。此外，他们主张，只有持续增长才能提供保护自然环境免受工业化破坏所需的财政资源。

blocks.text: This debate over the desirability of continued economic growth is of vital importance to business and industry. If those who argue against economic growth are correct, the problems they mention cannot be ignored. To find a solution, economists and the business community must pay attention to these problems and continue discussing them with one another.
blocks.translation: 这场关于持续经济增长是否可取的争论，对商业和工业至关重要。如果反对经济增长的人是对的，他们提到的问题就不能被忽视。为了找到解决办法，经济学家和商界必须关注这些问题，并继续相互讨论。

articles.title: Human needs seem endless
articles.fallbackTitle: Human needs seem endless

blocks.text: Human needs seem endless. When a hungry man gets a meal, he begins to think about an overcoat; when a manager gets a new sports car, a big house and pleasure boats dance into view.
blocks.translation: 人的需求似乎永无止境。饥饿的人吃上一顿饭，就开始想大衣；经理得到一辆新跑车，大房子和游艇又浮现在眼前。

blocks.text: The many needs of mankind might be regarded as making up several levels. When there is money enough to satisfy one level of needs, another level appears.
blocks.translation: 人类的诸多需求可以看作由若干层次构成。当有足够的钱满足某一层需求时，另一层需求就会出现。

blocks.text: The first and most basic level of needs involves food. Once this level is satisfied, the second level of needs, clothing and some sort of shelter, appears. By the end of World War Ⅱ, these needs were satisfied for a great majority of Americans. Then a third level appeared. It included such items as automobiles and new houses.
blocks.translation: 第一层也是最基本的一层需求涉及食物。这一层满足后，第二层需求——衣物和某种住所——就会出现。到第二次世界大战结束时，绝大多数美国人已满足这些需求。随后出现了第三层，包括汽车和新房子之类的东西。

blocks.text: By 1957 or 1958 this third level of needs was fairly well satisfied. Then, in the late 1950s, a fourth level of needs appeared: the “life-enriching” level. While the other levels involve physical satisfaction, that is, the feeding, comfort, safety, and transportation, this level stresses mental needs for recognition, achievement, and happiness. It includes a variety of goods and services, many of which could be called “luxury” items. Among them are vacation trips, the best medical and dental care, and recreation. Also included here are fancy goods and the latest styles in clothing.
blocks.translation: 到 1957 或 1958 年，第三层需求已得到较好满足。然后，在 20 世纪 50 年代末，出现了第四层需求：“丰富生活”层。其他层次涉及物质满足，即吃、舒适、安全和交通，而这一层强调被认可、成就和幸福等精神需求。它包括各种商品和服务，其中许多可称为“奢侈品”。其中有度假旅行、最好的医疗和牙科护理以及娱乐。还包括精美商品和最新款式的服装。

blocks.text: On the fourth level, a lot of money is spent on services, while on the first three levels more is spent on goods. Will consumers raise their sights to a fifth level of needs as their income increases, or will they continue to demand luxuries and personal services on the fourth level?
blocks.translation: 在第四层，大量钱花在服务上，而在前三层，更多钱花在商品上。随着收入增加，消费者会把目光投向第五层需求，还是继续在第四层要求奢侈品和个人服务？

blocks.text: A fifth level would probably involve needs that can be achieved best by community action. Consumers may be spending more on taxes to pay for government action against disease, ignorance, crime, and prejudice. After filling our stomachs, our clothes closets, our garages, our teeth, and our minds, we now may seek to ensure the health, safety, and leisure to enjoy more fully the good things on the first four levels.
blocks.translation: 第五层可能涉及最好通过社区行动实现的需求。消费者可能缴纳更多税，用于政府对抗疾病、无知、犯罪和偏见的行动。在填饱肚子、装满衣橱和车库、护理好牙齿和头脑之后，我们现在也许要寻求健康、安全和闲暇，以更充分地享受前四层的好东西。

The first and most basic level of needs involves food. Once this level is satisfied, the second level of needs, clothing and some sort of shelter, appears. By the end of World War Ⅱ, these needs were satisfied for a great majority of Americans. Then a third level appeared. It included such items as automobiles and new houses.

By 1957 or 1958 this third level of needs was fairly well satisfied. Then, in the late 1950s, a fourth level of needs appeared: the “life-enriching” level. While the other levels involve physical satisfaction, that is, the feeding, comfort, safety, and transportation, this level stresses mental needs for recognition, achievement, and happiness. It includes a variety of goods and services, many of which could be called “luxury” items. Among them are vacation trips, the best medical and dental care, and recreation. Also included here are fancy goods and the latest styles in clothing.

On the fourth level, a lot of money is spent on services, while on the first three levels more is spent on goods. Will consumers raise their sights to a fifth level of needs as their income increases, or will they continue to demand luxuries and personal services on the fourth level?

人类的诸多需求可以看作由若干层次构成。当有足够的钱满足某一层需求时，另一层需求就会出现。
第一层也是最基本的一层需求涉及食物。这一层满足后，第二层需求——衣物和某种住所——就会出现。到第二次世界大战结束时，绝大多数美国人已满足这些需求。随后出现了第三层，包括汽车和新房子之类的东西。
到 1957 或 1958 年，第三层需求已得到较好满足。然后，在 20 世纪 50 年代末，出现了第四层需求：“丰富生活”层。其他层次涉及物质满足，即吃、舒适、安全和交通，而这一层强调被认可、成就和幸福等精神需求。它包括各种商品和服务，其中许多可称为“奢侈品”。其中有度假旅行、最好的医疗和牙科护理以及娱乐。还包括精美商品和最新款式的服装。
在第四层，大量钱花在服务上，而在前三层，更多钱花在商品上。随着收入增加，消费者会把目光投向第五层需求，还是继续在第四层要求奢侈品和个人服务？
第五层可能涉及最好通过社区行动实现的需求。消费者可能缴纳更多税，用于政府对抗疾病、无知、犯罪和偏见的行动。在填饱肚子、装满衣橱和车库、护理好牙齿和头脑之后，我们现在也许要寻求健康、安全和闲暇，以更充分地享受前四层的好东西。

blocks.text: President Coolidge’s statement, “The business of America is business,” still points to an important truth today—that business institutions have more prestige (威望) in American society than any other kind of organization, including the government. Why do business institutions possess this great prestige?
blocks.translation: 柯立芝总统“美国的事务就是商业”这句话，今天仍指向一个重要事实：商业机构在美国社会中的威望超过任何其他类型的组织，包括政府。为什么商业机构拥有如此高的威望？

blocks.text: One reason is that Americans view business as being more firmly based on the ideal of competition than other institutions in society. Since competition is seen as the major source of progress and prosperity by most Americans, competitive business institutions are respected. Competition is not only good in itself, it is the means by which other basic American values such as individual freedom, equality of opportunity, and hard work is protected.
blocks.translation: 一个原因是，美国人认为商业比其他社会机构更牢固地建立在竞争理念之上。既然多数美国人把竞争视为进步与繁荣的主要源泉，竞争性的商业机构就受到尊重。竞争本身不仅有益，它还是保护个人自由、机会平等和勤奋等美国基本价值观的手段。

blocks.text: Competition protects the freedom of the individual by ensuring that there is no monopoly (垄断) of power. In contrast to one, all-powerful government, many businesses compete against each other for profits. Theoretically, if one business tries to take unfair advantage of its customers, it will lose to competing business which treats its customers more fairly. Where many businesses compete for the customers’ dollar, they cannot afford to treat them like inferiors or slaves.
blocks.translation: 竞争通过确保权力不被垄断来保护个人自由。与一个全能的政府不同，许多企业为利润相互竞争。理论上，如果一家企业试图不公平地占顾客便宜，它就会输给对待顾客更公平的竞争对手。当许多企业争夺顾客的钱时，它们负担不起把顾客当作下人或奴隶。

blocks.text: A contrast is often made between business, which is competitive, and government, which is a monopoly. Because business is competitive, many Americans believe that it is more supportive of freedom than government, even though government leaders are elected by the people and business leaders are not. Many Americans believe, then, that competition is as important, or even more important, than democracy in preserving freedom.
blocks.translation: 人们常把竞争性的商业与垄断性的政府作对比。由于商业是竞争性的，许多美国人认为它比政府更支持自由，尽管政府领导人是民选的，而商业领袖不是。因此，许多美国人认为，在维护自由方面，竞争与民主同等重要，甚至更重要。

blocks.text: Competition in business is also believed to strengthen the ideal of equality of opportunity. Competition is seen as an open and fair race where success goes to the swiftest person regardless of his or her social class background. Competitive success is commonly seen as the American alternative to social rank based on family background.
blocks.translation: 商业竞争也被认为能强化机会平等的理念。竞争被视为一场公开公平的赛跑，成功属于最快的人，不论其社会阶层背景如何。竞争性成功通常被视为美国式替代品，取代以家庭背景为基础的社会等级。

blocks.text: Business is therefore viewed as an expression of the idea of equality of opportunity rather than the aristocratic (贵族的) idea of inherited privilege.

articles.fallbackTitle: I am one of the many city people who are always saying that given the choice we would pref

blocks.text: I am one of the many city people who are always saying that given the choice we would prefer to live in the country away from the dirt and noise of a large city. I have managed to convince myself that if it weren’t for my job I would immediately head out for the open spaces and go back to nature in some sleepy village buried in the country. But how realistic is the dream?
blocks.translation: 我是许多城里人中的一个，我们总说：如果有得选，我们宁愿住在乡下，远离大城市的污浊和喧嚣。我说服了自己：要不是为了工作，我会立刻奔向开阔的天地，回到某个沉睡在乡间的小村庄，回归自然。但这个梦想有多现实呢？

blocks.text: Cities can be frightening places. The majority of the population live in massive tower blocks, noisy, dirty and impersonal. The sense of belonging to a community tends to disappear when you live fifteen floors up. All you can see from your window is sky, or other blocks of flats. Children become aggressive and nervous — cooped up at home all day, with nowhere to play; their mothers feel isolated from the rest of the world. Strangely enough, whereas in the past the inhabitants of one street all knew each other, nowadays people on the same floor in tower blocks don’t even say hello to each other.
blocks.translation: 城市可能是令人恐惧的地方。大多数人口住在巨大的高楼里，嘈杂、肮脏而且冷漠。当你住在十五层楼以上时，对社区的归属感往往会消失。从窗口只能看到天空或别的公寓楼。孩子们变得好斗、紧张——整天被关在家里，没有地方玩；他们的母亲感到与外界隔绝。奇怪的是，过去一条街上的人都互相认识，而如今同一层楼的人甚至彼此连招呼都不打。

blocks.text: Country life, on the other hand, differs from this kind of isolated existence in that a sense of community generally binds the inhabitants of small villages together. People have the advantage of knowing that there is always someone to turn to when they need help. But country life has disadvantages too. While it is true that you may be among friends in a village, it is also true that you are cut off from the existing and important events that take place in cities. There’s little possibility of going to a new show or the latest movie. Shopping becomes a major problem, and for anything slightly out of the ordinary you have to go on an expedition to the nearest large town. The city-dweller who leaves for the country is often oppressed by a sense of unbearable stillness and quiet.
blocks.translation: 另一方面，乡村生活与这种孤立的存在不同，因为一种社区感通常把一个小村庄的居民联系在一起。人们有一个好处：知道自己需要帮助时总有人可以求助。但乡村生活也有缺点。虽然你在村里可能置身于朋友之中，但你也确实与城市里发生的重要事件隔绝。去看一场新演出或最新电影的机会很少。购物成了大问题，稍微不寻常一点的东西都得跑到最近的大城镇去采购。离开城市去乡下的人，常常被一种难以忍受的寂静压得喘不过气。

blocks.text: What, then, is the answer? The country has the advantage of peace and quiet, but suffers from the disadvantage of being cut off; the city breeds a feeling of isolation, and constant noise batters the senses. But one of its main advantages is that you are at the center of things, and that life doesn’t come to an end at half-past nine at night. Some people have found (or rather bought) a compromise between the two: they have expressed their preference for the “quiet life” by leaving the suburbs and moving to villages within commuting distance of large cities. They generally have about as much sensitivity as the plastic flowers they leave behind — they are polluted with strange ideas about change and improvement which they force on to the unwilling original inhabitants of the villages.
blocks.translation: 那么，答案是什么呢？乡村有宁静的好处，却有与世隔绝的缺点；城市滋生孤立感，持续的噪音冲击着感官。但城市的主要优点之一是，你身处事物的中心，生活不会在晚上九点半就结束。有些人找到了（或者说买到了）两者之间的折中：他们选择“安静的生活”，离开郊区，搬到离大城市通勤距离内的村庄。他们的敏感程度大概和他们留下的塑料花差不多——他们满脑子奇怪的想法，想要“改变”和“改善”，并把这些强加给不情愿的原有村民。

blocks.text: What then of my dreams of leaning on a cottage gate and murmuring “morning” to the locals as they pass by? I’m keen on the idea, but you see there’s my cat, Toby. I’m not at all sure that he would take to all that fresh air and exercise in the long grass. I mean, can you see him mixing with all those hearty males down the farm? No, he would rather have the electric imitation-coal fire any evening.
blocks.translation: 那么，我倚在村舍门前，对着路过的当地人低声说“早上好”的梦想又怎样呢？我很喜欢这个想法，但你知道，我还有我的猫托比。我完全不确定它会不会喜欢那么多新鲜空气和在深草丛里的运动。我的意思是，你能想象它和农场里那些健壮的雄性动物打成一片吗？不，它宁愿每天晚上守着那台电动的仿煤火炉。

articles.title: Shopping for clothes is not the same experience for a man as it is for a woman
articles.fallbackTitle: Shopping for clothes is not the same experience for a man as it is for a woman

blocks.text: Shopping for clothes is not the same experience for a man as it is for a woman. A man goes shopping because he needs something. His purpose is clear and decided in advance. He knows what he wants, and his objective is to find it and buy it; the price is the second place for consideration (考虑). All men simply walk into a shop and ask the assistant for what they want. If the shop has it, the salesman quickly produces it, and the man begins to try it at once. For a man, the small problems may begin when the shop does not have what he wants, or does not have exactly what he wants. In that case the salesman will try to sell the customer something else. Very often, he offers the nearest thing that he can produce.
blocks.translation: 买衣服对男人和女人来说不是同一种体验。男人去购物是因为他需要某样东西。他的目的明确，而且是事先决定好的。他知道自己想要什么，目标是找到它并买下它；价格是第二位要考虑的因素。所有男人都会直接走进商店，向店员要他们想要的东西。如果店里有，售货员很快拿出来，男人马上开始试穿。对男人来说，小麻烦可能始于店里没有他想要的东西，或者没有完全符合他想要的东西。那种情况下，售货员会试图向顾客推销别的东西，而且常常拿出他能找到的最接近的东西。

blocks.text: Now how does a woman go about buying clothes? In almost every respect, she does so in the opposite way. Her shopping is not often based on need. She has never fully made up her mind about what she wants, and she is only “having a look round”. She will still be satisfied even if she has bought nothing.
blocks.translation: 那么女人是怎样买衣服的呢？几乎在每个方面，她的做法都相反。她购物通常不是出于需要。她从未完全想清楚自己想要什么，只是“随便看看”。即使什么也没买，她仍然会感到满足。

articles.title: The multi-billion-dollar Western pop music industry is under fire
articles.fallbackTitle: The multi-billion-dollar Western pop music industry is under fire

blocks.text: The multi-billion-dollar Western pop music industry is under fire. It is being blamed by the United Nations for the dramatic rise in drug abuse worldwide, “The most worrying development is a culture of drug-friendliness,” says the UN’s International Narcotics Control Board in a report released last year.
blocks.translation: 价值数十亿美元的西方流行音乐产业正受到抨击。联合国指责它导致全世界吸毒现象急剧增加。联合国国际麻醉品管制局在去年发布的一份报告中说：“最令人担忧的事态发展是一种对毒品友好的文化。”

blocks.text: The 74-page study says the pop music, as a global industry, is by far the most influential trend-setter for young people of most cultures. “Some songs encourage people to take drugs. Certain pop stars make statements and set examples as if the use of drugs for non-medicinal purposes were a normal and acceptable part of a person’s lifestyle,” the study says.
blocks.translation: 这份 74 页的研究报告指出，流行音乐作为一个全球产业，迄今为止是大多数文化中年轻人最具影响力的潮流引领者。报告说：“一些歌曲鼓励人们吸毒。某些流行歌星发表言论、树立榜样，仿佛非医疗用途使用毒品是人们生活方式中正常且可接受的一部分。”

blocks.text: Surprisingly, says the Board, the effect of drug-friendly pop music seems to survive despite the occasional shock of death by overdose. “Such incidents tend to be seen as an occasion to mourn the loss of a role model, and not an opportunity to face the deadly effect of drug use,” it notes. Since the 1970s, several internationally famous singers and movie stars — including Elvis Presley, Janice Joplin, John Belushi, Jimi Hendrix, Jonathan Melvin and Andy Gibbs — have died of either drug abuse or drug related illnesses. With the globalization of popular music — messages promoting drug abuse are now reaching beyond their countries of origin. “In most countries, the names of certain pop stars have become familiar to the members of every household,” the study says.
blocks.translation: 该机构表示，令人惊讶的是，尽管偶尔发生吸毒过量致死的震惊事件，对毒品友好的流行音乐的影响似乎依然存在。报告指出：“这类事件往往被视为悼念失去偶像的场合，而不是正视吸毒致命后果的机会。”自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，几位国际知名歌手和影星——包括埃尔维斯·普雷斯利、贾尼斯·乔普林、约翰·贝鲁西、吉米·亨德里克斯、乔纳森·梅尔文和安迪·吉布斯——死于吸毒或与毒品相关的疾病。随着流行音乐的全球化，宣扬吸毒的信息如今已传播到原产国之外。报告说：“在大多数国家，某些流行歌星的名字已为家家户户所熟悉。”

blocks.text: The UN study also blames the media for its description of certain drug incidents, which encourages rather than prevents drug abuse. “Over the past years, we have seen how drug abuse is increasingly regarded as being acceptable or even attractive,” says Hamid Ghodse, president of the Board. “Powerful pressure groups run political campaigns aimed at legalizing controlled drugs,” he says. Ghodse also points out that all these developments have created an environment which is tolerant of or even favorable to drug abuse and spoils international drug prevention efforts currently under way.
blocks.translation: 联合国的研究还指责媒体对某些毒品事件的描述，这种描述鼓励而非阻止吸毒。“过去几年，我们看到吸毒越来越被视为可接受甚至具有吸引力，”该机构主席哈米德·戈德塞说。“势力强大的压力集团开展政治运动，旨在使受管制毒品合法化，”他说。戈德塞还指出，所有这些事态发展营造了一种宽容甚至纵容吸毒的环境，破坏了目前正在进行的国际禁毒努力。

blocks.text: The study focuses on demand reduction and prevention within an environment that has become tolerant of drug abuse. The Board calls on governments to do their legal and moral duties, and to act against the pro-drug-abuse messages of the youth culture to which young people are increasingly being exposed.

translations: 价值数十亿美元的西方流行音乐产业正受到抨击。联合国指责它导致全世界吸毒现象急剧增加。联合国国际麻醉品管制局在去年发布的一份报告中说：“最令人担忧的事态发展是一种对毒品友好的文化。”
这份 74 页的研究报告指出，流行音乐作为一个全球产业，迄今为止是大多数文化中年轻人最具影响力的潮流引领者。报告说：“一些歌曲鼓励人们吸毒。某些流行歌星发表言论、树立榜样，仿佛非医疗用途使用毒品是人们生活方式中正常且可接受的一部分。”

该机构表示，令人惊讶的是，尽管偶尔发生吸毒过量致死的震惊事件，对毒品友好的流行音乐的影响似乎依然存在。报告指出：“这类事件往往被视为悼念失去偶像的场合，而不是正视吸毒致命后果的机会。”自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，几位国际知名歌手和影星——包括埃尔维斯·普雷斯利、贾尼斯·乔普林、约翰·贝鲁西、吉米·亨德里克斯、乔纳森·梅尔文和安迪·吉布斯——死于吸毒或与毒品相关的疾病。随着流行音乐的全球化，宣扬吸毒的信息如今已传播到原产国之外。报告说：“在大多数国家，某些流行歌星的名字已为家家户户所熟悉。”
联合国的研究还指责媒体对某些毒品事件的描述，这种描述鼓励而非阻止吸毒。“过去几年，我们看到吸毒越来越被视为可接受甚至具有吸引力，”该机构主席哈米德·戈德塞说。“势力强大的压力集团开展政治运动，旨在使受管制毒品合法化，”他说。戈德塞还指出，所有这些事态发展营造了一种宽容甚至纵容吸毒的环境，破坏了目前正在进行的国际禁毒努力。
这项研究重点关注在一个已变得宽容吸毒的环境中减少需求和预防吸毒。该机构呼吁各国政府履行法律和道德义务，并针对青年文化中宣扬吸毒的信息采取行动，因为年轻人正越来越多地接触这些信息。

articles.title: Who takes care of the elderly in the United States today
articles.fallbackTitle: Who takes care of the elderly in the United States today

blocks.text: Who takes care of the elderly in the United States today? The fact is that family members provide over 80% of the care that elderly people need. In most cases the elderly live in their own homes. A very small percentage of America’s elderly live in nursing homes.
blocks.translation: 今天在美国，谁照顾老人？事实是，家庭成员提供了老人所需照料的 80% 以上。多数情况下老人住在自己家里。美国老人中只有很小一部分住在养老院。

blocks.text: Samuel Preston, a sociologist at the University of Pennsylvania, studied how the American family is changing. He reported that by the time the average American couple reaches about 40 years of age, their parents are usually still alive. The statistics show the change in lifestyles and responsibilities of aging (老龄化) Americans. The average middle-aged couple can look forward to caring for elderly parents some time after their own children have grown up. Moreover, because people today live longer after an illness than people did years ago, family members must provide long-term care. These facts also mean that after caregivers provide for their elderly parents, who will eventually die, they will be old and may require care too. When they do, their spouses (配偶) will probably take care of them because they have had fewer children than their parents did.
blocks.translation: 宾夕法尼亚大学社会学家塞缪尔·普雷斯顿研究了美国家庭如何变化。他报告说，到美国夫妻平均约 40 岁时，他们的父母通常还健在。统计数字显示了老龄美国人生活方式与责任的变化。普通中年夫妻可以预期，在自己的孩子长大之后的某个时候要照顾年迈的父母。此外，由于今天人们在病后存活的时间比过去更长，家庭成员必须提供长期照料。这些事实还意味着，当照护者送走最终会去世的年迈父母后，他们自己也将年老，也可能需要照料。到那时，照顾他们的很可能是配偶，因为他们比父母那一代生的孩子少。

blocks.text: Because Americans are living longer than ever, more social workers have begun to study ways of care-giving to improve the care of the elderly. They have found that all caregivers share a common characteristic: they believe that they are the best people for the job. The social workers have also discovered three basic reasons why the caregivers take on the responsibility of caring for an elderly, dependent relative. Many caregivers believe they had an obligation (职责) to help their relatives. Some think that helping others makes them feel more useful. Others hope that by helping someone now, they will deserve care when they become old and dependent.

blocks.text: Some people argue that the pressure on international sportsmen and sportswomen kills the essence of sport—the pursuit of personal excellence. Children kick a football around for fun. When they get older and play for local school teams, they will become competitive but they still enjoy playing. The individual representing his country cannot afford to think about enjoying himself, and he has to think only about winning. He is responsible for the entire nation’s hopes, dreams and reputation.
blocks.translation: 有人主张，国际男女运动员身上的压力扼杀了体育的本质——对个人卓越的追求。孩子们踢足球是为了好玩。当他们长大、为当地校队踢球时，会变得好胜，但仍然享受踢球。代表国家出战的个人则不能想着享受，他只能想着赢。他肩负着整个民族的希望、梦想与声誉。

blocks.text: A good example is the FIFA World Cup. Football is the third most important sport in the world. Winning the World Cup is perhaps the summit of international sporting success. Mention Argentina to someone and the chances are that he’ll think of football. In a sense, winning the World Cup put Argentina on the map.
blocks.translation: 国际足联世界杯就是一个好例子。足球是世界上第三重要的运动。赢得世界杯也许是国际体育成功的顶峰。向某人提到阿根廷，他很可能会想到足球。某种意义上，赢得世界杯让阿根廷闻名于世。

blocks.text: Some sports fans and supporters get quite unreasonable about the World Cup. People in England felt that their country was somehow important after they won in 1966. In 1978, thousands of the Scots sold their cars, and even their houses, and spent all their money traveling to Argentina, where the finals were played.
blocks.translation: 一些球迷和支持者对世界杯相当不理智。1966 年英格兰夺冠后，英国人觉得自己的国家似乎变得重要了。1978 年，成千上万的苏格兰人卖掉汽车甚至房子，花光所有的钱前往决赛举办地阿根廷。

blocks.text: So, am I arguing that international competition kills the idea of sport? Certainly not! Do the Argentinean really believe that because eleven of their men proved the most skillful at football, their nation is in every way better than all others? Not really. But it’s nice to know that you won and that in one way at least your country is the best.
blocks.translation: 那么，我是在主张国际竞争扼杀了体育的理念吗？当然不是！阿根廷人真的相信，因为他们的十一个男人证明了自己最擅长足球，他们的国家就在各方面都优于所有其他国家吗？并非如此。但知道自己赢了，知道自己的国家至少在某一方面是最好的，这种感觉很好。

blocks.text: Imagine walking through someone’s apartment. The rooms are almost empty, and the only pieces of furniture are a simple table and folded sofa. There are no decorative objects lying around—just the essentials. You open the closet to find you can count the number of clothing items inside on one hand. The space seems more like a prison cell than a home, and you may think the resident cannot afford to buy more things fill the apartment with.
blocks.translation: 想象你走过某人的公寓。房间几乎空无一物，仅有的家具是一张简易桌子和一张折叠沙发。周围没有装饰品——只有必需品。你打开衣柜，发现里面的衣物一只手就能数完。这个空间更像牢房而不是家，你可能会想，住户是买不起更多东西来填满公寓。

blocks.text: It turns out that the apartment’s owner is a minimalist (简约主义者) who chooses to limit his number of belongings. Minimalism goes against consumer society by dramatically reducing possessions. Minimalists follow this philosophy to varying degrees, but they claim that cutting back on excess stuff leads to a more fulfilling life.
blocks.translation: 原来，这套公寓的主人是一位简约主义者，他选择限制自己的物品数量。极简主义通过大幅减少所有物来对抗消费社会。极简主义者践行这一理念的程度各不相同，但他们声称，削减多余的东西能带来更充实的生活。

blocks.text: With fewer possessions, they do not have to spend as much time cleaning, thinking about what they are missing, or trying to keep up with the latest trends. Minimalists say this frees up their time for things that they find meaningful such as exercising, traveling, and being with loved ones.
blocks.translation: 物品更少，他们就不必花那么多时间打扫、琢磨自己缺什么，或努力追赶最新潮流。极简主义者说，这为他们认为有意义的事情腾出了时间，比如锻炼、旅行和与所爱之人相处。

blocks.text: Extreme minimalism is not for everyone, but a mild form of it has grown in popularity recently, thanks to Marie Kondo’s best-selling book The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up. Kondo has become distinguished for her tidying skills, which she developed naturally. One of her main beliefs is that one should only own things that one truly loves.
blocks.translation: 极端极简主义并不适合所有人，但多亏近藤麻理惠的畅销书《怦然心动的人生整理魔法》，一种温和的极简主义近来日益流行。近藤因其整理技巧而闻名，这些技巧是她自然而然发展出来的。她的主要信念之一是：人只应拥有自己真正喜爱的物品。

blocks.text: It can be unpleasant to part with belongings, but Kondo’s methods have helped millions to remove useless things. Her technique for making space is to go through things by category, starting with clothing, then books, papers, tiny objects, and finally, memorable items. She instructs her followers to touch each object they own and keep only those that spark joy, promising that this will lead to domestic happiness.

blocks.text: Kondo stresses that it is not about throwing things away, but about finding the things you want to remain with you and striking a balance between personal joy and possessions. It can be unpleasant to part with belongings, but Kondo’s methods have helped millions to remove useless things. Her technique for making space is to go through things by category, starting with clothing, then books, papers, tiny objects, and finally, memorable items. She instructs her followers to touch each object they own and keep only those that spark joy, promising that this will lead to domestic happiness.

Kondo stresses that it is not about throwing things away, but about finding the things you want to remain with you and striking a balance between personal joy and possessions. Even if you are not ready to become a minimalist, you may want to consider reducing the number of things you own, for it seems that letting go of things can truly make room for happiness.

translations: 想象你走过某人的公寓。房间几乎空无一物，仅有的家具是一张简易桌子和一张折叠沙发。周围没有装饰品——只有必需品。你打开衣柜，发现里面的衣物一只手就能数完。这个空间更像牢房而不是家，你可能会想，住户是买不起更多东西来填满公寓。
原来，这套公寓的主人是一位简约主义者，他选择限制自己的物品数量。极简主义通过大幅减少所有物来对抗消费社会。极简主义者践行这一理念的程度各不相同，但他们声称，削减多余的东西能带来更充实的生活。
物品更少，他们就不必花那么多时间打扫、琢磨自己缺什么，或努力追赶最新潮流。极简主义者说，这为他们认为有意义的事情腾出了时间，比如锻炼、旅行和与所爱之人相处。
极端极简主义并不适合所有人，但多亏近藤麻理惠的畅销书《怦然心动的人生整理魔法》，一种温和的极简主义近来日益流行。近藤因其整理技巧而闻名，这些技巧是她自然而然发展出来的。她的主要信念之一是：人只应拥有自己真正喜爱的物品。
与物品告别可能令人不快，但近藤的方法已帮助数百万人清除无用之物。她腾出空间的方法是按类别逐一整理，从衣物开始，然后是书籍、纸张、小物件，最后是有纪念意义的物品。她指导追随者触摸自己拥有的每件物品，只保留那些能带来心动感的，并承诺这会带来家庭幸福。
近藤强调，这不是关于扔掉东西，而是关于找到你想留在身边的东西，并在个人快乐与物品之间取得平衡。即使你还没准备成为极简主义者，也不妨考虑减少自己拥有的物品数量，因为放下物品似乎真的能为幸福腾出空间。

blocks.text: Today’s grandparents are joining their grandchildren on social media. In the UK the over-55s are joining social media sites in increasing numbers, meaning that they will soon be the second biggest user group of these sites, with 3.5 million users aged 55–64 and 2.9 million over-65s.
blocks.translation: 如今的祖父母正加入孙辈的社交媒体。在英国，55 岁以上人群正越来越多地加入社交网站，这意味着他们很快将成为这些网站的第二大用户群：55 至 64 岁用户有 350 万，65 岁以上有 290 万。

blocks.text: Sheila, aged 59, says, “I joined to see what my grandchildren are doing, as my daughter posts videos and photos of them. It’s a much better way to see what they’re doing than waiting for letters and photos in the post. That’s how we did it when I was a child, but I think I’m lucky I get to see so much more of their lives than my grandparents did.”
blocks.translation: 59 岁的希拉说：“我加入是为了看看孙辈在做什么，因为我女儿会发他们的视频和照片。这比等邮寄来的信件和照片好多了。我小时候我们就是这样做的，但我觉得自己很幸运，能比我的祖父母看到更多孙辈的生活。”

blocks.text: Unexpectedly, Sheila’s grandchildren are less likely to use social media sites themselves. Children under 17 in the UK are leaving the sites—only 2.2 million users are under 17—but they’re not going far from their smartphones. Chloe, aged 15, even sleeps with her phone. “It’s my alarm clock, so I have to,” she says. “I look at it before I go to sleep and as soon as I wake up.” Unlike her grandmother’s generation, Chloe’s age group is spending so much time on their phones at home that they are missing out on spending time with their friends in real life. Sheila, on the other hand, has made contact with old friends from school that she has not heard from in forty years.
blocks.translation: 出乎意料的是，希拉的孙辈自己倒不太使用社交网站。英国 17 岁以下的孩子正在离开这些网站——只有 220 万用户未满 17 岁——但他们并没有远离智能手机。15 岁的克洛伊甚至和手机一起睡觉。“它是我的闹钟，所以我必须这样，”她说。“我睡前看它，一醒来就看。”与祖母那一代不同，克洛伊这个年龄段的人在家花太多时间在手机上，以至于错过了与朋友在现实生活中相处的时间。而希拉则与四十年来没有联系的老同学重新建立了联系。

blocks.text: “We use social media sites to arrange to meet all over the country,” she says. “They have changed my social life completely.”
blocks.translation: “我们用社交网站安排在全国各地见面，”她说。“它们彻底改变了我的社交生活。”

blocks.text: The first forest library in Shanghai recently opened to the public. Known as Read \& Joy Forest, the library was jointly founded by Pudong New Area and Shanghai Library. It is located in an urban wood, covering an area of 20, 546 square meters.
blocks.translation: 上海首个森林图书馆最近向公众开放。这座图书馆名为“悦读森林”，由浦东新区和上海图书馆共同创办。它位于一片城市林地中，占地 20,546 平方米。

blocks.text: The design of forest library allows an environment-friendly principle — ensuring minimum disturbance to nature, with existing green spaces connected by wooden walkways.
blocks.translation: 森林图书馆的设计遵循环保原则——确保对自然的干扰最小，用木制步道连接现有的绿地。

blocks.text: The library is can be open air and equipped with facilities such as benches and an information booth. Visitors can read and relax in a natural environment. It allows visitors to take a pleasant walk in the quiet forest, which includes osmanthus.
blocks.translation: 这座图书馆可以是露天的，配备长椅和信息亭等设施。游客可以在自然环境中阅读和放松。它让游客能在安静的森林中愉快散步，林中还有桂花。

blocks.text: “I learned about the forest library from my friends, so I came here,” said a 21-year-old college student, Mr. Wang. “The green outdoor environment helps reduce eyestrain. I will come back for sure.”
blocks.translation: “我是从朋友那里听说森林图书馆的，所以就来这里了，”21 岁的大学生王先生说。“绿色的户外环境有助于减轻眼睛疲劳。我一定会再来的。”

blocks.text: Having a library in a wood is an extension of reading indoors, according to Xu Qiang, who works in Shanghai Library. “It offers a different reading experience to readers,” he added.
blocks.translation: 在上海图书馆工作的徐强认为，在森林里设图书馆是室内阅读的延伸。“它给读者提供了一种不同的阅读体验，”他补充道。

articles.title: Social change is more likely to occur in societies where there is a mixture of different k
articles.fallbackTitle: Social change is more likely to occur in societies where there is a mixture of different k

blocks.text: Social change is more likely to occur in societies where there is a mixture of different kinds of people than in societies where people are similar in many ways. The simple reason for this is that there are more different ways of looking at things present in the first kind of society. There are more ideas, more disagreements in interest, and more groups and organizations with different beliefs. In addition, there is usually a greater worldly interest and greater tolerance in mixed societies. All these factors tend to promote social change by opening more areas of life to decision. In a society where people are quite similar in many ways, there are fewer occasions for people to see the need or the opportunity for change because everything seems to be the same. And although conditions may not be satisfactory, they are at least customary and undisputed.
blocks.translation: 社会变化更可能发生在由不同人群混合组成的社会，而不是在人们许多方面都相似的社会。简单的原因是，前一种社会存在更多不同的看待事物的方式。有更多想法、更多利益分歧，也有更多持不同信念的团体和组织。此外，混合社会通常有更广泛的世俗兴趣和更大的宽容。所有这些因素都倾向于通过把更多生活领域开放给决策来推动社会变化。而在人们许多方面都相似的社会里，人们看到改变的需要或机会的场合更少，因为一切似乎都一样。即使条件并不令人满意，至少它们是习以为常、无人质疑的。

blocks.text: Within a society, social change is also likely to occur more frequently and more readily in the material aspects of the culture than in the non-material, for example, in technology rather than in values; in what has been learned later in life rather than what was learned early; in the less basic and less emotional aspects of society than in their opposites; in the simple elements rather than in the complex ones; in form rather than in substance; and in elements that are acceptable to the culture rather than in strange elements.
blocks.translation: 在一个社会内部，社会变化也更容易、更频繁地发生在文化的物质层面而非非物质层面，例如在技术而非价值观中；在人生后期学到的内容而非早期学到的内容中；在社会中较不基本、较不涉及情感的方面而非其对立面中；在简单要素而非复杂要素中；在形式而非实质中；在文化可接受的要素而非陌生要素中。

paragraphs: Social change is more likely to occur in societies where there is a mixture of different kinds of people than in societies where people are similar in many ways. The simple reason for this is that there are more different ways of looking at things present in the first kind of society. There are more ideas, more disagreements in interest, and more groups and organizations with different beliefs. In addition, there is usually a greater worldly interest and greater tolerance in mixed societies. All these factors tend to promote social change by opening more areas of life to decision. In a society where people are quite similar in many ways, there are fewer occasions for people to see the need or the opportunity for change because everything seems to be the same. And although conditions may not be satisfactory, they are at least customary and undisputed.

Within a society, social change is also likely to occur more frequently and more readily in the material aspects of the culture than in the non-material, for example, in technology rather than in values; in what has been learned later in life rather than what was learned early; in the less basic and less emotional aspects of society than in their opposites; in the simple elements rather than in the complex ones; in form rather than in substance; and in elements that are acceptable to the culture rather than in strange elements.

certain factors that determine the ease with which social changes occur
different types of social change in two different societies and in different aspects
certain factors that promote social change

Different points of view
Greater tolerance
Advanced technology

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT true?

questions.stem: The expression "greater tolerance" (Para. 1) refers to ________.

more respect for different beliefs and behavior
greater willingness to accept social change

questions.stem: Social change is less likely to occur in a society where people are quite similar in many ways because ________.

people there have got so accustomed to their conditions that they seldom think it necessary to change
people there are easy to please

articles.title: In 2013, New York State ordered stores to charge a deposit on beverage(饮料) containers
articles.fallbackTitle: In 2013, New York State ordered stores to charge a deposit on beverage(饮料) containers

blocks.text: In 2013, New York State ordered stores to charge a deposit on beverage(饮料) containers. Within a year, consumers had returned millions of aluminum cans and glass and plastic bottles. Plenty of companies were eager to accept the aluminum and glass as raw materials for new products, but because few could figure out what to do with the plastic, much of it would be buried in landfills(垃圾填埋场). The problem was not limited to New York. Unfortunately, there were too few uses for second hand plastic.
blocks.translation: 2013 年，纽约州命令商店对饮料容器收取押金。一年之内，消费者退回了数百万个铝罐以及玻璃瓶和塑料瓶。许多公司急于收购铝和玻璃作为新产品的原料，但由于很少有人能想出如何处理塑料，大部分塑料被埋进垃圾填埋场。这个问题不仅限于纽约。不幸的是，二手塑料的用途太少了。

blocks.text: Today, one out of five plastic soda bottles is recycled in the United States. The reason for the change is that now there are dozens of companies across the country buying discarded plastic soda bottles and turning them into fence posts, paint brushes, etc.
blocks.translation: 如今，美国每五个塑料汽水瓶中就有一个被回收。变化的原因是，现在全国有数十家公司购买废弃的塑料汽水瓶，把它们制成栅栏柱、油漆刷等。

blocks.text: As the New York experience shows, recycling involves more than simply separating valuable materials from the rest of the rubbish. A discard remains a discard until somebody figures out how to give it a second life—and until economic arrangements exist to give that second life value. Without adequate markets to absorb materials collected for recycling, throwaways actually depress prices for used materials.
blocks.translation: 正如纽约的经验所示，回收不仅仅是把有价值的材料从其余垃圾中分出来。一件废弃物仍然是废弃物，直到有人想出如何赋予它第二次生命——并且直到存在经济安排，让这第二次生命具有价值。如果没有足够的市场吸收回收来的材料，一次性用品实际上会压低旧材料的价格。

blocks.text: Shrinking landfill space, and rising costs for burying and burning rubbish are forcing local governments to look more closely at recycling. In many areas, the East Coast especially, recycling is already the least expensive waste management option. For every ton of waste recycled, a city avoids paying for its disposal, which, in parts of New York, amounts to savings of more than $100 per ton. Recycling also stimulates the local economy by creating jobs and trims the pollution control and energy costs of industries that make recycled products by giving them a more refined raw material.
blocks.translation: 填埋空间缩小，掩埋和焚烧垃圾的成本上升，正迫使地方政府更仔细地审视回收。在许多地区，尤其是东海岸，回收已经是最便宜的垃圾管理选择。每回收一吨垃圾，城市就省下一笔处理费；在纽约部分地区，每吨可节省 100 多美元。回收还通过创造就业刺激地方经济，并通过为利用回收材料的企业提供更精细的原料，降低其污染控制和能源成本。

questions.stem: The returned plastic bottles in New York used to _______.

be turned into raw materials

questions.stem: Recycling has become the first choice for the disposal of rubbish because _______.

recycling causes little pollution

questions.stem: It can be concluded from the passage that _______.

local governments in the U.S. can expect big profits from recycling

articles.title: For years and years people have been saying that the railways are dead
articles.fallbackTitle: For years and years people have been saying that the railways are dead

blocks.text: For years and years people have been saying that the railways are dead. “We can do without railways, people say, as if motorcars and planes made the railways unnecessary. We all keep hearing that trains are slow, that they lose money, and that they’re dying. But this is far from the truth. In these days when oil is expensive, the railways have become highly competitive with motorcars and planes. If you want to carry people or goods from place to place, they’re cheaper than planes.
blocks.translation: 多年来人们一直说铁路已经死了。“没有铁路我们也行，”人们说，仿佛汽车和飞机让铁路变得多余。我们不断听到火车很慢、铁路亏钱、正在消亡的说法。但这远非事实。在石油昂贵的今天，铁路与汽车和飞机相比已极具竞争力。如果要运送人或货物，铁路比飞机便宜。

blocks.text: Railways have much in common with planes. A plane goes in a straight line and so does a railway. What is more, it takes you from the heart of a city into the heart of another. But a railway doesn’t leave you as a plane does, miles and miles away from the city center. It doesn’t hold you up as a motorcar does, in endless traffic jams. And a single train can carry goods which no plane or motorcar could ever do.
blocks.translation: 铁路与飞机有许多共同之处。飞机走直线，铁路也走直线。更重要的是，它把你从一个城市的中心送到另一个城市的中心。但铁路不会像飞机那样，把你丢在离市中心许多英里之外。它也不会像汽车那样，让你堵在没完没了的车流里。而且一列火车能运的货物，任何飞机或汽车都做不到。

blocks.text: Far from being dead, the railways are very much alive. Modern railway lines give you a smooth, untroubled journey. Where else can you eat well, sleep in comfort, feel safe and enjoy the scene while you are traveling at speed at the same time? And we are only at the beginning. We have entered the age of superfast trains, traveling at 150 miles an hour and more. Soon we will be wondering why spend so much on motorways we can’t use because we don’t have enough money to buy oil and planes we can’t fly for the same reason.
blocks.translation: 铁路远没有死，而是活得很好。现代铁路给你平稳、无忧的旅程。还有哪里能让你在高速行进的同时吃得好、睡得舒服、感到安全并欣赏风景？而且我们才刚刚开始。我们已经进入超高速列车时代，时速达到 150 英里甚至更高。很快我们就会纳闷：为什么要花那么多钱修我们无法使用的高速公路——因为我们没钱买油；又为什么要买同样因为没油而飞不起来的飞机。

articles.title: Airline companies are responsible for transporting your luggage
articles.fallbackTitle: Airline companies are responsible for transporting your luggage

blocks.text: Airline companies are responsible for transporting your luggage. If you cannot recover it at the point of arrival, you must inform the airline immediately. They will carry out the necessary search. If the luggage is recovered, it will be delivered to your place of residence. If you wish to insure your luggage, you may do so at your own expense.
blocks.translation: 航空公司负责运送你的行李。如果你在抵达地点无法取回行李，必须立即通知航空公司。他们会进行必要的查找。如果行李被找回，将会送到你的住处。如果你希望为行李投保，可以自费办理。

blocks.text: Some airlines restrict luggage weight to 44 pounds(20 kg); in other cases, there is no weight restriction, but you are not allowed more than two pieces of luggage. Inquire about luggage allowances from the airline with which you will be traveling. However, you must pay extra for excess luggage, which is not reimbursed(补偿) by Canadian International Development Agency(CIDA).
blocks.translation: 有些航空公司把行李重量限制在 44 磅（20 公斤）；另一些则没有重量限制，但不允许携带超过两件行李。请向你将乘坐的航空公司咨询行李额度。不过，超重行李必须额外付费，加拿大国际开发署（CIDA）不予补偿。

blocks.text: Each suitcase, bag or package must be clearly labeled with your name and destination. paragraphs: Airline companies are responsible for transporting your luggage. If you cannot recover it at the point of arrival, you must inform the airline immediately. They will carry out the necessary search. If the luggage is recovered, it will be delivered to your place of residence. If you wish to insure your luggage, you may do so at your own expense.

Some airlines restrict luggage weight to 44 pounds(20 kg); in other cases, there is no weight restriction, but you are not allowed more than two pieces of luggage. Inquire about luggage allowances from the airline with which you will be traveling. However, you must pay extra for excess luggage, which is not reimbursed(补偿) by Canadian International Development Agency(CIDA).

articles.title: Cars are an important part of life in the United States
articles.fallbackTitle: Cars are an important part of life in the United States

blocks.text: Cars are an important part of life in the United States. Without a car most people feel that they are poor. And even if a person is poor, he doesn’t feel really poor when he has a car.
blocks.translation: 汽车是美国生活的重要部分。没有车，多数人觉得自己很穷。即使一个人很穷，只要有车，他就不会觉得自己真的穷。

blocks.text: Henry Ford was the man who first started making cars in large numbers. He probably didn’t know how much the car was going to change American culture. The car made the United States a nation on wheels. And it helped make the United States what it is today.
blocks.translation: 亨利·福特是第一个开始大量生产汽车的人。他也许不知道汽车将如何改变美国文化。汽车使美国成为一个“车轮上的国家”，也帮助美国成为今天的样子。

blocks.text: There are three main reasons why the car became so popular in the United States. First of all, the country is a big one and Americans like to move around it. The car makes the travel the most comfortable and cheapest. With a car people can go to any place without spending a lot of money.
blocks.translation: 汽车在美国如此流行有三个主要原因。首先，这个国家很大，美国人喜欢四处走动。汽车使旅行成为最舒适、最便宜的方式。有车，人们可以不花很多钱就去任何地方。

blocks.text: The second reason cars are popular is the fact that the United States never really developed a practical and cheap public travel system. Long distance trains have never been as common in the United States as they are in other parts of the world. Now there is a good system of air-service provided by planes. But it is too expensive to be used often.
blocks.translation: 汽车流行的第二个原因，是美国从未真正发展出实用而廉价的公共交通系统。长途火车在美国从未像在世界其他地区那样普遍。现在有飞机提供的良好航空服务，但太贵，无法经常使用。

blocks.text: The third reason is the most important one, though. The American spirit of independence is what really made cars popular. Americans don’t like waiting for a bus, or a train or even a plane. They don’t like to have to follow an exact timetable. A car gives them the freedom to plan their own time. And this is the freedom that Americans want most to have.
blocks.translation: 不过第三个原因最重要。真正让汽车流行的是美国人的独立精神。美国人不喜欢等公交、等火车甚至等飞机。他们不喜欢必须遵守精确的时间表。汽车给了他们自由安排自己时间的自由，而这正是美国人最想要的自由。

blocks.text: Less oil has caused a big problem for Americans. But the answer will not be a bigger system of public transportation. The real answer will have to be a new kind of car, one that does not use so much oil.
blocks.translation: 石油减少给美国人带来了大问题。但答案不会是更大的公共交通系统。真正的答案必须是一种新型汽车——一种不消耗那么多石油的汽车。

articles.title: Men have traveled ever since they first appeared on the earth
articles.fallbackTitle: Men have traveled ever since they first appeared on the earth

blocks.text: Men have traveled ever since they first appeared on the earth.
blocks.translation: 自人类在地球上出现以来，就一直有人旅行。

blocks.text: In primitive times they did not travel for pleasure but to find new places where their herds could feed, or to escape from hostile neighbors, or to find more favorable climates. They traveled on foot. Their journeys were long, tiring, and often dangerous. They protected themselves with simple weapons, such as wooden sticks or stone clubs, and by lighting fires at night and, above all, by keeping together.
blocks.translation: 在原始时代，人们旅行不是为了消遣，而是为了寻找可供畜群吃草的新地方，或躲避怀有敌意的邻居，或寻找更宜人的气候。他们徒步而行，旅途漫长、疲惫，而且常常危险。他们用简单的武器保护自己，比如木棍或石棒，还在夜里点火，最重要的是结伴同行。

blocks.text: Being intelligent and creative, they soon discovered easier ways of traveling. They rode on the backs of their domesticated animals; they hollowed out tree trunks, and by using bits of wood as paddles, were able to travel across water. Later they traveled, not from necessity, but for the joy and excitement of seeing and experiencing new things. This is still the main reason why we travel today.
blocks.translation: 由于聪明而富有创造力，他们很快发现了更省力的出行方式。他们骑在家畜背上；他们把树干挖空，用木片当桨，就能渡水而行。后来，他们旅行不再出于需要，而是为了见识和体验新事物带来的快乐与兴奋。这至今仍是我们旅行的主要原因。

blocks.text: Traveling, of course, has now become a highly organized business. There are cars and splendid roads, express trains, huge ships and jet airliners, all of which provide us with comforts and security. This sounds wonderful. But there are difficulties, if you want to go abroad, you need a passport and a visa, tickets, luggage, and a hundred and one other things. If you lose any of them, your journey may be ruined.
blocks.translation: 当然，如今旅行已成为高度组织化的产业。有汽车和宽阔的道路、特快列车、巨轮和喷气式客机，它们为我们提供舒适与安全。这听起来很美妙。但也有麻烦：如果你想出国，就需要护照和签证、机票、行李，还有许许多多别的东西。一旦丢了其中任何一样，你的旅程就可能泡汤。

paragraphs: Men have traveled ever since they first appeared on the earth.

In primitive times they did not travel for pleasure but to find new places where their herds could feed, or to escape from hostile neighbors, or to find more favorable climates. They traveled on foot. Their journeys were long, tiring, and often dangerous. They protected themselves with simple weapons, such as wooden sticks or stone clubs, and by lighting fires at night and, above all, by keeping together.

Being intelligent and creative, they soon discovered easier ways of traveling. They rode on the backs of their domesticated animals; they hollowed out tree trunks, and by using bits of wood as paddles, were able to travel across water. Later they traveled, not from necessity, but for the joy and excitement of seeing and experiencing new things. This is still the main reason why we travel today.

Traveling, of course, has now become a highly organized business. There are cars and splendid roads, express trains, huge ships and jet airliners, all of which provide us with comforts and security. This sounds wonderful. But there are difficulties, if you want to go abroad, you need a passport and a visa, tickets, luggage, and a hundred and one other things. If you lose any of them, your journey may be ruined.

from necessity
to broaden the mind
to escape from the wild animals

articles.title: Most airlines allow passengers to book an airline flight online
articles.fallbackTitle: Most airlines allow passengers to book an airline flight online

blocks.text: Most airlines allow passengers to book an airline flight online. Travel sites such as Yahoo and Google, all offer search engines and online booking for an airline flight. The first thing a traveler should do when booking online is to shop around. There are numerous web sites offering this service, and some may have cheaper fares than others.
blocks.translation: 大多数航空公司允许乘客在线预订机票。雅虎、谷歌等旅行网站都提供搜索引擎和机票在线预订服务。旅客在线订票时，首先要做的就是货比三家。提供这类服务的网站很多，有些网站的票价可能比别家便宜。

blocks.text: A traveler also needs to check fares for the desired flight times. Fares can change, depending on when the airline flight departs, how many stops are involved, and at what airport. The traveler needs to make sure he is comparing fares so as to get the best deal.
blocks.translation: 旅客还需要查看所需航班时段的票价。票价会变化，取决于航班何时起飞、经停几次以及在哪个机场起降。旅客要确保自己是在比较票价，才能拿到最划算的交易。

blocks.text: When booking online, the traveler also needs to check the travel site’s policies and fees. Some sites charge a small booking fee and have other restrictions about canceling flights, and other types of fees. Many travelers think about looking on a travel search engine first for the best airline flight fares. However, the airline web site may offer the best deal, since they often have “Internet only” deals booked through their own sites.
blocks.translation: 在线订票时，旅客还需要查看旅行网站的政策和费用。有些网站会收取少量订票费，并对取消航班等设有其他限制，还会收取其他类型的费用。许多旅客会先到旅行搜索引擎上查找最优惠的机票价格。不过，航空公司自己的网站可能给出最划算的交易，因为它们常有通过自家网站预订的“仅限网络”优惠。

blocks.text: A traveler should always have a credit card available when he or she purchases the ticket, and make the reservation in the name appearing on the card. The traveler will then be issued an e-ticket for the airline flight, rather than the traditional paper ticket. When he receives flight confirmation, usually through e-mail, he should print out the reservation e-mail and save it with his travel documents.
blocks.translation: 旅客购票时应始终备好信用卡，并以卡上出现的姓名进行预订。之后旅客会收到电子机票，而不是传统的纸质机票。当他收到航班确认（通常通过电子邮件）时，应当把预订确认邮件打印出来，与旅行证件放在一起保存。

blocks.text: Once upon a time all you needed for a camping trip was a sleeping bag, a compass and some common sense. Now, according to my local sporting goods retailer, a lot more should be added. However, outdoor travel has become such a trend that urban people find themselves with some upscale retailers to address their every desire.
blocks.translation: 从前，一次露营之旅只需要一个睡袋、一个指南针和一点常识。如今，按我当地体育用品零售商的说法，还应该加上许多东西。然而，户外旅行已成潮流，城里人发现自己身边尽是高端零售商，来满足他们的每一个欲望。

blocks.text: “Eco” and “adventure” are the latest fashionable words in destination travel; those in the industry know they can make serious cash off all the consumers. These are consumers who get outdoors not for nature’s sake, but to work out simply for a splendid cocktail party.
blocks.translation: “生态”和“探险”是目的地旅行中最时髦的词；业内人士知道，他们能从所有这些消费者身上大赚一笔。这些消费者到户外不是为了自然，而只是为了锻炼一下，好在精彩的鸡尾酒会上有谈资。

blocks.text: As a result of high-end demand, the great outdoors is becoming less affordable and accessible for ordinary people. Our national parks used to be vast acres of wilderness where people could go and enjoy nature, for free. But over the past 100 years, the government has been slowly selling or leasing off public lands for profit, and our current president is continuing the trend. Large ski resorts have swallowed up plenty of wilderness and small towns in the West by attracting more high-end businesses. Nature is now a commodity that can be repackaged and sold to the wealthy developers. As for the small amount of public land left, well, try to remember the last time you camped at a state park for free.
blocks.translation: 由于高端需求，伟大的户外对普通人来说变得越来越昂贵、越来越难以企及。我们的国家公园曾是广袤的荒野，人们可以免费去享受自然。但在过去一百年里，政府一直在慢慢出售或出租公共土地牟利，现任总统也在延续这一趋势。大型滑雪度假村通过吸引更多高端商业，吞并了大量荒野和西部小镇。自然如今成了一种可以重新包装、卖给富有开发商的商品。至于剩下的一小部分公共土地，那就想想你上次免费在州立公园露营是什么时候吧。

blocks.text: The Joneses and everyone trying to keep up with them want a piece of the outdoors, but only with creature comforts included. The rest of us are being slowly priced out of nature. Pretty soon my tent and sleeping pack will be out of date; since camping will mean a luxury yurt with skylights for star-gazing. If this is what signifies experiencing nature in the new millennium, then Thoreau must be rolling in his grave.
blocks.translation: 琼斯一家以及所有想跟他们攀比的人都想分得户外的一杯羹，但必须附带舒适享受。我们其余的人正被慢慢挤出自然。很快，我的帐篷和睡袋就会过时，因为露营将意味着住进带天窗、可以观星的豪华蒙古包。如果这就是新千年体验自然的方式，那梭罗在坟墓里也要辗转反侧了。
