blocks.text: What are the beauties of Hawaii? Let’s start with four.
blocks.translation: 夏威夷的美在哪里？让我们从四处说起。

blocks.text: The beach, famous for its water temperature, air temperature and waves, is the first beauty. There are hundreds of miles of beaches on the twenty islands of Hawaii. They are thought to be among the finest beaches in the world.
blocks.translation: 海滩以水温、气温和海浪闻名，是第一美。夏威夷二十座岛上有数百英里海滩。它们被认为是世界上最美的海滩之一。

blocks.text: Then, what do you think would be the second beautiful thing? It is volcanoes (火山), of course. These volcanoes are not just a part of the islands; they made the islands in the first place. Because of them the islands are still growing.
blocks.translation: 那么，你认为第二美的是什么？当然是火山。这些火山不只是岛屿的一部分；它们最初造就了这些岛屿。正因为它们，岛屿至今仍在生长。

blocks.text: What would be the third thing of beauty that the first visitor to Hawaii would notice? It probably wouldn’t be just one thing, but many things: all the wonderful fruits and flowers of the islands. Sugar cane, bananas and pineapples are Hawaii’s biggest exports. Sugar cane has been growing in Hawaii for a thousand years. As for pineapples, the islands produce more than any other places in the world, which has made Dole Company the biggest fruit-packing company in the world.
blocks.translation: 初到夏威夷的游客会注意到的第三美是什么？可能不止一样，而是许多样：岛上所有美妙的水果和花卉。甘蔗、香蕉和菠萝是夏威夷最大的出口产品。甘蔗在夏威夷已种植一千年。至于菠萝，这些岛屿的产量超过世界其他任何地方，这使都乐公司成为世界上最大的水果包装公司。

blocks.text: The fourth and most beautiful thing about Hawaii is the people who live there. The Hawaiians never rush, and perhaps this is because they care more for human life than they care for the machine. There is an old Hawaiian law that a man can go to sleep in the middle of the road if he wants to. What makes the people of Hawaii so beautiful is their feeling about people. There are 64 different combinations of races on the islands, and they all live in peace. They believe “Above all nations is humanity.” That is the most beautiful thing of all.
blocks.translation: 夏威夷第四美，也是最美的一处，是住在那里的人。夏威夷人从不匆忙，也许这是因为他们更看重人而不是机器。夏威夷有一条古老的法律：一个人愿意的话，可以睡在马路中间。夏威夷人之所以如此美好，在于他们对人的情感。岛上有 64 种不同的种族组合，他们全都和平相处。他们相信“人性高于一切民族”。那才是最美好的事。

articles.title: The U
articles.fallbackTitle: The U

blocks.text: The U. S. Travel Association confirmed in a survey what many frustrated fliers already know: The No. 1 airport headache is passengers who pull too many carry-on bags through security and onto flights.
blocks.translation: 美国旅游协会在一项调查中证实了许多沮丧的飞行者早已知道的事：机场头号烦心事是乘客带太多随身行李过安检、上飞机。

blocks.text: That number has skyrocketed in recent years—86 million more bags were carried on in the year than during the same period two years earlier, the Transportation Security Administration estimates.
blocks.translation: 这个数字近年来猛增——据运输安全管理局估计，这一年随身携带的行李比两年前同期多了 8600 万件。

blocks.text: The reason for the carry-on jump is no mystery: All the major domestic airlines now charge to check (托运) even one bag, generally $25. To save money and time at the baggage claim, passengers carry as much as they can on board, with predictable consequences.
blocks.translation: 随身行李激增的原因并不神秘：国内所有主要航空公司现在连一件托运行李都要收费，通常 25 美元。为了省钱、也为了在行李提取处省时间，乘客尽可能多地把东西带上飞机，后果可想而知。

blocks.text: At security checkpoints, these millions of extra bags, many of them densely packed, mean longer lines. Once past security, the fun continues at boarding. On a typical flight, there’s a fierce fight for scarce overhead bin space, extending the boarding process. Bags that are stuffed under seats make passengers even more uncomfortable.
blocks.translation: 在安检口，这数百万件额外行李（许多塞得密不透风）意味着更长的队伍。过了安检，好戏在登机时继续。在典型航班上，人们为稀缺的头顶行李架空间激烈争抢，拖长了登机过程。塞在座位下的包让乘客更加不舒服。

blocks.text: There has got to be a better way. In fact, there is. Here’s what a more sensible system would look like:
blocks.translation: 一定有更好的办法。事实上确实有。一个更合理的制度应该是这样：

blocks.text: No fee for the first piece of checked luggage. It would be better if airlines simply raised fares instead of fees. Limit the carry-on size and charge for large carry-ons. Use templates (模板) at the security checkpoints to cut off the monster bags that now often escape airline staff’s notice until they’re right at the door of the plane. Tax the airlines’ income from fees the same way that fares are taxed. Currently, the fees are tax free, encouraging airlines to generate income through fees rather than fare increases.
blocks.translation: 第一件托运行李免费。航空公司直接提高票价，而不是收费，会更好。限制随身行李尺寸，对大件随身行李收费。在安检口使用模板，拦下那些如今常常逃过航空公司员工注意、直到机舱门口才被发现的大件行李。对航空公司的行李费收入像对票价一样征税。目前这些费用免税，反而鼓励航空公司通过收费而不是提价来创收。

blocks.text: We’re sympathetic to the airline industry’s need to make money, but the baggage fees—previously intended to offset rising fuel costs—have become an interruption that slows down the security check, offloads costs onto fliers and makes the boarding process even more unpleasant than it already is.
blocks.translation: 我们同情航空业赚钱的需要，但行李费——原本是为了抵消不断上涨的燃油成本——已经变成一种干扰：拖慢安检、把成本转嫁给乘客，并让本就令人不快的登机过程更加难受。

paragraphs: The U. S. Travel Association confirmed in a survey what many frustrated fliers already know: The No. 1 airport headache is passengers who pull too many carry-on bags through security and onto flights.
That number has skyrocketed in recent years—86 million more bags were carried on in the year than during the same period two years earlier, the Transportation Security Administration estimates.

The reason for the carry-on jump is no mystery: All the major domestic airlines now charge to check (托运) even one bag, generally $25. To save money and time at the baggage claim, passengers carry as much as they can on board, with predictable consequences.

At security checkpoints, these millions of extra bags, many of them densely packed, mean longer lines. Once past security, the fun continues at boarding. On a typical flight, there’s a fierce fight for scarce overhead bin space, extending the boarding process. Bags that are stuffed under seats make passengers even more uncomfortable.
There has got to be a better way. In fact, there is. Here’s what a more sensible system would look like:

No fee for the first piece of checked luggage. It would be better if airlines simply raised fares instead of fees. Limit the carry-on size and charge for large carry-ons. Use templates (模板) at the security checkpoints to cut off the monster bags that now often escape airline staff’s notice until they’re right at the door of the plane. Tax the airlines’ income from fees the same way that fares are taxed. Currently, the fees are tax free, encouraging airlines to generate income through fees rather than fare increases.

We’re sympathetic to the airline industry’s need to make money, but the baggage fees—previously intended to offset rising fuel costs—have become an interruption that slows down the security check, offloads costs onto fliers and makes the boarding process even more unpleasant than it already is.

questions.evidence: We're sympathetic to the airline industry's need to make money

translations: 美国旅游协会在一项调查中证实了许多沮丧的飞行者早已知道的事：机场头号烦心事是乘客带太多随身行李过安检、上飞机。
这个数字近年来猛增——据运输安全管理局估计，这一年随身携带的行李比两年前同期多了 8600 万件。
随身行李激增的原因并不神秘：国内所有主要航空公司现在连一件托运行李都要收费，通常 25 美元。为了省钱、也为了在行李提取处省时间，乘客尽可能多地把东西带上飞机，后果可想而知。
在安检口，这数百万件额外行李（许多塞得密不透风）意味着更长的队伍。过了安检，好戏在登机时继续。在典型航班上，人们为稀缺的头顶行李架空间激烈争抢，拖长了登机过程。塞在座位下的包让乘客更加不舒服。
一定有更好的办法。事实上确实有。一个更合理的制度应该是这样：
第一件托运行李免费。航空公司直接提高票价，而不是收费，会更好。限制随身行李尺寸，对大件随身行李收费。在安检口使用模板，拦下那些如今常常逃过航空公司员工注意、直到机舱门口才被发现的大件行李。对航空公司的行李费收入像对票价一样征税。目前这些费用免税，反而鼓励航空公司通过收费而不是提价来创收。
我们同情航空业赚钱的需要，但行李费——原本是为了抵消不断上涨的燃油成本——已经变成一种干扰：拖慢安检、把成本转嫁给乘客，并让本就令人不快的登机过程更加难受。

articles.title: Every year there is the Spring Festival in China
articles.fallbackTitle: Every year there is the Spring Festival in China

blocks.text: Every year there is the Spring Festival in China. Usually it is in January or February. It is the most important festival in China. So before it comes, everyone has to prepare things. They buy beef, pork, chicken, fruit and many other things. And they often make a special kind of food called “dumplings”. It means “come together” in Chinese. On the day before the festival, parents buy new clothes for their children and children also buy presents for their parents. On the festival eve, all the family members come back to their home. This is a happy moment. They sing, dance and play cards. When they enjoy the meal, they give each other the best wishes for the coming year. They all have a good time.
blocks.translation: 每年中国都有春节，通常在 1 月或 2 月。它是中国最重要的节日。所以春节到来之前，每个人都要做准备。人们买牛肉、猪肉、鸡肉、水果和许多其他东西，还常常做一种叫“饺子”的特殊食物。饺子在中文里寓意“团聚”。节前一天，父母给孩子买新衣服，孩子也会给父母买礼物。除夕之夜，全家人都会回到家里。这是一个快乐的时刻。他们唱歌、跳舞、打牌。吃饭时，他们互致来年的美好祝愿。大家都过得很开心。

articles.title: The Winter Olympics is also called the White Olympics
articles.fallbackTitle: The Winter Olympics is also called the White Olympics

blocks.text: The Winter Olympics is also called the White Olympics. At this time, many colorful stamps are published to mark the great Games. The first stamps marking the opening came out on January 25, 1932 in the United States for the 3rd White Olympics. From then on, publishing stamps during the White Olympics became a rule.
blocks.translation: 冬季奥运会也被称为“白色奥运会”。届时，许多色彩鲜艳的邮票会发行，以纪念这一体育盛会。第一套纪念奥运会开幕的邮票于 1932 年 1 月 25 日在美国发行，纪念第三届白色奥运会。从那时起，在白色奥运会期间发行邮票便成了一项惯例。

blocks.text: During the 4th Winter Olympic Games a group of stamps were published in Germany in November 1936. The five rings of Olympics were sewn(缝制)on the front of the sportswear. It was the first time that the rings appeared on the stamps of the White Olympics.
blocks.translation: 1936 年 11 月，德国发行了一组邮票纪念第四届冬季奥运会。奥运五环被缝制在运动服的前面。这是五环首次出现在白色奥运会的邮票上。

blocks.text: In the 1950’s, the stamps of this kind became more colorful. When the White Olympics came, the host countries as well as the non-host countries published stamps to mark those Games. China also published four stamps in February 1980, when the Chinese sportsmen began to take part in the White Olympics.
blocks.translation: 20 世纪 50 年代，这类邮票变得更加色彩丰富。白色奥运会举办时，主办国和非主办国都会发行邮票来纪念这些赛事。1980 年 2 月，当中国运动员开始参加白色奥运会时，中国也发行了四枚邮票。

blocks.text: Japan is the only Asian country that has ever held the White Olympics. Altogether 14, 500 million stamps were sold to raise money for this sports meet.
blocks.translation: 日本是唯一举办过白色奥运会的亚洲国家，共售出 145 亿枚邮票，为这届运动会筹集资金。

blocks.text: Different kinds of sports were drawn on these small stamps. People can enjoy the beauty of the wonderful movements of some sportsmen.
blocks.translation: 这些小邮票上绘制了各种不同的运动项目。人们可以欣赏到一些运动员优美动作的美感。

During the 4th Winter Olympic Games a group of stamps were published in Germany in November 1936. The five rings of Olympics were sewn(缝制)on the front of the sportswear. It was the first time that the rings appeared on the stamps of the White Olympics.

China also published four stamps in February 1980, when the Chinese sportsmen began to take part in the White Olympics.

articles.title: Finally, the Christmas season is over
articles.fallbackTitle: Finally, the Christmas season is over

blocks.text: Finally, the Christmas season is over. We can take a long breath, put up our feet, sip from a cup of good tea and relax. The frenzy, starting from Black Friday right after Thanksgiving until Christmas Eve, of gift shopping, buying, wrapping, giving, receiving, opening, returning…is exhausting and time-consuming, but it takes place every year.
blocks.translation: 圣诞季终于结束了。我们可以长舒一口气，把脚翘起来，啜一口好茶，放松一下。从感恩节后的“黑色星期五”一直到圣诞前夜的这阵疯狂——买礼物、购物、包装、送礼、收礼、拆礼、退货……——既累人又费时，但每年都会上演。

blocks.text: There is considerable difference between the cultures in China and western countries when it comes to gift giving. In China, it is not polite to open a gift in front of the gift giver, and the gift is only looked at after the guest has left. Here in America, gift givers always wrap their gifts, large or small, priceless or valueless, carefully and decorate them with colorful ribbons and little pretty paper flowers; and the lucky receiver is expected to open the gift right away in front of the giver, with great eagerness and curiosity, and should always express appreciation with the all time truthful comment, “this is just exactly what I wanted!” Well, as a matter of fact, most people would take their “always wanted” gifts back to the store to exchange for something they really wanted.
blocks.translation: 在送礼这件事上，中国和西方国家的文化有相当大的差异。在中国，当着送礼人的面拆礼物是不礼貌的，礼物要等客人离开后才会被查看。而在美国，送礼人总会仔细包装礼物，无论大小、贵重与否，还会用彩色丝带和小巧的纸花装饰；幸运的收礼人则应当当着送礼人的面，带着极大的热切和好奇立刻打开礼物，并且总要表达赞赏，说一句永远“真实”的评价：“这正是我想要的！”嗯，事实上，大多数人会把他们“一直想要”的礼物拿回商店，换成自己真正想要的东西。

blocks.text: Finding a gift for somebody, even a close family member, you will have to know what the person likes and shop for days before you can locate the perfect gift. But, still the person may not like the gift from you. Nowadays, stores would provide two copies of the receipts for anything they sell as a gift, one of which is included in the gift package so that the receiver can come back for an exchange. I know, it was unthinkable to cash out the gift you get, but times are different. Another good way to avoid all that shopping hassle is to purchase a gift card from one of the stores and send it to your niece, nephews, or a family member, so that they can get whatever they want or even keep the money.
blocks.translation: 为别人找礼物，哪怕是关系亲密的家人，你也得知道对方喜欢什么，还要花好几天去逛，才能找到完美的礼物。但即便如此，对方可能还是不喜欢你送的礼物。如今，商店出售作为礼物的商品时通常会提供两份收据，其中一份放进礼物包装里，以便收礼人回来换货。我知道，把收到的礼物变现曾是不可想象的，但时代不同了。另一个避免这些购物麻烦的好办法是从某家商店买一张礼品卡，送给你的侄女、侄子或家人，这样他们就能想要什么买什么，甚至把钱留着。

paragraphs: Finally, the Christmas season is over. We can take a long breath, put up our feet, sip from a cup of good tea and relax. The frenzy, starting from Black Friday right after Thanksgiving until Christmas Eve, of gift shopping, buying, wrapping, giving, receiving, opening, returning…is exhausting and time-consuming, but it takes place every year.

There is considerable difference between the cultures in China and western countries when it comes to gift giving. In China, it is not polite to open a gift in front of the gift giver, and the gift is only looked at after the guest has left. Here in America, gift givers always wrap their gifts, large or small, priceless or valueless, carefully and decorate them with colorful ribbons and little pretty paper flowers; and the lucky receiver is expected to open the gift right away in front of the giver, with great eagerness and curiosity, and should always express appreciation with the all time truthful comment, “this is just exactly what I wanted!” Well, as a matter of fact, most people would take their “always wanted” gifts back to the store to exchange for something they really wanted.

Finding a gift for somebody, even a close family member, you will have to know what the person likes and shop for days before you can locate the perfect gift. But, still the person may not like the gift from you. Nowadays, stores would provide two copies of the receipts for anything they sell as a gift, one of which is included in the gift package so that the receiver can come back for an exchange. I know, it was unthinkable to cash out the gift you get, but times are different. Another good way to avoid all that shopping hassle is to purchase a gift card from one of the stores and send it to your niece, nephews, or a family member, so that they can get whatever they want or even keep the money.

translations: 圣诞季终于结束了。我们可以长舒一口气，把脚翘起来，啜一口好茶，放松一下。从感恩节后的“黑色星期五”一直到圣诞前夜的这阵疯狂——买礼物、购物、包装、送礼、收礼、拆礼、退货……——既累人又费时，但每年都会上演。

在送礼这件事上，中国和西方国家的文化有相当大的差异。在中国，当着送礼人的面拆礼物是不礼貌的，礼物要等客人离开后才会被查看。而在美国，送礼人总会仔细包装礼物，无论大小、贵重与否，还会用彩色丝带和小巧的纸花装饰；幸运的收礼人则应当当着送礼人的面，带着极大的热切和好奇立刻打开礼物，并且总要表达赞赏，说一句永远“真实”的评价：“这正是我想要的！”嗯，事实上，大多数人会把他们“一直想要”的礼物拿回商店，换成自己真正想要的东西。

为别人找礼物，哪怕是关系亲密的家人，你也得知道对方喜欢什么，还要花好几天去逛，才能找到完美的礼物。但即便如此，对方可能还是不喜欢你送的礼物。如今，商店出售作为礼物的商品时通常会提供两份收据，其中一份放进礼物包装里，以便收礼人回来换货。我知道，把收到的礼物变现曾是不可想象的，但时代不同了。另一个避免这些购物麻烦的好办法是从某家商店买一张礼品卡，送给你的侄女、侄子或家人，这样他们就能想要什么买什么，甚至把钱留着。

blocks.text: Are you interested in country music? I like it very much! It will take me away for a while when I am tired. The guitars and songs will take me to the mountains and fields.
blocks.translation: 你对乡村音乐感兴趣吗？我非常喜欢它！疲惫的时候，它能带我离开一会儿。吉他和歌声会把我带到山间和田野。

blocks.text: Country music usually talks of everyday life and feeling. It’s the spirit of America, easy to understand, slow and simple.
blocks.translation: 乡村音乐通常歌唱日常生活和情感。它是美国的精神，通俗易懂，缓慢而简单。

blocks.text: Country music developed in the Southern United States. It was folk music of American countryside. Many songs tell about the lives of farmers. They talk about love, crops or death.
blocks.translation: 乡村音乐发展于美国南部。它是美国乡村的民间音乐。许多歌曲讲述农民的生活，唱的是爱情、庄稼或死亡。

blocks.text: The life of the countryside can be hard, so the words in country music are often sad. At first, people played the music only at family parties. But it became more popular later. In the 1920s, people played country songs on the radio and they made them into the records.
blocks.translation: 乡村生活可能很艰苦，所以乡村音乐的歌词常常带着忧伤。起初，人们只在家庭聚会上演奏这种音乐，后来它越来越受欢迎。20 世纪 20 年代，人们在广播里播放乡村歌曲，并把它们录成唱片。

blocks.text: When people in the countryside moved to towns and cities to look for work, they took their music with them. Country music continued to change and became popular across America.
blocks.translation: 当乡下人搬到城镇寻找工作时，他们把音乐也带到了那里。乡村音乐不断变化，并在全美流行起来。

blocks.text: John Denver was one of America’s most famous country singers in the 1970s. His song “Take Me Home, Country Roads ” is well-known and people still play it today.

articles.title: In ancient times wealth was measured and exchanged in things that could be touched: food,
articles.fallbackTitle: In ancient times wealth was measured and exchanged in things that could be touched: food,

blocks.text: In ancient times wealth was measured and exchanged in things that could be touched: food, tools, and precious metals and stones. Then the barter system was replaced by coins, which still had real value since they were pieces of rare metal. Coins were followed by fiat money, paper notes that have value only because everyone agrees to accept them.
blocks.translation: 在古代，财富是用可以触摸的东西来衡量和交换的：食物、工具以及贵金属和宝石。后来，以物易物制度被硬币取代，硬币仍然具有真实价值，因为它们是由稀有金属制成的。继硬币之后出现的是法定货币，即纸币，它之所以有价值，只是因为大家都同意接受它。

blocks.text: Today electronic monetary systems are gradually being introduced that will transform money into even less tangible forms, reducing it to a series of “bits and bytes”, or units of computerized information, going between machines at the speed of light. Already, electronic fund transfer allows money to be instantly sent and received by different banks, companies, and countries through computers and telecommunications devices.
blocks.translation: 如今，电子货币系统正逐渐被引入，它将把货币变成更加无形的形式，使其简化为一系列“比特和字节”，即计算机化信息的单位，以光速在机器之间传递。电子资金转账已经可以让资金通过计算机和电信设备在不同银行、公司和国家之间即时收发。

Coins were followed by fiat money, paper notes that have value only because everyone agrees to accept them.

Today electronic monetary systems are gradually being introduced that will transform money into even less tangible forms, reducing it to a series of “bits and bytes”, or units of computerized information, going between machines at the speed of light. Already, electronic fund transfer allows money to be instantly sent and received by different banks, companies, and countries through computers and telecommunications devices.

articles.title: Some people hate everything that is modern
articles.fallbackTitle: Some people hate everything that is modern

blocks.text: Some people hate everything that is modern. They cannot imagine how anyone can really like modern music; they find it hard to accept the new fashions in clothing; they think that all modern paintings are ugly; and they seldom have a good word for the new buildings that are being built everywhere in the world. Such people look for perfection in everything, and they take their standards of perfection from the past. They are usually impatient with anyone who is brave enough to experiment with new things or to express himself or the age in original ways.
blocks.translation: 有些人憎恨一切现代的东西。他们无法想象怎么会有人真的喜欢现代音乐；他们觉得很难接受新款式的服装；他们认为所有现代绘画都很丑；对于世界各地正在建造的新建筑，他们也很少说一句好话。这样的人凡事都追求完美，而他们的完美标准来自过去。对于那些勇于尝试新事物或以原创方式表达自我、表达时代的人，他们通常很不耐烦。

blocks.text: It is, of course, true that many artists do not succeed in their work and instead produce works that can only be considered as failures. If the work of art is a painting, the artist’s failure concerns himself alone, but if it is a building, his failure concerns others too. Because it may damage the beauty of the whole place. This does sometimes happen, but it is completely untrue to say, as some people do, that modern architecture is nothing.
blocks.translation: 当然，许多艺术家确实没有在作品中取得成功，反而创作出只能被视为失败的作品。如果艺术作品是一幅画，艺术家的失败只关乎他自己；但如果是一座建筑，他的失败也会影响别人，因为它可能破坏整个地方的美感。这种情况确实有时会发生，但像有些人那样说现代建筑一无是处，则是完全不正确的。

blocks.text: We can’t judge every modern building by the standards of the ancient time, even though we admire the ancient buildings. Technologically, the modern buildings are more advanced. The modern architect knows he should learn from the ancient works, but with his greater resources of knowledge and materials, he will never be content to imitate the past. He is too proud to do that.
blocks.translation: 即使我们欣赏古代建筑，也不能用古代的标准来评判每一座现代建筑。从技术上讲，现代建筑更先进。现代建筑师知道自己应该向古代作品学习，但凭借更丰富的知识和材料资源，他绝不会满足于模仿过去。他太骄傲了，不会那样做。

articles.title: Anthropology (人类学) is the study of how people live
articles.fallbackTitle: Anthropology (人类学) is the study of how people live

blocks.text: Anthropology (人类学) is the study of how people live. It includes their family life, religion, laws and language. The term “anthropology” comes from two Greek words: “anthropos” means “human being” and “logy” means “the science of”. Anthropology can be divided into two areas. These two main divisions are cultural anthropology and physical anthropology.
blocks.translation: 人类学是研究人们如何生活的学科。它包括人们的家庭生活、宗教、法律和语言。“anthropology”一词来自两个希腊词：“anthropos”意为“人”，“logy”意为“……学”。人类学可分为两个领域，这两个主要分支是文化人类学和体质人类学。

blocks.text: Anthropologists define human progress in three main steps. Step one begins with the first human being and continues until the last of people who hunted animals just to survive. Step two includes people who grew food. In this step, there was progress in invention and religion. Step three deals with first civilizations, such as those in Egypt and parts of Asia.
blocks.translation: 人类学家把人类进步划分为三个主要阶段。第一阶段从最早的人类开始，一直延续到最后一批只为生存而猎捕动物的人。第二阶段包括种植食物的人。在这一阶段，发明和宗教都有所进步。第三阶段涉及最早的文明，例如埃及和亚洲部分地区的文明。

blocks.text: Anthropologists always seek new information about people. For instance, recent evidence found in Ethiopia and Kenya shows humans existed earlier in history than it was previously believed.
blocks.translation: 人类学家总是寻求关于人的新信息。例如，最近在埃塞俄比亚和肯尼亚发现的证据表明，人类在历史上存在的时间比人们以前认为的更早。

These two main divisions are cultural anthropology and physical anthropology.

Step two includes people who grew food. In this step, there was progress in invention and religion. Step three deals with first civilizations, such as those in Egypt and parts of Asia.

articles.fallbackTitle: Benjamin Franklin was born in 1706 in Boston, Massachusetts

blocks.text: Benjamin Franklin was born in 1706 in Boston, Massachusetts. His mother and father were Puritans (清教徒). They left England and moved to the English colony of Massachusetts in order to escape persecution (迫害) for their religion. In Boston, Franklin left school when he was ten years old and worked for his father for two years. Then he went to work on his brother’s newspaper. He became the editor of this paper when he was sixteen. Because he wanted to be independent, he went to Philadelphia. There he began his own newspaper. He worked hard and saved his money. And by the age of 24, he was one of the most successful men in Philadelphia.
blocks.translation: 本杰明·富兰克林 1706 年出生于马萨诸塞州的波士顿。他的父母是清教徒。为了逃避宗教迫害，他们离开英国，搬到英国殖民地马萨诸塞。在波士顿，富兰克林十岁时辍学，为父亲工作了两年。之后他去哥哥的报社工作，十六岁时成为这份报纸的编辑。因为想要独立，他去了费城。在那里，他创办了自己的报纸。他努力工作，节省开支。到 24 岁时，他已成为费城最成功的人士之一。

blocks.text: In 1732, Franklin published a book Poor Richard’s Almanac (穷理查年鉴). Most almanacs contained information for farmers, such as information about the days and weeks of the year and about the weather. To his almanacs, Franklin added wise sayings and his observations about life. Some of these sayings are still famous today. For example, “Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.” “Waste not, want not.” and “A penny saved is a penny earned.”
blocks.translation: 1732 年，富兰克林出版了《穷理查年鉴》。大多数年鉴包含供农民使用的信息，比如一年中的日期、周次以及天气信息。富兰克林在自己的年鉴中加入了格言和对生活的观察。其中一些格言至今仍然著名，例如：“早睡早起使人健康、富有、明智。”“不浪费，不愁缺。”以及“省下一便士就是赚到一便士。”

blocks.text: For millions of people around the world, the very word “Christmas” brings warmth and joy to their hearts and homes. To some, it is simply a very popular holiday. But for many, it honors the birth of Jesus Christ. Here is a brief history of Christmas, and some of the traditions connected with it.
blocks.translation: 对全世界数百万人来说，“圣诞节”这个词本身就给他们的心灵和家庭带来温暖与欢乐。对一些人来说，它只是一个很受欢迎的节日；但对许多人来说，它是纪念耶稣基督的诞生。以下是圣诞节的简史，以及与之相关的一些传统。

blocks.text: Why December 25th?
blocks.translation: 为什么是 12 月 25 日？

blocks.text: Well, during the first two centuries after Jesus’ death, Christmas was not celebrated at all. Various attempts were made to determine the date of birth of Jesus, and at first, May 20th became the favored date. By the middle of the fourth century, however, Pope Julius selected December 25th as the day on which to celebrate Christ’s birth. Before that, December 25th had been a widely celebrated day in the Roman world. On that date, people honored a Roman sun god. Many modern Christmas customs, such as having a tree in the house and preparing special meals, came from this ancient celebration.
blocks.translation: 在耶稣去世后的最初两个世纪里，人们根本不庆祝圣诞节。人们曾多次尝试确定耶稣的出生日期，起初 5 月 20 日成为受青睐的日期。然而到四世纪中叶，教皇尤利乌斯选定 12 月 25 日作为庆祝基督诞生的日子。在此之前，12 月 25 日在罗马世界已是一个广泛庆祝的日子。在那一天，人们纪念罗马的太阳神。许多现代圣诞习俗，比如在家里摆一棵树、准备特别的饭菜，都来自这一古老的庆祝活动。

blocks.text: Let’s decorate the tree!
blocks.translation: 我们来装饰圣诞树吧！

blocks.text: The Christmas tree tradition was started in Germany in the late fifteenth century. At that time, there was a popular theater play which included a fir tree hung with apples. Today, more than 80 percent of American families buy and decorate a tree at Christmas.
blocks.translation: 圣诞树的传统始于 15 世纪末的德国。当时有一出很受欢迎的戏剧，剧中有一棵挂着苹果的冷杉树。如今，超过 80% 的美国家庭会在圣诞节购买并装饰圣诞树。

blocks.text: How many Christmas cards do you usually send?
blocks.translation: 你通常寄多少张圣诞贺卡？

blocks.text: The first commercial Christmas cards were made in London in 1843. A rich man paid an artist to design a card. He then proudly sent it to his friends and relatives to wish them a “Merry Christmas”. It was a good idea and it soon caught on. Today, Americans exchange millions of Christmas cards every year.
blocks.translation: 第一批商业圣诞贺卡于 1843 年在伦敦制作。一位富人花钱请艺术家设计了一张贺卡，然后自豪地寄给亲友，祝他们“圣诞快乐”。这是个好主意，很快流行起来。如今，美国人每年交换数百万张圣诞贺卡。

blocks.text: Santa Claus is coming to town!
blocks.translation: 圣诞老人进城啦！

blocks.text: St. Nicholas was the original Santa Claus or “Father Christmas”. He was widely known as a kind man who loved children. After his death, a story developed that he used to visit children on Christmas Eve and give them presents. When the Dutch people came to live in America many years ago, they brought their St. Nicholas, or Sinterklaas in Dutch, with them. Sinterklaas is therefore where we get the name Santa Claus.
blocks.translation: 圣尼古拉斯就是最初的圣诞老人，或称“圣诞之父”。他广为人知，是一位喜爱孩子的善良之人。他去世后，流传出一个故事，说他常在圣诞前夜探望孩子并送他们礼物。许多年前荷兰人来到美国定居时，也带来了他们的圣尼古拉斯，荷兰语叫 Sinterklaas。Santa Claus 这个名字正是由 Sinterklaas 演变而来。

blocks.text: What’s in that stocking?
blocks.translation: 圣诞袜里装的是什么？

blocks.text: According to the story, the practice of hanging up stockings is connected with St. Nicholas. It is believed that St. Nicholas learned about a man who was hopelessly in debt. He also learned that the man and his daughters were about to be sold as slaves. Nicholas went to the man’s home at night and threw a bag of gold through the man’s window. The bag of gold landed in one of the daughters’ stockings that had been hung up to dry.
blocks.translation: 根据传说，挂圣诞袜的习俗与圣尼古拉斯有关。据说圣尼古拉斯得知有一个人债台高筑、走投无路，还得知这个人和他的女儿们即将被卖为奴隶。尼古拉斯夜里来到那人家中，从窗户扔进一袋金币。这袋金币正好落进其中一个女儿挂起来晾干的袜子里。

blocks.text: Today, all the above traditions are still kept as ways of celebrating Christmas.
blocks.translation: 如今，上述所有传统仍作为庆祝圣诞节的方式保留着。

Before that, December 25th had been a widely celebrated day in the Roman world. On that date, people honored a Roman sun god. Many modern Christmas customs, such as having a tree in the house and preparing special meals, came from this ancient celebration.
Let’s decorate the tree!

The Christmas tree tradition was started in Germany in the late fifteenth century. At that time, there was a popular theater play which included a fir tree hung with apples. Today, more than 80 percent of American families buy and decorate a tree at Christmas.
How many Christmas cards do you usually send?

The first commercial Christmas cards were made in London in 1843. A rich man paid an artist to design a card. He then proudly sent it to his friends and relatives to wish them a “Merry Christmas”. It was a good idea and it soon caught on. Today, Americans exchange millions of Christmas cards every year.
Santa Claus is coming to town!

St. Nicholas was the original Santa Claus or “Father Christmas”. He was widely known as a kind man who loved children. After his death, a story developed that he used to visit children on Christmas Eve and give them presents. When the Dutch people came to live in America many years ago, they brought their St. Nicholas, or Sinterklaas in Dutch, with them. Sinterklaas is therefore where we get the name Santa Claus.
What’s in that stocking?

According to the story, the practice of hanging up stockings is connected with St. Nicholas. It is believed that St. Nicholas learned about a man who was hopelessly in debt. He also learned that the man and his daughters were about to be sold as slaves. Nicholas went to the man’s home at night and threw a bag of gold through the man’s window. The bag of gold landed in one of the daughters’ stockings that had been hung up to dry.
Today, all the above traditions are still kept as ways of celebrating Christmas.

translations: 对全世界数百万人来说，“圣诞节”这个词本身就给他们的心灵和家庭带来温暖与欢乐。对一些人来说，它只是一个很受欢迎的节日；但对许多人来说，它是纪念耶稣基督的诞生。以下是圣诞节的简史，以及与之相关的一些传统。
为什么是 12 月 25 日？
在耶稣去世后的最初两个世纪里，人们根本不庆祝圣诞节。人们曾多次尝试确定耶稣的出生日期，起初 5 月 20 日成为受青睐的日期。然而到四世纪中叶，教皇尤利乌斯选定 12 月 25 日作为庆祝基督诞生的日子。在此之前，12 月 25 日在罗马世界已是一个广泛庆祝的日子。在那一天，人们纪念罗马的太阳神。许多现代圣诞习俗，比如在家里摆一棵树、准备特别的饭菜，都来自这一古老的庆祝活动。
我们来装饰圣诞树吧！
圣诞树的传统始于 15 世纪末的德国。当时有一出很受欢迎的戏剧，剧中有一棵挂着苹果的冷杉树。如今，超过 80% 的美国家庭会在圣诞节购买并装饰圣诞树。
你通常寄多少张圣诞贺卡？
第一批商业圣诞贺卡于 1843 年在伦敦制作。一位富人花钱请艺术家设计了一张贺卡，然后自豪地寄给亲友，祝他们“圣诞快乐”。这是个好主意，很快流行起来。如今，美国人每年交换数百万张圣诞贺卡。
圣诞老人进城啦！
圣尼古拉斯就是最初的圣诞老人，或称“圣诞之父”。他广为人知，是一位喜爱孩子的善良之人。他去世后，流传出一个故事，说他常在圣诞前夜探望孩子并送他们礼物。许多年前荷兰人来到美国定居时，也带来了他们的圣尼古拉斯，荷兰语叫 Sinterklaas。Santa Claus 这个名字正是由 Sinterklaas 演变而来。
圣诞袜里装的是什么？
根据传说，挂圣诞袜的习俗与圣尼古拉斯有关。据说圣尼古拉斯得知有一个人债台高筑、走投无路，还得知这个人和他的女儿们即将被卖为奴隶。尼古拉斯夜里来到那人家中，从窗户扔进一袋金币。这袋金币正好落进其中一个女儿挂起来晾干的袜子里。
如今，上述所有传统仍作为庆祝圣诞节的方式保留着。

blocks.text: On November 19, 1863, Abraham Lincoln went to Gettysburg in Pennsylvania to speak at the National Soldiers Cemetery. The Civil War was still going on. There was much criticism of President Lincoln at the time. He was not at all popular. He had been invited to speak at Gettysburg only out of courtesy. The principal speaker was to be Edward Everett, a famous statesman and speaker of the day. Everett was a handsome man and very popular everywhere.
blocks.translation: 1863 年 11 月 19 日，亚伯拉罕·林肯前往宾夕法尼亚州的葛底斯堡，在国家士兵公墓发表演讲。当时内战仍在进行。那时人们对林肯总统有很多批评，他一点也不受欢迎。他受邀到葛底斯堡演讲只是出于礼节。主要演讲者是当时著名的政治家和演说家爱德华·埃弗雷特。埃弗雷特相貌英俊，到处都很受欢迎。

blocks.text: It is said that Lincoln prepared his speech on the train while going to Gettysburg. Late that night, alone in his hotel room and tired out, he again worked briefly on the speech. The next day Everett spoke first. He spoke for an hour and 57 minutes. His speech was a perfect example of the rich oratory of the day. Then Lincoln rose. The crowd of 15,000 people at first paid little attention to him. He spoke for only nine minutes. At the end there was little applause. Lincoln turned to a friend and remarked, “I have failed again.” On the train back to Washington he commented sadly, “That speech was a flat failure, and the people are disappointed.”
blocks.translation: 据说林肯是在前往葛底斯堡的火车上准备演讲的。那天深夜，他独自在酒店房间里，疲惫不堪，又简短地修改了一下演讲。第二天，埃弗雷特先发言。他讲了一小时五十七分钟，其演讲是当时华丽辞藻的完美典范。然后林肯站了起来。一万五千名听众起初几乎没怎么注意他。他只讲了九分钟。结束时掌声寥寥。林肯转身对一位朋友说：“我又失败了。”在返回华盛顿的火车上，他难过地说：“那篇演讲彻底失败了，人们很失望。”

blocks.text: Some newspapers at first criticized the speech. But little by little, as people read the speech, they began to understand better. They began to appreciate its simplicity and its deep meaning. It was a speech which only Abraham Lincoln could have made. Today, every American school child learns Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address by heart. Now everyone thinks of it as one of the greatest orations ever given in American history.
blocks.translation: 起初有些报纸批评这篇演讲。但渐渐地，随着人们阅读这篇演讲，他们开始更好地理解它，开始欣赏它的简洁和深刻含义。这是一篇只有亚伯拉罕·林肯才能作出的演讲。今天，每个美国学童都要背诵林肯的《葛底斯堡演说》。现在大家都认为它是美国历史上最伟大的演说之一。

paragraphs: On November 19, 1863, Abraham Lincoln went to Gettysburg in Pennsylvania to speak at the National Soldiers Cemetery. The Civil War was still going on. There was much criticism of President Lincoln at the time. He was not at all popular. He had been invited to speak at Gettysburg only out of courtesy. The principal speaker was to be Edward Everett, a famous statesman and speaker of the day. Everett was a handsome man and very popular everywhere.

It is said that Lincoln prepared his speech on the train while going to Gettysburg. Late that night, alone in his hotel room and tired out, he again worked briefly on the speech. The next day Everett spoke first. He spoke for an hour and 57 minutes. His speech was a perfect example of the rich oratory of the day. Then Lincoln rose. The crowd of 15,000 people at first paid little attention to him. He spoke for only nine minutes. At the end there was little applause. Lincoln turned to a friend and remarked, “I have failed again.” On the train back to Washington he commented sadly, “That speech was a flat failure, and the people are disappointed.”

Some newspapers at first criticized the speech. But little by little, as people read the speech, they began to understand better. They began to appreciate its simplicity and its deep meaning. It was a speech which only Abraham Lincoln could have made. Today, every American school child learns Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address by heart. Now everyone thinks of it as one of the greatest orations ever given in American history.

blocks.text: I used to go to Starbucks for their coffee, but that’s changed since I discovered their comforting, tasty teas, which are better than coffee any time. Tea is cool even when it’s hot. People drink more tea than any other drink in the world, except for water.
blocks.translation: 我以前去星巴克是为了喝咖啡，但自从发现他们令人舒适、美味的茶之后，情况就变了——这些茶任何时候都比咖啡好。茶是酷的，即使它是热的。除水以外，茶是世界上消费量最大的饮料。

blocks.text: Whether it’s served hot or cold, natural and flavored teas are drinks that have been consumed for centuries. Everywhere you look, you’ll find various kinds of teas—in restaurants, grocery stores, television advertisements, and gift shops.
blocks.translation: 无论冷饮还是热饮，天然茶和调味茶都是人们饮用了数百年的饮料。放眼四周，你都会发现各种各样的茶——在餐馆、杂货店、电视广告和礼品店里。

blocks.text: Why is there all this excitement about tea? What’s its attraction? Well, there are many possibilities for why more and more people are drinking tea. One possibility is that people are coming to notice the benefits of drinking tea, particularly green tea. Studies show that drinking four cups of green tea a day can reduce the risk of developing various types of cancers, as well as heart disease. The key to tea’s effects of cure seems to lie in chemicals found in tea which prevent a process that leads to the growth of cancers. Green tea may also prevent skin cancer. It has also been linked with helping the body to rid itself of harmful materials, and green tea is thought to possibly protect against colds and Parkinson’s (帕金森) disease.
blocks.translation: 为什么人们对茶如此兴奋？它的吸引力在哪里？越来越多的人喝茶，原因有很多可能。一种可能是人们逐渐注意到喝茶的好处，尤其是绿茶。研究表明，每天喝四杯绿茶可以降低患多种癌症以及心脏病的风险。茶的疗效似乎关键在于茶中发现的化学物质，它们能阻止导致癌症生长的过程。绿茶还可能预防皮肤癌。它还被认为有助于身体排出有害物质，并且有人认为绿茶可能有助于预防感冒和帕金森病。

blocks.text: Another explanation for why people are drinking more tea may be due to the comforting process of just making a cup of tea. The time it takes to prepare tea leaves in hot water and enjoy its gentle flavor forces drinkers to slow down and relax a while, making it the perfect way to improve a world where people are so crazy about cappuccino, a hot coffee with milk in it.
blocks.translation: 人们喝更多茶的另一个解释，可能在于泡一杯茶这一令人舒适的过程。把茶叶放入热水、享受其柔和滋味所需的时间，迫使饮者放慢脚步、放松片刻，这使它成为改善这个疯狂迷恋卡布奇诺（一种加奶的热咖啡）的世界的最佳方式。

blocks.text: So, whether you drink tea, eat it in foods, wear it to smell good, or take it in pills, one thing is certain, the use of tea is more than a trend—it is a habit of our past and if studies prove the benefits of its use, it will undoubtedly be an important element of our future.
blocks.translation: 所以，无论你是喝茶、把茶吃进食物、佩戴茶香，还是服用茶片，有一点是确定的：茶的使用不只是一种潮流——它是我们过去的习惯；如果研究证实了它的益处，它无疑将成为我们未来的重要元素。

paragraphs: I used to go to Starbucks for their coffee, but that’s changed since I discovered their comforting, tasty teas, which are better than coffee any time. Tea is cool even when it’s hot. People drink more tea than any other drink in the world, except for water.

Whether it’s served hot or cold, natural and flavored teas are drinks that have been consumed for centuries. Everywhere you look, you’ll find various kinds of teas—in restaurants, grocery stores, television advertisements, and gift shops.

Why is there all this excitement about tea? What’s its attraction? Well, there are many possibilities for why more and more people are drinking tea. One possibility is that people are coming to notice the benefits of drinking tea, particularly green tea. Studies show that drinking four cups of green tea a day can reduce the risk of developing various types of cancers, as well as heart disease. The key to tea’s effects of cure seems to lie in chemicals found in tea which prevent a process that leads to the growth of cancers. Green tea may also prevent skin cancer. It has also been linked with helping the body to rid itself of harmful materials, and green tea is thought to possibly protect against colds and Parkinson’s (帕金森) disease.

Another explanation for why people are drinking more tea may be due to the comforting process of just making a cup of tea. The time it takes to prepare tea leaves in hot water and enjoy its gentle flavor forces drinkers to slow down and relax a while, making it the perfect way to improve a world where people are so crazy about cappuccino, a hot coffee with milk in it.

So, whether you drink tea, eat it in foods, wear it to smell good, or take it in pills, one thing is certain, the use of tea is more than a trend—it is a habit of our past and if studies prove the benefits of its use, it will undoubtedly be an important element of our future.

所以，无论你是喝茶、把茶吃进食物、佩戴茶香，还是服用茶片，有一点是确定的：茶的使用不只是一种潮流——它是我们过去的习惯；如果研究证实了它的益处，它无疑将成为我们未来的重要元素。

articles.title: A study of art history might be a good way to learn more about a culture than is possible
articles.fallbackTitle: A study of art history might be a good way to learn more about a culture than is possible

blocks.text: A study of art history might be a good way to learn more about a culture than is possible to learn in general history classes. Most typical history courses concentrate on politics, economics and war. But art history focuses on much more than this because art reflects not only the political values of a people, but also religious beliefs, emotions and psychology. In addition, information about the daily activities of our ancestors can be provided by art. In short, art expresses the essential qualities of a time and a place, and a study of it clearly offers us a deeper understanding than can be found in most history books.
blocks.translation: 学习艺术史也许是了解一种文化的好方法，比在一般历史课上学到的更多。大多数典型的历史课程集中于政治、经济和战争。但艺术史关注的远不止这些，因为艺术不仅反映一个民族的政治价值观，也反映宗教信仰、情感和心理。此外，艺术还能提供关于我们先人日常活动的信息。总之，艺术表达了一个时代和一个地方的本质特征，研究艺术显然能让我们获得比大多数历史书更深入的理解。

blocks.text: In history books, objective information about the political life of a country is presented; that is, facts about politics are given, but opinions are not expressed. Art, on the other hand, is subjective (主观的): it reflects emotions and opinions. The great Spanish painter Francisco Goya was perhaps the first truly "political" artist. In his well-known painting The Third of May, 1808, he criticized the Spanish government for its abuse (滥用) of power over people.
blocks.translation: 历史书呈现的是关于一个国家政治生活的客观信息；也就是说，给出政治事实，但不表达观点。而艺术是主观的：它反映情感和观点。伟大的西班牙画家弗朗西斯科·戈雅也许是第一位真正“政治性”的艺术家。在他的名画《1808 年 5 月 3 日》中，他批评西班牙政府滥用权力压迫人民。

blocks.text: In the same way, art can reflect a culture's religious beliefs. For hundreds of years in Europe, religious art had been almost the only type of art that existed. Churches and other religious buildings were filled with paintings that described people and stories from the Bible. Although most people couldn't read, they could still understand the Bible stories in the pictures on church walls. By contrast, one of the main characteristics of art in the Middle East was (and still is) its absence of human and animal images. This reflects the Islamic belief that statues are not holy.
blocks.translation: 同样，艺术也能反映一种文化的宗教信仰。在欧洲数百年间，宗教艺术几乎是唯一存在的艺术类型。教堂和其他宗教建筑里满是描绘圣经人物和故事的画作。虽然大多数人不会阅读，他们仍能看懂教堂墙壁图画中的圣经故事。相比之下，中东艺术的主要特征之一过去是（现在仍是）不出现人与动物形象。这反映了伊斯兰教信仰：雕像并不神圣。

articles.fallbackTitle: I once knew a young man, nineteen years of age, who lived with absolute outward (外表的) conf

blocks.text: I once knew a young man, nineteen years of age, who lived with absolute outward (外表的) confidence and self-possession for a number of years before I discovered that he could not read or write. His various methods of trick, which were also skills of self-protection, were so skillful and so desperate (绝望) that neither I nor any of his other adult friends were aware of his entire helplessness in face of written words until we went to dinner one night at a local restaurant — and suddenly discovered that he could not read.
blocks.translation: 我曾认识一个十九岁的年轻人，多年来一直表现得极其自信、沉着，直到后来我发现他既不识字也不会写。他用各种花招掩饰自己，这些花招同时也是自我保护的手段，手法娴熟又带着绝望，以至于我和他其他成年朋友都没有察觉他在文字面前完全无助，直到有一天晚上我们去当地一家餐馆吃饭，才突然发现他不识字。

blocks.text: Even here, it was not the first time we went out to eat, but something like the second or third, that Peter’s desperation shocked me. The first time, he was clever enough to cover the truth. He studied the menu for a moment, then looked up to the waitress and asked her if he could have "just a coke and a hamburger". He told me later that he had done the same thing many times before and that he had learned to act as if he were examining the menu: "Then I ask for a coke and a hamburger... Sometimes they give me a hamburger on a plate with salad and potatoes... Then I ask them for a roll and make my own hamburger."
blocks.translation: 即使在那时，那也不是我们第一次出去吃饭，大概是第二次或第三次，彼得的绝望才让我震惊。第一次他机灵地掩饰了真相：他盯着菜单看了一会儿，然后抬头问女服务员能不能只给他“一杯可乐和一个汉堡”。后来他告诉我，他以前多次这样做，已经学会装出研究菜单的样子：“然后我要一杯可乐和一个汉堡……有时他们给我一个放在盘子里的汉堡，配沙拉和土豆……然后我再要一个小圆面包，自己做一个汉堡。”

blocks.text: As we began to go out more frequently, Peter would ask to go to Howard Johnson’s. I soon discovered the reason for his choice: The photographs, attached in cellophane (玻璃纸) containers to each of the standard items on the menu, could help him not to struggle with the shape of words at all. Howard Johnson’s, whether intentionally or not, had provided the perfect escape for the endangered pride of an adult who was illiterate (文盲).
blocks.translation: 随着我们外出越来越频繁，彼得总要求去霍华德·约翰逊餐厅。我很快发现了他选择那里的原因：菜单上每道标准菜都附有装在玻璃纸套里的照片，这让他完全不必费力辨认单词的形状。不管有意与否，霍华德·约翰逊餐厅为一个文盲成年人岌岌可危的自尊提供了完美的避难所。

articles.title: College is a new and different experience for me
articles.fallbackTitle: College is a new and different experience for me

blocks.text: College is a new and different experience for me. I’m away from home, so I have many things to adjust to, such as being on my own and meeting many different types of people. There are a lot of things that I like about college that I would like to describe for you.
blocks.translation: 大学对我来说是一种全新而不同的经历。我离开家，有很多东西要适应，比如独立生活、认识各种不同类型的人。大学里有很多我喜欢的地方，我想向你描述。

blocks.text: First of all, living at college gives me a sense of responsibility and of being on my own. My parents aren’t around to say, "No, you’re not going out tonight," or "Did you finish your homework?" Everything I do has to be my decision, and that makes me responsible for my own life. During the second week I was at college, I had to go out and look for a bank where I could open an account. And when I got to the bank, I had to decide whether to have a checking or savings account and whether or not to get a credit card. Decisions! Decisions!
blocks.translation: 首先，住在大学里让我有一种责任感和独立感。父母不在身边，不会说“不行，你今晚不许出去”或“作业写完了吗”。我做的一切都必须自己决定，这让我对自己的人生负责。到大学的第二周，我得出去找一家银行开户。到了银行，我还得决定开活期账户还是储蓄账户，要不要办信用卡。决定，决定，全是决定！

blocks.text: Friendly people is another thing I like about college. On the first day I came to Marymount University here in Virginia from New York, I was a bit confused about where I was going. My mother and I drove in. We did not know the building we were supposed to go to, but the guard was very nice. With a smile, he told us what building we were looking for and where we could park our car. My room was on the first floor of New Gerard, and I knew I had to go through some glass doors, but my mother and I didn’t know which ones. Some students saw me and asked, "Are you a new student?" When they found out I was looking for New Gerard, one said, "Oh, just follow us; that’s where we’re going." Even now I feel comfortable in the dorm because there are friendly people around to talk with.
blocks.translation: 友善的人是大学里另一件让我喜欢的事。第一天我从纽约来到弗吉尼亚的玛丽蒙特大学时，有点搞不清该往哪走。我和妈妈开车来的，不知道要去哪栋楼，但保安非常好，笑着告诉我们该找哪栋楼、车停在哪里。我的房间在新杰拉德楼一层，我知道要穿过几扇玻璃门，但我和妈妈不知道是哪几扇。一些学生看到我，问：“你是新生吗？”当他们得知我在找新杰拉德楼时，一个学生说：“哦，跟着我们走吧，我们也去那儿。”直到现在，我在宿舍里仍觉得很自在，因为周围有友善的人可以聊天。

blocks.text: I do like a lot of things about college, but that doesn’t mean I don’t think about things at home. Although I like college, I can still get homesick. New York is a very good place, too! And sometimes I miss it!
blocks.translation: 我确实喜欢大学的许多方面，但这并不意味着我不想家里的事。虽然我喜欢大学，我仍然会想家。纽约也是个很好的地方！有时我会想念它！

questions.evidence: Friendly people is another thing I like about college.

questions.stem: What is New Gerard?
options: It’s a student’s name.
It’s a teacher’s name.
It’s a dorm’s name.
It’s a school’s name.
questions.explanation: 文中说“My room was on the first floor of New Gerard”，New Gerard 是宿舍楼的名字。
questions.evidence: My room was on the first floor of New Gerard

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true?
options: People in Marymount University are friendly.
The writer likes the new experience in the university.
The writer drove to Marymount University with his mother.
The writer is not homesick.
questions.explanation: 最后一段作者明确说“I can still get homesick”，因此“作者不想家”是错误的；A、B、C 都与原文相符。
questions.evidence: Although I like college, I can still get homesick.

translations: 大学对我来说是一种全新而不同的经历。我离开家，有很多东西要适应，比如独立生活、认识各种不同类型的人。大学里有很多我喜欢的地方，我想向你描述。
首先，住在大学里让我有一种责任感和独立感。父母不在身边，不会说“不行，你今晚不许出去”或“作业写完了吗”。我做的一切都必须自己决定，这让我对自己的人生负责。到大学的第二周，我得出去找一家银行开户。到了银行，我还得决定开活期账户还是储蓄账户，要不要办信用卡。决定，决定，全是决定！

友善的人是大学里另一件让我喜欢的事。第一天我从纽约来到弗吉尼亚的玛丽蒙特大学时，有点搞不清该往哪走。我和妈妈开车来的，不知道要去哪栋楼，但保安非常好，笑着告诉我们该找哪栋楼、车停在哪里。我的房间在新杰拉德楼一层，我知道要穿过几扇玻璃门，但我和妈妈不知道是哪几扇。一些学生看到我，问：“你是新生吗？”当他们得知我在找新杰拉德楼时，一个学生说：“哦，跟着我们走吧，我们也去那儿。”直到现在，我在宿舍里仍觉得很自在，因为周围有友善的人可以聊天。
我确实喜欢大学的许多方面，但这并不意味着我不想家里的事。虽然我喜欢大学，我仍然会想家。纽约也是个很好的地方！有时我会想念它！

articles.title: When I was studying English at a training center in Washington D.C
articles.fallbackTitle: When I was studying English at a training center in Washington D.C

blocks.text: When I was studying English at a training center in Washington D.C. in 1998, I shared a house with two young Americans, Jim and Steve. Jim was studying French and Steve was studying Chinese, both at the Foreign Service Institute. We shared many things in common, but we also thought and acted quite differently. Steve was interested in speaking Chinese. He always tried every opportunity to talk with me with his very English-like pronunciation. I was often touched with his diligence. However, I wanted to practice English with him, too. So we often spoke at the same time in the other’s mother tongue. Jim was fresh from college and the youngest of the three. He was going out all the time. The only time we met was at breakfast. There was a small round table in our kitchen, where we sat around to enjoy our food. Steve had Chinese fast food such as dumplings or noodles, and I ate bread and boiled eggs. But Jim often just drank a cup of tea because he had nothing in his fridge. He was too busy dating pretty French girls to do any shopping. I often offered him some of my food. But Steve told me in his poor Chinese that I didn’t need to do that. He said that it was Jim’s own fault and that it served him right. Although he was learning Chinese, he still held his American sense of value.
blocks.translation: 1998 年，我在华盛顿特区的一个培训中心学英语时，和两个美国年轻人吉姆和史蒂夫合住一栋房子。吉姆学法语，史蒂夫学中文，都在外交学院。我们有许多共同点，但想法和行事方式也很不同。史蒂夫对说中文很感兴趣，总是抓住每个机会用他那带着浓重英语腔的发音和我说话。我常被他的勤奋感动。不过，我也想和他练英语，所以我们经常同时用对方的母语交谈。吉姆刚大学毕业，是三人中最年轻的。他总在外面，我们唯一能见面的时候是早餐。厨房里有一张小圆桌，我们围坐着吃东西。史蒂夫吃饺子、面条等中式快餐，我吃面包和煮鸡蛋，而吉姆常常只喝一杯茶，因为冰箱里什么都没有。他忙于和漂亮的法国女孩约会，根本没时间购物。我常分给他一些食物，但史蒂夫用蹩脚的中文告诉我不用这样做。他说那是吉姆自己的错，活该。尽管他在学中文，他仍持有美国人的价值观。

blocks.text: Two years later, I returned to China. The three of us still keep in touch. Jim now works in a travel agency in Paris. He got married to one of the pretty girls. He wrote to tell us that now he can enjoy a delicious breakfast with his beautiful wife every morning in their comfortable living room. Steve wants to work in China. And I’m helping him with this. I have introduced him to the dean of the Overseas Section of our university. He is very interested in Steve. He wants to know if Steve can work here teaching the overseas students Chinese. I have sent the message to Steve. I’m sure he’d be very happy to accept the job. However, I hope he could try harder to improve himself. Otherwise, all the overseas students would speak with his terrible pronunciation!
blocks.translation: 两年后我回到中国，我们三人仍保持联系。吉姆现在在巴黎一家旅行社工作，娶了其中一个漂亮女孩。他写信告诉我们，现在他每天早上都能和美丽的妻子在舒适的客厅里享用美味的早餐。史蒂夫想来中国工作，我正在帮他。我把他介绍给我们大学海外部的主任，主任对史蒂夫很感兴趣，想知道他能否来这里教留学生中文。我已把消息转给史蒂夫，相信他会很乐意接受这份工作。不过，我希望他能更努力地提升自己，否则所有留学生都会学成他那种糟糕的发音！

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true according to the passage?
options: The three of them were all language majors.
Steve and Jim were more alike in character.
The author didn’t enjoy talking with Steve.
Their living condition was rather poor.
questions.explanation: 作者学英语，Jim 学法语，Steve 学中文，三人都在学习语言，可视为语言专业学生；B 与“thought and acted quite differently”相反，C 与作者常和 Steve 交流不符，D 无依据。
questions.evidence: Jim was studying French and Steve was studying Chinese

questions.stem: What is the author’s opinion of Steve?
options: Steve was a very hardworking fellow.
Steve enjoyed cooking Chinese food.
Steve enjoyed shopping more than Jim.
Steve’s Chinese accent was quite pure.
questions.explanation: 作者说 Steve 抓住每个机会说中文，自己常被他的“diligence”（勤奋）感动，因此认为 Steve 很用功；他的中文发音并不纯正，文中还调侃他的口音。

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Jim?
options: Going out with girls cost him a lot of time.
He had a French way of making friends.
He learned French in order to date Paris girls.
He liked doing housework.
questions.explanation: 第一段说 Jim“too busy dating pretty French girls to do any shopping”，即约会占用了大量时间；他并没有为了约会才学法语，也不是爱做家务。

questions.stem: What does the last sentence of the first paragraph imply?
options: Steve didn’t like offering help to others.
American people only eat their own food.
Americans and Chinese differ in their sense of value.
Steve wanted Jim to do his own shopping.
questions.explanation: Steve 认为 Jim 不买东西是“his own fault”，不应由作者帮忙，作者由此感叹 Steve 仍持有美国人的价值观，说明中美价值观存在差异。
questions.evidence: he still held his American sense of value

questions.stem: From the last paragraph, we can learn that ______.
options: Jim is a very good husband
Steve enjoys teaching Chinese
the author works for overseas students
the three friends still keep in touch
questions.explanation: 最后一段开头说“The three of us still keep in touch”，三人仍保持联系；Jim 是否是好丈夫、Steve 是否喜欢教书都无法确定，作者是在大学工作而非专门为留学生工作。
questions.evidence: The three of us still keep in touch.

articles.title: I saved the grain carefully and finally had enough to plant
articles.fallbackTitle: I saved the grain carefully and finally had enough to plant

blocks.text: I saved the grain carefully and finally had enough to plant. I built a wall around my garden to keep the wild goats away.
blocks.translation: 我小心地保存粮食，终于攒够了播种的量。我在园子周围筑起一道墙，防止野山羊进来。

blocks.text: Then when my crop bore its fruit, the birds discovered it. The birds were not afraid of my dog at all. I shot them but as soon as I walked away, they returned. At last, I killed some birds and hung them among the crop, hoping they would serve as the scarecrows, which turned out to be successful. By harvest time, I had nearly two bushels of rice and two and a half bushels of wheat.
blocks.translation: 后来庄稼结果时，鸟群发现了它。鸟一点也不怕我的狗。我开枪打它们，但我一走开它们就回来。最后我打死一些鸟，挂在庄稼中间，希望它们能当稻草人，结果很成功。到收获时，我收了近两蒲式耳稻谷和两蒲式耳半小麦。

blocks.text: With my new grain to store, I found a new problem. The fine grain ran through my baskets. It took me nearly two months to form and dry two ugly pots — one for rice and one for wheat.
blocks.translation: 有了新粮食要储存，我又遇到新问题：细小的谷粒会从篮子里漏出去。我花了近两个月，做成并晾干两个难看的陶罐——一个装稻谷，一个装小麦。

blocks.text: Next I formed a clay oven and made some other tools from hard wood and cloth to bake bread. I made and baked bread in my oven. I spent the third year on the island in farming and baking.
blocks.translation: 接着我做了黏土烤炉，又用硬木和布做了些工具来烤面包。我在自己的烤炉里做面包、烤面包。在岛上的第三年，我用来种地和烤面包。

blocks.text: Soon after that, I began to think of my days sailing in a tidy boat with Xury. I wished to have a boat and explore the island by sea.
blocks.translation: 不久之后，我开始想起和 Xury 一起乘小船航行的日子。我希望有一条船，从海上探索这座岛。

blocks.text: I tried to turn over the ship’s boat that I had seen washed up, but failed. I was still determined to have a boat. So I chose a strong tree and spent weeks cutting it down. Then it took me months to turn it from tree to boat.
blocks.translation: 我试着把冲到岸上的那条大船翻过来，但失败了。我仍决心要有一条船，于是选了一棵粗壮的树，花了几周把它砍倒，又花了几个月把它从一棵树变成一条船。

blocks.text: When it was time to launch, I realized I had made my boat too far from the nearest stream. The boat was far too heavy for me to move. I tried bringing the water to the boat instead of the boat to the water. I soon saw it would take me twenty years of constant labor.
blocks.translation: 到了该下水的时候，我才发现船造得离最近的溪流太远。船太重，我根本搬不动。我试着把水引到船边，而不是把船搬到水边，但很快明白那需要我连续干二十年。

blocks.text: I celebrated my fourth year on the island with two boats, but I was no closer to a sea journey.
blocks.translation: 我在岛上第四年时有了两条船，但离真正的海上航行并没有更近一步。

blocks.text: ——Taken from The Adventures of Robinson Crusoe
blocks.translation: ——选自《鲁滨逊漂流记》

paragraphs: I saved the grain carefully and finally had enough to plant. I built a wall around my garden to keep the wild goats away.

Then when my crop bore its fruit, the birds discovered it. The birds were not afraid of my dog at all. I shot them but as soon as I walked away, they returned. At last, I killed some birds and hung them among the crop, hoping they would serve as the scarecrows, which turned out to be successful. By harvest time, I had nearly two bushels of rice and two and a half bushels of wheat.
With my new grain to store, I found a new problem. The fine grain ran through my baskets. It took me nearly two months to form and dry two ugly pots — one for rice and one for wheat.
Next I formed a clay oven and made some other tools from hard wood and cloth to bake bread. I made and baked bread in my oven. I spent the third year on the island in farming and baking.
Soon after that, I began to think of my days sailing in a tidy boat with Xury. I wished to have a boat and explore the island by sea.

I tried to turn over the ship’s boat that I had seen washed up, but failed. I was still determined to have a boat. So I chose a strong tree and spent weeks cutting it down. Then it took me months to turn it from tree to boat.

When it was time to launch, I realized I had made my boat too far from the nearest stream. The boat was far too heavy for me to move. I tried bringing the water to the boat instead of the boat to the water. I soon saw it would take me twenty years of constant labor.
I celebrated my fourth year on the island with two boats, but I was no closer to a sea journey.
——Taken from The Adventures of Robinson Crusoe

questions.stem: Paragraph 2 mainly tells us ______.
options: how much rice and wheat I harvested
how many tools I made to bake bread
how I protected my crop from the birds
how I kept the wild goats away from my crop
questions.explanation: 第二段写鸟群来吃庄稼，作者先开枪、再挂死鸟当稻草人，最后成功保住收成，核心是“如何从鸟口中保护庄稼”；A 只是结果，B 是下一段的内容。
questions.evidence: I killed some birds and hung them among the crop, hoping they would serve as the scarecrows

questions.stem: The reason why I wanted to have a boat is that I wanted ______.
options: explore the island
bring water to the plants
catch fish
leave the island
questions.explanation: 第五段说作者想起和 Xury 坐船航行的日子，“I wished to have a boat and explore the island by sea”，想有船是为了从海上探索这座岛。
questions.evidence: I wished to have a boat and explore the island by sea.

questions.stem: What does "a new problem" in Paragraph 3 refer to?
options: How to plant grain.
How to make pots.
How to store grain.
How to fix the baskets.
questions.explanation: 第三段说有了新粮食要储存，但细粮从篮子里漏出去，于是花了两个月做陶罐，因此“a new problem”指如何储存粮食。
questions.evidence: With my new grain to store, I found a new problem.

questions.stem: By the last sentence, the writer means ______.
options: I was getting closer and closer to the sea
I was getting farther and farther from the sea
it was possible for me to have a sea journey in my boats
it was still impossible for me to explore the island by sea
questions.explanation: 最后一句说“我”在岛上第四年有了两条船，但离海上航行并没有更近一步，意思是仍然无法乘船探索海岛。
questions.evidence: I was no closer to a sea journey.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the passage?
options: I managed to turn over the ship’s boat.
I spent months bringing the boat to the nearest stream.
I tried to solve the problems with my courage and wisdom.
I spent the third year on the island in farming and baking.
questions.explanation: 作者不断用墙、稻草人、陶罐、造船等办法解决生存问题，体现勇气与智慧；A 与“failed”相反，B 与“twenty years”不符，D 是原文直述而非推断。
questions.evidence: I was still determined to have a boat.

articles.title: It’s not easy to be an astronaut’s son
articles.fallbackTitle: It’s not easy to be an astronaut’s son

blocks.text: It’s not easy to be an astronaut’s son. Everybody expects you to be special or perfect. I often wonder how my father ever had a son like me. I mean, he is so special and so good at everything he does. Even in middle school he was the class monitor and captain of the football team.
blocks.translation: 做宇航员的儿子并不容易。每个人都期待你特别或完美。我常想，父亲怎么会有我这样的儿子。我是说，他那么特别，做什么都那么出色。甚至在中学时，他就是班长和足球队队长。

blocks.text: Well, to be honest, I often dream about being some kind of hero or doing something special, like saving a child from a burning building or discovering a new star. I was daydreaming at school one morning when my teacher said: "There would be a Father’s Day writing competition for the whole school. I hope we have a winner right here in my class."
blocks.translation: 说实话，我常梦想成为某种英雄，或做点特别的事，比如从着火的楼里救出孩子，或发现一颗新星。一天早上我在学校做白日梦，老师却说：“学校要举办父亲节写作比赛，我希望我们班的获奖者就在这里。”

blocks.text: When I got home, I started to think about what to write. My father is an astronaut. No, I wouldn’t start like that. That was the way others saw him. How did I see my father?
blocks.translation: 回到家，我开始想写什么。“我父亲是宇航员。”不，我不能这样开头。那是别人看他的方式。我是怎么看父亲的？

blocks.text: I saw him sitting with me in the dark when I had a terrible dream. I remembered how he hugged me for hours when my dog Spotty was killed by a car. Yes, these were the things I was going to write. To me he wasn’t just a world-famous astronaut. He was my dad.
blocks.translation: 我看到他在我做噩梦时坐在黑暗中陪我；我记得我的狗 Spotty 被车撞死后，他抱着我好几个小时。对，这些才是我要写的。对我来说，他不只是世界闻名的宇航员，他是我的爸爸。

blocks.text: My parents and I went to school on Thursday. There were so many people in the big hall! My dad looked at me, and shrugged(耸肩).
blocks.translation: 星期四，我和父母去了学校。大礼堂里人真多！爸爸看着我，耸了耸肩。

blocks.text: The third prize was announced and it was not me. I was relieved and disappointed at the same time. The second prize was announced. It was me.
blocks.translation: 三等奖宣布了，不是我。我既松了一口气，又有些失望。二等奖宣布了，是我。

blocks.text: I went up to the stage and read what I had written. When I finished, the people stood up and cheered. I saw my father blowing his nose. Tears were running down my mother’s face. Dad cleared his throat and put his hand on my shoulder. "Son, this is the proudest moment of my life."
blocks.translation: 我走上台，朗读我写的内容。读完后，全场起立欢呼。我看到父亲在擤鼻子，泪水顺着母亲的脸颊流下。父亲清了清嗓子，把手放在我肩上：“儿子，这是我一生中最骄傲的时刻。”

blocks.text: It was the proudest moment of my life, too. Maybe I will never be a great hero or win a Nobel Prize, but it was enough just to be my father’s son.
blocks.translation: 这也是我一生中最骄傲的时刻。也许我永远不会成为伟大的英雄，也不会获得诺贝尔奖，但仅仅是做我父亲的儿子，就已经足够了。

paragraphs: It’s not easy to be an astronaut’s son. Everybody expects you to be special or perfect. I often wonder how my father ever had a son like me. I mean, he is so special and so good at everything he does. Even in middle school he was the class monitor and captain of the football team.

Well, to be honest, I often dream about being some kind of hero or doing something special, like saving a child from a burning building or discovering a new star. I was daydreaming at school one morning when my teacher said: "There would be a Father’s Day writing competition for the whole school. I hope we have a winner right here in my class."
When I got home, I started to think about what to write. My father is an astronaut. No, I wouldn’t start like that. That was the way others saw him. How did I see my father?

I saw him sitting with me in the dark when I had a terrible dream. I remembered how he hugged me for hours when my dog Spotty was killed by a car. Yes, these were the things I was going to write. To me he wasn’t just a world-famous astronaut. He was my dad.
My parents and I went to school on Thursday. There were so many people in the big hall! My dad looked at me, and shrugged(耸肩).
The third prize was announced and it was not me. I was relieved and disappointed at the same time. The second prize was announced. It was me.

I went up to the stage and read what I had written. When I finished, the people stood up and cheered. I saw my father blowing his nose. Tears were running down my mother’s face. Dad cleared his throat and put his hand on my shoulder. "Son, this is the proudest moment of my life."
It was the proudest moment of my life, too. Maybe I will never be a great hero or win a Nobel Prize, but it was enough just to be my father’s son.

articles.title: Having graduated from college, I succeeded in finding a job at Toyota
articles.fallbackTitle: Having graduated from college, I succeeded in finding a job at Toyota

blocks.text: Having graduated from college, I succeeded in finding a job at Toyota. My first workday was not as busy as I had expected, but it taught me a lot. In actual fact, it will benefit me for my whole life.
blocks.translation: 大学毕业后，我成功在丰田找到一份工作。第一个工作日没有我想象的那么忙，却教会了我很多。事实上，它让我受益终生。

blocks.text: When I was enrolled in the financial department, I was assigned by the chief to check some data in the account books with the invoices. I was glad at first and thought, "It’s a piece of cake for a graduate majoring in accounting." It didn’t take me long before I finished the job. Expecting to be praised, I went to the chief.
blocks.translation: 我被分配到财务部后，主管让我核对账本与发票之间的一些数据。起初我很高兴，心想：“对一个会计专业毕业生来说，这是小菜一碟。”我没花多久就完成了。我期待着被表扬，便去找主管。

blocks.text: Unexpectedly, he asked me to check all the data again with care, without stopping doing his own work. I felt a little disappointed. Time was passing slowly when I felt hungry. The chief came to me and said, "Put your work aside; it’s time for lunch now." I relaxed, and went to the dining hall.
blocks.translation: 没想到，他头也不抬地继续自己的工作，只让我把所有数据再仔细核对一遍。我有点失望。时间过得很慢，我感到饿了。主管走过来对我说：“把工作放一放，该吃午饭了。”我放松下来，去了食堂。

blocks.text: I went on with my assignment immediately after I came back. I found some mistakes that I hadn’t noticed the first time. At this moment the chief approached me and said, "Are there any errors? Do you think it’s necessary to repeat the whole cycle?" I nodded with embarrassment, and told him that I’d like to do it a third time. The chief was satisfied when I handed the account books to him.
blocks.translation: 回来后我立刻继续任务。我发现了一些第一次没有注意到的错误。这时主管走近我，说：“有错误吗？你觉得有必要把整个流程再来一遍吗？”我尴尬地点点头，告诉他我愿意再做第三遍。当我把账本交给他时，主管满意了。

blocks.text: Now he’s retired, and I have taken over his post. I attribute my success to the experience of my first workday at Toyota. It taught me that everything must be handled with care. There is no trifling matter in the financial department.
blocks.translation: 如今他已退休，我接替了他的职位。我把自己的成功归功于在丰田第一个工作日的经历。它教会我，做任何事都必须认真细致。财务部里没有小事。

Unexpectedly, he asked me to check all the data again with care, without stopping doing his own work. I felt a little disappointed. Time was passing slowly when I felt hungry. The chief came to me and said, "Put your work aside; it’s time for lunch now." I relaxed, and went to the dining hall.

I went on with my assignment immediately after I came back. I found some mistakes that I hadn’t noticed the first time. At this moment the chief approached me and said, "Are there any errors? Do you think it’s necessary to repeat the whole cycle?" I nodded with embarrassment, and told him that I’d like to do it a third time. The chief was satisfied when I handed the account books to him.

Now he’s retired, and I have taken over his post. I attribute my success to the experience of my first workday at Toyota. It taught me that everything must be handled with care. There is no trifling matter in the financial department.

blocks.text: Some people bring out the best in you in a way that you might never have fully realized on your own. My mom was one of those people.
blocks.translation: 有些人能以你自己从未完全意识到的方式，激发出你最好的一面。我母亲就是其中之一。

blocks.text: When I was nine years old, my mom became a single mother. While I was growing up, we lived a very hard life. But she gave me a lot of love. Each night, she spoke the words that would change my life, "Kemmons, you are certain to be a great man and you can do anything in life if you work hard enough to get it."
blocks.translation: 我九岁时，母亲成了单亲妈妈。成长过程中，我们生活非常艰难，但她给了我很多爱。每天晚上，她都会说那句改变我一生的话：“肯蒙斯，你一定会成为了不起的人。只要足够努力，你可以做到任何事。”

blocks.text: At fourteen, I was hit by a car and the doctors said I would never walk again. Every day, my mother spoke to me in her gentle, loving voice, telling me that no matter what those doctors said, I could walk again if I wanted to walk badly enough. She drove that message so deep into my heart that I finally believed her. A year later, I returned to school-walking on my own!
blocks.translation: 十四岁时，我被车撞了，医生说我再也无法走路。每天，母亲都用温柔而充满爱意的声音对我说，不管医生怎么说，只要我足够想走，我就能重新走路。她把这句话深深植入我心里，我终于相信了她。一年后，我重返学校——自己走着去的！

blocks.text: When the Great Depression hit, I left school. Over the years, I experienced various levels of business success. But the real turning point occurred on a vacation I took with my wife and five kids. I was dissatisfied with the second-class hotels available for families and was angry that they charged an extra $2 for each child. I told my wife that I was going to open a motel for families that would never charge extra for children.
blocks.translation: 大萧条来临时，我离开了学校。多年来，我经历了不同层次的商业成功。但真正的转折点发生在一次我和妻子、五个孩子的度假中。我对可供家庭入住的二流酒店很不满意，也对每个孩子额外收 2 美元感到愤怒。我告诉妻子，我要开一家家庭旅馆，永远不向儿童额外收费。

blocks.text: Not surprisingly, my mom was one of my strongest supporters. She worked behind the desk and even designed the room style. As in any business, we experienced a lot of challenges. But with my mother’s words deeply rooted in my soul, I never doubted we would succeed. Fifteen years later, we had the largest hotel system in the World-Holiday Inn. In 1979 my company had 1,759 Inns in more than fifty countries with an income of $1 billion a year.
blocks.translation: 不出所料，母亲是我最坚定的支持者之一。她在前台工作，甚至设计了房间风格。和任何生意一样，我们经历了许多挑战。但母亲的话深植于我灵魂中，我从未怀疑我们会成功。十五年后，我们拥有了世界上最大的酒店系统——假日酒店。1979 年，我的公司在五十多个国家拥有 1,759 家酒店，年收入 10 亿美元。

不出所料，母亲是我最坚定的支持者之一。她在前台工作，甚至设计了房间风格。和任何生意一样，我们经历了许多挑战。但母亲的话深植于我灵魂中，我从未怀疑我们会成功。十五年后，我们拥有了世界上最大的酒店系统——假日酒店。1979 年，我的公司在五十多个国家拥有 1,759 家酒店，年收入 10 亿美元。
你的人生起点也许并不好。但如果你能找到一件值得为之奋斗的事，并相信自己，就没有什么能阻止你。

blocks.text: On Thursday afternoon Mrs. Clarke, dressed for going out, took her handbag with some money and her key in it, pulled the door behind her to lock it and went to the Over 60s Club. She always went there on Thursdays. It was a nice outing for an old woman who lived alone.
blocks.translation: 星期四下午，克拉克太太穿戴好准备出门，拿起装了些钱和钥匙的手提包，拉上门锁好，去了“六十岁以上俱乐部”。她每周四都去那里。对一个独居老人来说，这是一次愉快的出游。

blocks.text: At six o’clock she came home, let herself in and at once smelt cigarette smoke. Cigarette smoke in her house? How? Had someone got in? She checked the back door and the windows. All were locked or fastened, as usual. There was no sign of forced entry.
blocks.translation: 六点时她回到家，开门进去，立刻闻到香烟味。她家里怎么会有香烟味？有人进来了吗？她检查了后门和窗户，都像往常一样锁着或扣着，没有强行闯入的迹象。

blocks.text: Over a cup of tea she was wondering whether someone might have a key that fitted her front door — "a master key" perhaps. So she stayed at home the following Thursday. Nothing happened. Was anyone watching her movements? On the Thursday after that, dressed as usual, she went out at her usual time, but she didn’t go to the club. Instead she took a short cut home again, letting herself in through her garden and the back door. She settled down to wait.
blocks.translation: 她边喝茶边想，会不会有人有一把能开她前门的钥匙——“万能钥匙”？于是下一个星期四她留在家里，什么也没发生。有人在观察她的行踪吗？再下一个星期四，她像往常一样穿戴好，按平时的时间出门，但没有去俱乐部，而是抄近路从花园和后门回了家。她坐下来等待。

blocks.text: It was just after four o’clock when the front door bell rang. Mrs. Clarke was making a cup of tea at the time. The bell rang again, and then she heard her letter-box being pushed open. With the kettle of boiling water in her hand, she moved quietly toward the front door. A long piece of wire appeared through the letter-box, and then a hand. The wire turned and caught around the knob on the door-lock. Mrs. Clarke raised the kettle and poured the water over the hand. There was a shout outside, and the skin seemed to drop off the fingers like a glove. The wire fell to the floor, the hand was pulled back, and Mrs. Clarke heard the sound of running feet.

articles.title: Peter loved to buy used articles
articles.fallbackTitle: Peter loved to buy used articles

blocks.text: Peter loved to buy used articles. Almost a month ago, he bought a popular word game that used little pieces of wood with different letters on them. As he was purchasing it, the salesgirl said, "Uh, look, the game box hasn’t even been opened yet. That might be worth some money."
blocks.translation: 彼得喜欢买二手物品。大约一个月前，他买了一款很流行的拼字游戏，游戏用小块木头制成，上面印着不同字母。购买时，女店员说：“哎，你看，游戏盒还没开封呢。说不定值点钱。”

blocks.text: Peter examined the box, and sure enough, it was completely covered in factory-sealed plastic. He saw a date of 1973 on the back of the box.
blocks.translation: 彼得仔细看了看盒子，果然，它完全被工厂密封塑料包着。他看到盒子背面印着 1973 年的日期。

blocks.text: "You should put that up for auction (拍卖) on the Internet, and see what happens," the salesgirl said.
blocks.translation: “你应该把它放到网上拍卖，看看会怎样。”女店员说。

blocks.text: "Yes, you’re right. People like something rare," Peter agreed, "I can’t imagine there being very many unopened boxes of this game still around 40 years later."
blocks.translation: “对，你说得对。人们喜欢稀有的东西。”彼得赞同道，“我无法想象 40 年后还有多少未开封的这款游戏。”

blocks.text: "Don’t forget to tell me if you sell it," the salesgirl smiled.
blocks.translation: “如果卖出去了，别忘了告诉我。”女店员笑着说。

blocks.text: "No problem," Peter said.
blocks.translation: “没问题。”彼得说。

blocks.text: After he got home, Peter went online to several auction websites looking for his game, but he could not find it. Then he typed in the name of the word game and hit SEARCH. The search result was 543 websites containing information about the changes of the games. Over the years, the game had been produced using letters in different sizes and game boards in different colors. He also found some lists of game fans looking for various versions of the game. Peter emailed some of them, telling them what he had.
blocks.translation: 回家后，彼得上了几个拍卖网站找这款游戏，但没找到。然后他输入游戏名称，按下搜索。搜索结果有 543 个网站，包含这款游戏变迁的信息。多年来，这款游戏使用过不同大小的字母和不同颜色的游戏板。他还找到一些游戏迷的名单，他们在寻找不同版本。彼得给其中一些人发了邮件，告诉他们自己有什么。

blocks.text: Two weeks later, Peter went back to the shop.
blocks.translation: 两周后，彼得回到那家店。

blocks.text: "Hello! Do you still remember the unopened word game?"
blocks.translation: “你好！你还记得那盒未开封的拼字游戏吗？”

blocks.text: The salesgirl looked at him for a second, then recognized him and said, "Oh, hi!"
blocks.translation: 女店员看了他一秒，认出他后说：“哦，你好！”

blocks.text: "I’ve got something for you," Peter said, "I sold the game and made $1,000. Thank you for your suggestion," He handed her three $100 bills.
blocks.translation: “我有东西给你，”彼得说，“我把游戏卖了，赚了 1000 美元。谢谢你的建议。”他递给她三张 100 美元钞票。

blocks.text: "Wow!" the salesgirl cried out. "Thank you! I never expected it."
blocks.translation: “哇！”女店员叫起来，“谢谢你！我完全没想到。”

paragraphs: Peter loved to buy used articles. Almost a month ago, he bought a popular word game that used little pieces of wood with different letters on them. As he was purchasing it, the salesgirl said, "Uh, look, the game box hasn’t even been opened yet. That might be worth some money."
Peter examined the box, and sure enough, it was completely covered in factory-sealed plastic. He saw a date of 1973 on the back of the box.
"You should put that up for auction (拍卖) on the Internet, and see what happens," the salesgirl said.
"Yes, you’re right. People like something rare," Peter agreed, "I can’t imagine there being very many unopened boxes of this game still around 40 years later."
"Don’t forget to tell me if you sell it," the salesgirl smiled.
"No problem," Peter said.

The search result was 543 websites containing information about the changes of the games. Over the years, the game had been produced using letters in different sizes and game boards in different colors. He also found some lists of game fans looking for various versions of the game. Peter emailed some of them, telling them what he had.
Two weeks later, Peter went back to the shop.
"Hello! Do you still remember the unopened word game?"
The salesgirl looked at him for a second, then recognized him and said, "Oh, hi!"
"I’ve got something for you," Peter said, "I sold the game and made $1,000. Thank you for your suggestion," He handed her three $100 bills.
"Wow!" the salesgirl cried out. "Thank you! I never expected it."

articles.title: I am the owner of a small clothing store
articles.fallbackTitle: I am the owner of a small clothing store

blocks.text: I am the owner of a small clothing store. Three months ago I decided to move my store to Glendale, another area of town, because business was not very good. Now I rent a store in an old building. The new location in Glendale is excellent, and my sales have improved a lot. (The utilities are also cheaper!) There is a high school nearby, and many of the students come to my store to buy their clothes. This location has other advantages, too. It is closer to my home, and there is a food store on the next block, so it is convenient for me to go shopping after work.
blocks.translation: 我是一家小服装店的店主。三个月前，因为生意不太好，我决定把店搬到城里的另一个区域 Glendale。现在我租了一栋老建筑里的店面。Glendale 的新位置很好，我的销售额提高了很多。（水电费也更便宜！）附近有一所高中，很多学生来我店里买衣服。这个位置还有其他优势：它离我家更近，而且下一个街区有一家食品店，所以我下班后购物很方便。

blocks.text: The size of my new store is better, too. It is much bigger, and there is a lot of storage space. But the building was not in very good condition, and I had to make many improvements. The paint was old and dirty, and I had to pick a new color and paint all of the walls. I hired a man to build new wooden dressing rooms. I also made new curtains for the rooms and the window. I am completely satisfied with the store now. Unfortunately, I learned last week that the owner wants to sell the building — after all my hard work! How did I learn this? I came to work on Friday and saw a "For Sale" sign in front of my store.
blocks.translation: 新店的面积也更好。它大得多，有很多储物空间。但这栋建筑状况不太好，我不得不做很多改善。油漆又旧又脏，我只好重新选颜色，把所有的墙都刷了一遍。我雇人搭了新的木制试衣间，还为试衣间和窗户做了新窗帘。现在我对这家店非常满意。不幸的是，上周我得知房东想卖掉这栋楼——在我辛苦付出之后！我是怎么知道的？星期五我来上班，看到店门前立着一块“出售”的牌子。
