blocks.text: Alan Chang was a handsome young man with good manners. One morning he was walking along a street on his way to an appointment. He did not want to be early or late. He had forgotten to put on his watch so he went up to a man who was waiting for a taxi.
blocks.translation: 艾伦·张是个相貌英俊、举止得体的年轻人。一天早晨，他走在街上，要去赴一个约。他不想早到，也不想迟到。他忘了戴手表，于是走向一个正在等出租车的人。

blocks.text: “Excuse me, sir,” he said, very politely, “but could you tell me the time?”
blocks.translation: “打扰一下，先生，”他非常有礼貌地说，“您能告诉我现在几点吗？”

blocks.text: The man, who was very well-dressed and looked quite rich, said nothing. He did not even look at Alan. Alan spoke to him again. "Excuse me, sir," he said, "but could you please tell me what time it is?"
blocks.translation: 那人衣着考究，看上去相当富有，却什么也没说，甚至没看艾伦一眼。艾伦又说了一遍：“打扰一下，先生，”他说，“请问现在几点了？”

blocks.text: This time the man looked at him, but he did not speak and looked quickly away. Alan thought to himself: well, he can hear me; he must be just rude. So Alan asked again, "Why wouldn't you tell me the time, sir?"
blocks.translation: 这次那人看了他一眼，但没有说话，很快又把目光移开了。艾伦心想：好吧，他听得见我说话，他只是没礼貌。于是艾伦又问：“先生，您为什么不愿意告诉我时间呢？”

blocks.text: The man turned towards him and said, "Put yourself in my shoes. I am standing here waiting for a taxi. You come up to me and ask me for the time. If I tell it to you, you will thank me. I will say 'That's all right.' You may then say 'It's a beautiful day,' to which I may reply 'Yes, I like these sunny winter days.' Before we know what is happening we have a friendly conversation. You are a pleasant, polite young man, so when my taxi comes, I offer you a ride. You accept. We talk. I like you. You like me. I invite you to my home. You meet my daughter. She is a very pretty girl. You are a good-looking man. You like each other. Soon you fall in love. You want to marry. Now do you understand my problem?"
blocks.translation: 那人转过身来对他说：“你设身处地为我想想。我站在这儿等出租车。你走过来问我时间。如果我告诉了你，你会谢我。我会说‘没关系’。你可能接着说‘今天天气真好’，我可能回答‘是啊，我喜欢这些晴朗的冬日’。不知不觉我们就聊得很投机。你是个讨人喜欢、有礼貌的年轻人，所以我的出租车来了，我顺路捎上你。你接受了。我们聊天。我喜欢你。你喜欢我。我邀请你到我家。你见到我女儿。她是个很漂亮的姑娘。你是个英俊的小伙子。你们彼此喜欢。很快你们坠入爱河。你们想结婚。现在你明白我的问题了吗？”

blocks.text: Alan shook his head. "No, sir, I'm sorry, I don't. Everything you have said seems very natural to me."
blocks.translation: 艾伦摇了摇头。“不，先生，抱歉，我不明白。您说的这一切在我看来都很自然。”

blocks.text: "Exactly," the man said, "and I do not want my daughter to marry a man who is too poor to buy a watch. Good morning to you." And with these words he hurried away.
blocks.translation: “正是如此，”那人说，“而我不希望我女儿嫁给一个穷得买不起手表的男人。祝你早安。”说完这些话，他就匆匆走了。

paragraphs: Alan Chang was a handsome young man with good manners. One morning he was walking along a street on his way to an appointment. He did not want to be early or late. He had forgotten to put on his watch so he went up to a man who was waiting for a taxi.
“Excuse me, sir,” he said, very politely, “but could you tell me the time?”

The man, who was very well-dressed and looked quite rich, said nothing. He did not even look at Alan. Alan spoke to him again. "Excuse me, sir," he said, "but could you please tell me what time it is?"

This time the man looked at him, but he did not speak and looked quickly away. Alan thought to himself: well, he can hear me; he must be just rude. So Alan asked again, "Why wouldn't you tell me the time, sir?"

The man turned towards him and said, "Put yourself in my shoes. I am standing here waiting for a taxi. You come up to me and ask me for the time. If I tell it to you, you will thank me. I will say 'That's all right.' You may then say 'It's a beautiful day,' to which I may reply 'Yes, I like these sunny winter days.' Before we know what is happening we have a friendly conversation. You are a pleasant, polite young man, so when my taxi comes, I offer you a ride. You accept. We talk. I like you. You like me. I invite you to my home. You meet my daughter. She is a very pretty girl. You are a good-looking man. You like each other. Soon you fall in love. You want to marry. Now do you understand my problem?"
Alan shook his head. "No, sir, I'm sorry, I don't. Everything you have said seems very natural to me."
"Exactly," the man said, "and I do not want my daughter to marry a man who is too poor to buy a watch. Good morning to you." And with these words he hurried away.

blocks.text: I was only eight years old when the Second World War ended, but I can still remember something about the celebrations in the small town where I lived on the day when the war in Europe ended. We had not suffered much from the war there. But both at home and at school I had become accustomed to the phrases “before the war” and “when the war is over”. “Before the war”, apparently, things had been better, though I was too young to understand why, except that there had been no bombs then, and people had eaten things like ice-cream and bananas, which I had only heard of. When the war was over we would go back to London, but this meant little to me. I did not remember what London was like.
blocks.translation: 第二次世界大战结束时我只有八岁，但我仍记得欧洲战事结束那天，我居住的小镇上庆祝活动的一些情景。我们在那里没有受太多战争之苦。但在家里和学校，我都已经习惯了“战前”和“战争结束后”这些说法。“战前”显然一切更好，虽然我太小不明白为什么，只知道那时没有炸弹，人们吃过冰淇淋和香蕉之类的东西，而我只是听说过。战争结束后我们会回伦敦，但这对我意义不大。我不记得伦敦是什么样子。

blocks.text: What I remember now about VE (Victory in Europe) Day was the May evening. After dinner I said I wanted to see the bonfire (大火堆), so when it got dark my father took me to the end of the street. The bonfire was very high, and somehow people had collected some old clothes to dress the unmistakable figure (人形) with the moustache (胡子) they had put on top of it. Just as we arrived, they set light to it. The flames rose and soon swallowed the “guy”. Everyone was cheering and shouting, and an old woman came out of her house with two chairs and threw them on the fire to keep it going.
blocks.translation: 我现在记得的欧洲胜利日，是那个五月的傍晚。晚饭后我说想去看篝火，于是天黑后父亲带我到了街尾。篝火堆得很高，不知怎么人们还收集了一些旧衣服，给放在顶上那个留着胡子、一眼就能认出的人形穿上。我们刚到，他们就把火点着了。火焰升起，很快吞没了那个“家伙”。大家欢呼叫喊，一位老妇人从家里出来，搬了两把椅子扔进火里，让火继续烧。

我现在记得的欧洲胜利日，是那个五月的傍晚。晚饭后我说想去看篝火，于是天黑后父亲带我到了街尾。篝火堆得很高，不知怎么人们还收集了一些旧衣服，给放在顶上那个留着胡子、一眼就能认出的人形穿上。我们刚到，他们就把火点着了。火焰升起，很快吞没了那个“家伙”。大家欢呼叫喊，一位老妇人从家里出来，搬了两把椅子扔进火里，让火继续烧。
我站在父亲身旁，直到火开始变小，不知道该说什么。他也什么都没说。他参加过第一次世界大战，也许正在回忆那场战争的结束。最后他说：“好了，儿子，就这样了。希望这一次真的是最后一次。”

articles.title: Late last year, I needed to transport some furniture from our house in Sussex to my son’s
articles.fallbackTitle: Late last year, I needed to transport some furniture from our house in Sussex to my son’s

blocks.text: Late last year, I needed to transport some furniture from our house in Sussex to my son’s flat in central London. I should have paid a man to do it for me, but foolishly confident in my driving ability, I decided to hire a van and drive it myself. It was a Ford Transit 280, long and wide; you couldn’t see out of the back. You never really knew how close you were to anything else on the road.
blocks.translation: 去年年底，我需要把一些家具从我们位于萨塞克斯的家运到儿子在伦敦市中心的公寓。我本该花钱请人搬运，却愚蠢地对自己的驾驶技术过于自信，决定租一辆厢式货车自己开。那是一辆福特全顺 280，又长又宽，从后面根本看不见外面。你永远不知道自己和路上其他东西到底有多近。

blocks.text: Reversing in my home yard, I crashed into a small shed, causing permanent damage. At least I owned the shed.
blocks.translation: 在自家院子里倒车时，我撞上一间小棚屋，造成了永久性损坏。至少那棚屋是我自己的。

blocks.text: I loaded up the furniture and set out. By now it was rush hour. My nerves broke down, as I steered the huge van through ever-shifting lanes, across oncoming vehicles, between distances of buses, at last to Charlotte Street.
blocks.translation: 我装好家具出发。此时已是高峰时段。当我在不断变换的车道间、迎着来车、在公交车的缝隙中驾驶这辆巨大的货车，最后到达夏洛特街时，我的神经崩溃了。

blocks.text: Here, I found an available parking space. As I reversed into it, I noticed three people at a pavement café waving to me. I got out, trembling violently, like one who has just endured a stormy Atlantic crossing. “You’ve shifted the car parked behind you three feet,” they said, and it belonged to a disabled person. I examined the car. There were white scratches along its front bumper. It bore a disabled sign. So, now I was a bad driver and a bad man. Under the stern gaze of the three, I left an apologetic note on the damaged car’s windscreen, giving my phone number.
blocks.translation: 在这里，我找到一个空车位。倒车进去时，我注意到路边咖啡座有三个人朝我挥手。我下了车，浑身剧烈发抖，就像一个刚经历过大西洋风暴的人。“你把停在你后面的车撞得挪了三英尺，”他们说，那是残疾人的车。我检查了那辆车。前保险杠上有白色划痕。车上挂着残疾人标志。所以，我现在既是个糟糕的司机，又是个坏人。在那三人严厉的注视下，我在受损车辆的挡风玻璃上留了一张道歉便条，写上了我的电话号码。

blocks.text: I unloaded the furniture, dripping with sweat. Wanting only to escape the monster, I drove the van back to its base on the Edgware Road. On arrival, the hire man told me I must fill it up with petrol before returning it. “Just charge me,” I cried, still shaking with fear. He gazed at me with understanding. No doubt he’d witnessed others in this state before. “How about I drive you to a petrol station, you fill up, and I drive her back?” he asked.
blocks.translation: 我卸下家具，汗流浃背。我只想逃离这个怪物，于是把货车开回埃奇韦尔路的租车点。到达后，租车人告诉我，还车前必须加满油。“直接扣我钱吧，”我喊道，仍然吓得发抖。他理解地看着我。毫无疑问，他以前见过别人这副样子。“我开车送你去加油站，你加满油，我再把车开回来，怎么样？”他问。

blocks.text: He danced the great van through the traffic so casually that it would have shamed me if I had not been so grateful.
blocks.translation: 他漫不经心地开着这辆大货车穿过车流，如果我当时不是那么感激，这会让自愧不如。

paragraphs: Late last year, I needed to transport some furniture from our house in Sussex to my son’s flat in central London. I should have paid a man to do it for me, but foolishly confident in my driving ability, I decided to hire a van and drive it myself. It was a Ford Transit 280, long and wide; you couldn’t see out of the back. You never really knew how close you were to anything else on the road.
Reversing in my home yard, I crashed into a small shed, causing permanent damage. At least I owned the shed.

I loaded up the furniture and set out. By now it was rush hour. My nerves broke down, as I steered the huge van through ever-shifting lanes, across oncoming vehicles, between distances of buses, at last to Charlotte Street.

Here, I found an available parking space. As I reversed into it, I noticed three people at a pavement café waving to me. I got out, trembling violently, like one who has just endured a stormy Atlantic crossing. “You’ve shifted the car parked behind you three feet,” they said, and it belonged to a disabled person. I examined the car. There were white scratches along its front bumper. It bore a disabled sign. So, now I was a bad driver and a bad man. Under the stern gaze of the three, I left an apologetic note on the damaged car’s windscreen, giving my phone number.

I unloaded the furniture, dripping with sweat. Wanting only to escape the monster, I drove the van back to its base on the Edgware Road. On arrival, the hire man told me I must fill it up with petrol before returning it. “Just charge me,” I cried, still shaking with fear. He gazed at me with understanding. No doubt he’d witnessed others in this state before. “How about I drive you to a petrol station, you fill up, and I drive her back?” he asked.
He danced the great van through the traffic so casually that it would have shamed me if I had not been so grateful.

articles.title: The White House is the most visited residence in the world
articles.fallbackTitle: The White House is the most visited residence in the world

blocks.text: The White House is the most visited residence in the world. Tours may be scheduled through our Washington DC office. Due to security and scheduling procedures, there are a few things you should know before requesting a tour:
blocks.translation: 白宫是世界上参观人数最多的官邸。参观可以通过我们的华盛顿特区办公室预约。由于安全和日程安排程序，在申请参观之前，有几件事你需要了解：

blocks.text: Only groups of 10 or more may request a tour.
blocks.translation: 只有 10 人及以上的团体才能申请参观。

blocks.text: Requests must be submitted with a minimum of one month's advance notice from the date of the tour. Notice of whether your application is accepted will be given 10 days prior to the date requested. All tours, even after they have been confirmed, are subject to cancellation due to security interests.
blocks.translation: 申请必须在参观日期前至少一个月提交。申请是否被接受，会在参观日期前 10 天通知。所有参观即使已经确认，也可能因安全原因被取消。

blocks.text: Tours are only conducted Tuesday through Saturday from 7:30 am to 11:30 am.
blocks.translation: 参观只在周二至周六上午 7:30 至 11:30 进行。

blocks.text: To process your request for a tour, please contact our Washington office at (202) 224-5521 and provide the following information:
blocks.translation: 为处理你的参观申请，请联系我们的华盛顿办公室 (202) 224-5521，并提供以下信息：

blocks.text: Date(s) requesting.
blocks.translation: 申请参观的日期。

blocks.text: Security information for each person in your party, including: name as it appears on ID (ID required for ages 14 and up), date of birth, social security number, country of origin, and citizenship.
blocks.translation: 每位同行人员的安全信息，包括：身份证上的姓名（14 岁及以上需提供身份证）、出生日期、社会安全号码、原籍国和公民身份。

blocks.text: A home address and daytime and evening phone numbers for the designated (指派的) leader of the group.
blocks.translation: 指定团体负责人的家庭住址以及日间和晚间电话号码。

blocks.text: A contact number while in DC for the designated leader of the group.
blocks.translation: 指定团体负责人在华盛顿特区期间的联系电话。

blocks.text: After your request is confirmed or denied, our office will contact you with further instructions.
blocks.translation: 你的申请被确认或拒绝后，我们的办公室会联系你并给出进一步指示。

blocks.text: These terms and conditions should be read before you sign your contract.
blocks.translation: 签署合同前，请先阅读这些条款和条件。

blocks.text: Salary: Your starting salary is: $15,000. This is reviewed annually.
blocks.translation: 工资：起薪为 15,000 美元，每年审核一次。

blocks.text: Hours: Work are eight hours a day, Monday through Friday. You will start work on Feb. 21, 2008. On the first morning, report to your line manager John Knight.
blocks.translation: 工时：每天工作八小时，周一至周五。你将于 2008 年 2 月 21 日开始工作。第一天早上，向你的直线经理约翰·奈特报到。

blocks.text: Health and safety: Please read the safety regulations attached. If you have any questions, contact the health and safety officer, whose name is at the top of the regulation sheet. If you have health problems, please inform the Senior Nurse, Chris Thomas. If you cannot work because of illness, please telephone the factory.
blocks.translation: 健康与安全：请阅读随附的安全规定。如有疑问，联系安全规定表顶部的健康与安全官。如有健康问题，请通知高级护士克里斯·托马斯。如因病无法上班，请致电工厂。

blocks.text: Annual leave: During your first year of employment you are allowed twenty days' leave. This should be arranged with your line manager.
blocks.translation: 年假：入职第一年，你享有二十天假期，需与直线经理安排。

blocks.text: Overtime (加班): If you work more than forty hours a week, you will be paid at the current overtime rate. Your line manager will keep a record of the overtime you work. If you work on public holidays, you will be paid at the current rates. If you prefer, time can be taken instead of extra pay for public holidays and overtime.
blocks.translation: 加班：如果每周工作超过四十小时，将按当前加班费率支付。直线经理会记录你的加班时间。如果在公共假日工作，将按当前费率支付。如果你愿意，也可以用调休代替公共假日和加班的额外报酬。

blocks.text: Clothing: The Supplies Department provides overalls (工作服). Inform Supplies of your size two days before you need them. You can also order any other equipment you need for your job from Supplies.
blocks.translation: 服装：供应部提供工作服。需要在两天前把你的尺码告诉供应部。你也可以从供应部订购工作中需要的其他设备。

articles.heading: You Can Make a Windsock (风向袋)
articles.title: You Can Make a Windsock (风向袋)
articles.fallbackTitle: Have you ever seen a windsock blowing in the wind

blocks.text: Have you ever seen a windsock blowing in the wind? Well, you can make one of your own! This is a fun project that you can do with things you may have. You just need to follow a few easy steps.
blocks.translation: 你见过随风飘动的风向袋吗？其实，你也可以自己做一个！这是一个有趣的动手项目，用你可能已有的材料就能完成。你只需跟着几个简单的步骤做。

blocks.text: You will need:
blocks.translation: 你需要准备：

blocks.text: one piece of heavy colored paper
blocks.translation: 一张厚彩纸

blocks.text: five ribbons
blocks.translation: 五条丝带

blocks.text: strong tape
blocks.translation: 强力胶带

blocks.text: a string
blocks.translation: 一根细绳

blocks.text: a pencil
blocks.translation: 一支铅笔

blocks.text: What to do:
blocks.translation: 制作步骤：

blocks.text: Step 1: Draw pictures on the paper. You can write your name on it. Do anything that will make it special to you.
blocks.translation: 第 1 步：在纸上画画。你可以写上自己的名字，做任何能让它对你来说与众不同的装饰。

blocks.text: Step 2: Make the paper into the shape of a tube. Hold one of the shorter edges over the other. Then make them together with the tape at each end and in the middle.
blocks.translation: 第 2 步：把纸卷成筒状。将一条短边叠在另一条短边上，然后用胶带在两端和中间把它们粘在一起。

blocks.text: Step 3: Use a pencil to make a hole into both sides of the tube. The holes should be only on one end of the tube. Pull the string through both holes. Then tie the ends of the string together.
blocks.translation: 第 3 步：用铅笔在纸筒的两侧各扎一个孔。孔只应开在纸筒的一端。把细绳从两个孔中穿过，然后把绳子的两端系在一起。

blocks.text: Step 4: Now make five holes around the top of the other end of the tube. Put a ribbon through each of the holes. Tie a knot in the ends. Make sure the knots are bigger than the holes.
blocks.translation: 第 4 步：现在在纸筒另一端的顶部周围扎五个孔。把每条丝带穿过一个孔，在末端打结。注意结要比孔大。

blocks.text: Now your windsock is ready to use. But how does it work? The shape of the tube plays an important part. Wind blows through the tube and makes it fly and dance around. Hold the windsock up in the air by its string and run around. It will fly behind you. You can also hang it outside and watch it dance around on its own!
blocks.translation: 现在你的风向袋就做好了，可以用了。那它是怎么工作的呢？纸筒的形状起着重要作用。风穿过纸筒，使它飞舞旋转。提着绳子把风向袋举到空中跑动，它就会跟在你身后飞。你也可以把它挂在户外，看它自己随风舞动！

paragraphs: Have you ever seen a windsock blowing in the wind? Well, you can make one of your own! This is a fun project that you can do with things you may have. You just need to follow a few easy steps.
You will need:
What to do:
Step 1: Draw pictures on the paper. You can write your name on it. Do anything that will make it special to you.
Step 2: Make the paper into the shape of a tube. Hold one of the shorter edges over the other. Then make them together with the tape at each end and in the middle.
Step 3: Use a pencil to make a hole into both sides of the tube. The holes should be only on one end of the tube. Pull the string through both holes. Then tie the ends of the string together.
Step 4: Now make five holes around the top of the other end of the tube. Put a ribbon through each of the holes. Tie a knot in the ends. Make sure the knots are bigger than the holes.

Now your windsock is ready to use. But how does it work? The shape of the tube plays an important part. Wind blows through the tube and makes it fly and dance around. Hold the windsock up in the air by its string and run around. It will fly behind you. You can also hang it outside and watch it dance around on its own!

articles.title: When you are cooking with a pressure cooker, you should learn a few common sense rules:
articles.fallbackTitle: When you are cooking with a pressure cooker, you should learn a few common sense rules:

blocks.text: When you are cooking with a pressure cooker, you should learn a few common sense rules:
blocks.translation: 用高压锅做饭时，你应该了解几条常识性规则：

blocks.text: (1) Never leave the cooker unwatched when it is in use.
blocks.translation: （1）使用高压锅时，绝不要无人看管。

blocks.text: (2) Add sufficient liquid but never past the recommended fill point. Overfilling the cooker may block the vent (排气) pipe and cause the cooker to explode.
blocks.translation: （2）加入足够的液体，但绝不能超过建议的最高水位。装得过满可能堵塞排气管，导致高压锅爆炸。

blocks.text: (3) Set the cooking time. Too much time may overcook the food and too little time will lead to undercooked food.
blocks.translation: （3）设定烹饪时间。时间太长会把食物煮过头，时间太短则会导致食物没熟透。

blocks.text: (4) If you are new to pressure cooking, follow the cooking instructions carefully. Heat and time can either result in a great meal or a ruined one.
blocks.translation: （4）如果你是高压锅烹饪的新手，请仔细按照烹饪说明操作。火候和时间既可能成就一顿美餐，也可能毁掉一锅饭。

blocks.text: (5) Never try to force a pressure cooker cover open. Allow the cooker to cool or run it under cool water before trying to open the cover.
blocks.translation: （5）绝不要强行打开高压锅盖。应先让锅冷却，或把锅放到冷水下冲，然后再尝试打开锅盖。

blocks.text: (6) Clean the cooker thoroughly after each use. Mild detergent (洗涤剂) and hot water work the best. Do not use stove ash or sand for they may damage the cooker. The gasket (垫圈) is best cleaned in warm soapy water and then dried. Store the gasket in the bottom of the pot.
blocks.translation: （6）每次使用后都要彻底清洗高压锅。温和的洗涤剂和热水效果最好。不要使用炉灰或沙子，因为它们可能损坏锅体。垫圈最好在温肥皂水中清洗，然后擦干。把垫圈存放在锅底。

paragraphs: When you are cooking with a pressure cooker, you should learn a few common sense rules:
(1) Never leave the cooker unwatched when it is in use.
(2) Add sufficient liquid but never past the recommended fill point. Overfilling the cooker may block the vent (排气) pipe and cause the cooker to explode.
(3) Set the cooking time. Too much time may overcook the food and too little time will lead to undercooked food.
(4) If you are new to pressure cooking, follow the cooking instructions carefully. Heat and time can either result in a great meal or a ruined one.
(5) Never try to force a pressure cooker cover open. Allow the cooker to cool or run it under cool water before trying to open the cover.

(6) Clean the cooker thoroughly after each use. Mild detergent (洗涤剂) and hot water work the best. Do not use stove ash or sand for they may damage the cooker. The gasket (垫圈) is best cleaned in warm soapy water and then dried. Store the gasket in the bottom of the pot.

questions.stem: According to the first rule, the user should ______.
options: keep the cooker under close watch
always keep the cooker half full
never leave the cooker empty
never turn off the stove
questions.explanation: 第一条规则是“Never leave the cooker unwatched when it is in use”，即使用时绝不能无人看管，也就是要密切留意高压锅。
questions.evidence: Never leave the cooker unwatched when it is in use.

questions.stem: According to the instructions, a pressure cooker cover should be opened ______.
options: as soon as the stove is turned off
while the cooker is still cooking
with force when the cooker is hot
after the cooker is cooled down
questions.explanation: 第五条说不要强行打开锅盖，应让锅冷却或用水冲凉后再开，因此正确做法是等锅冷却后开盖。
questions.evidence: Allow the cooker to cool or run it under cool water before trying to open the cover.

questions.stem: According to the instructions, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The gasket should be cleaned thoroughly with cold water.
Mild detergent and hot water can best clean the cooker.
Soapy water will often damage the cooker.
Sand can be used to clean the cooker.
questions.explanation: 第六条明确说“Mild detergent and hot water work the best”，即温和洗涤剂加热水清洁效果最好；A、C、D 都与原文相反。
questions.evidence: Mild detergent (洗涤剂) and hot water work the best.

questions.stem: Which of the following operations may be dangerous?
options: Cleaning the cooker with detergent.
Overfilling the cooker with food and water.
Cooling the cooker with cold water.
Setting the cooking time too short.
questions.explanation: 第二条警告说装得太满会堵住排气管并可能导致高压锅爆炸，因此过度装填食物和水是最危险的操作。
questions.evidence: Overfilling the cooker may block the vent (排气) pipe and cause the cooker to explode.

questions.stem: The purpose of this piece of writing is to ______.
options: describe
persuade
instruct
narrate
questions.explanation: 文章用六条规则告诉读者使用高压锅时该做什么、不该做什么，属于说明操作方法的指导性文字，因此写作目的是 instruct（指导）。

（3）设定烹饪时间。时间太长会把食物煮过头，时间太短则会导致食物没熟透。
（4）如果你是高压锅烹饪的新手，请仔细按照烹饪说明操作。火候和时间既可能成就一顿美餐，也可能毁掉一锅饭。

blocks.text: Welcome to Green Village Community! Here is some information for the newcomers about the sports and fitness facilities in this area.
blocks.translation: 欢迎来到绿村社区！这里有一些关于本地区体育健身设施的信息，供新住户参考。

blocks.text: Power Station Gym
blocks.translation: 动力站健身房

blocks.text: This gym is well known in the area. Here you can find newly-built swimming pool and the latest fitness equipment. It has a team of skilled trainers that can provide personal training. Please note that the swimming pool is closed for cleaning every Sunday and it is not open to the public.
blocks.translation: 这家健身房在本地区很有名。这里有新建的游泳池和最先进的健身器材，还有一支技术娴熟的教练团队，可以提供私人训练。请注意，游泳池每周日关闭清洗，不对外开放。

blocks.text: Zest-booster Leisure Center
blocks.translation: 活力休闲中心

blocks.text: This is the largest leisure center in the area and it is open 24 hours a day. It is a perfect choice for people who need a flexible workout schedule. blocks.translation: 这是本地区最大的休闲中心，全天 24 小时开放，是需要灵活锻炼时间的人的完美选择。它有一条 400 米跑道，会员可免费使用。它为 VIP 会员提供特别设计的健身计划。它每周开放六天，周一关闭。

blocks.text: Wonder Ladies Club
blocks.translation: 魅力女士俱乐部

blocks.text: This club is for female members only. It has a modern gym with the newest equipment. It offers one-to-one training and programs that best meet females’ needs. blocks.translation: 这个俱乐部只面向女性会员。它有一个配备最新器材的现代化健身房，提供一对一的训练和最符合女性需求的项目。它还组织俱乐部活动，如健康讲座和会员聚会，你可以在聚会上一边喝咖啡、吃点心，一边认识其他会员。

blocks.translation: 乔希跑步俱乐部
